Hint.hp: Piercing a step higher, at (0.5); under 15mm (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.baton: Crushing at (0.25) with double knockback, at a fifth of the range; 15mm and up (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.monochain: Half damage and range, +1 to hit; cutting at (10) against a neck, face, skull, limb or extremity, or anywhere on SM -2 or less (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.shotshell: A quarter of the damage, pi++ or pi+ down to pi, half range, nine projectiles, Rcl 1 (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.burrow: At (0.5); a hit that injures burrows for 1 HP a turn, for seconds equal to the calibre in mm (Ultra-Tech p. 155).
Hint.he: A grenade's blast, or the round at (0.5) with a follow-up blast; +1 per die from TL10 (Ultra-Tech p. 153).
Hint.hec: As HE without fragments, the blast linked; +1 per die from TL10 (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.shaped: A (10) incendiary jet with a linked blast; grenades must be placed (Ultra-Tech p. 154).
Hint.hemp: A miniature shaped charge with a linked blast; +1 per die from TL11 (Ultra-Tech p. 155).
Hint.sefop: A forged slug from above, for homing rounds; it ignores posture and cover that doesn't protect from above (Ultra-Tech p. 155).
Hint.thermobaric: A blast of burning fuel; a quarter in vacuum, half in very thin air (Ultra-Tech p. 155).
Hint.stingray: Half the round at (0.25), then a linked lethal electrical discharge with surge (Ultra-Tech p. 156).
Hint.force: A gravity pulse: crushing, explosive, double knockback (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Hint.plasma: A one-shot plasma blast: burning, explosive, surge (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Hint.implosion: Crushing inward with double knockback, and linked toxic radiation (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Hint.emp: HT-8 (2) for anything Electrical in the radius, or out of action for seconds equal to the margin (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Hint.strobe: Anyone facing it resists at the table's penalty, +1 per yard from the center, or is stunned and blind (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Hint.warbler: Anyone hearing it resists at the table's penalty, +1 per yard from the center, or is deafened and in pain (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Hint.psiBomb: Will-5 in the radius, Mind Shield adding, or stunned; Digital Minds and IQ 0 are immune (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Hint.tangler: A grapple of the listed ST, rooting the victim in place: a Quick Contest of ST or Escape to break free (Ultra-Tech p. 155).
Hint.flare: 1d burn on a direct hit, and light over the radius; HT to avoid being blinded within 1% of it (Ultra-Tech p. 153).
Hint.jammer: -10 to radio and radar within the radius (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Hint.aerosol: A cloud of the filler's gas over the radius, taking that many doses (Ultra-Tech p. 153).
Hint.liquid: A pool of the filler over the radius, taking that many doses (Ultra-Tech p. 153).
Hint.swarm: Releases swarmbots over that many square yards (Ultra-Tech p. 156).
Hint.mininuke: Crushing explosive with a linked burn with radiation and surge, at the yield dialed (Ultra-Tech p. 156).
Hint.antimatter: Burning explosive with surge and linked toxic radiation, by the mass carried (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Hint.stasis: A stasis web over the radius, set for its duration before firing (Ultra-Tech p. 159).
Hint.vortex: Everything in the radius sent through hyperspace (Ultra-Tech p. 159).

Warheads.AmmunitionHint: This mode already fires a Basic Set round; clear it to fire the Ultra-Tech warhead.

Refusal.tl: That warhead needs a higher TL.
Refusal.notGrenade: That warhead isn't made for grenades or mines.
Refusal.notGun: That warhead is only for grenades and mines.
Refusal.tooSmall: The calibre is too small for that warhead.
Refusal.tooLarge: The calibre is too large for that warhead.
Refusal.electromagnetic: Gauss and rail guns already fire rounds like that.
Refusal.homing: Only homing projectiles carry that warhead.
Refusal.shotgun: Only shotguns, grenade launchers and gyrocs fire shotshells.

Note.monochain: Cutting (10) against a neck, face, skull, limb or extremity

Effect.emp: {name} is knocked out for {seconds} second(s) (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.empCyborg: {name} suffers a seizure for {seconds} second(s) (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.strobe: {name} is stunned and blind for {seconds} second(s) (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.strobeSeizure: {name} has a seizure for {minutes} minute(s) (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.warbler: {name} is deafened and in moderate pain for {minutes} minute(s) (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.warblerWorse: {name} is deafened and in moderate pain for {minutes} minute(s), with lingering hearing loss that heals like a crippling injury (Ultra-Tech p. 157).
Effect.psi: {name} is stunned, at -5 to recover, and loses the last two seconds of memory (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Effect.psiWorse: {name} is unconscious for {minutes} minute(s), and loses the last two seconds of memory (Ultra-Tech p. 158).
Effect.psiMessage: {name} is stunned by the message (Ultra-Tech p. 159).
Effect.psiMessageWorse: {name} hears the message echo for {minutes} minute(s), as moderate pain (Ultra-Tech p. 159).
Effect.psiImmune: {name} has no mind for a psi-bomb to reach: no effect (Ultra-Tech p. 158).

Proximity.Label: Proximity detonation
Proximity.Note: Proximity-fused: attack an area at +4; fragments only (Ultra-Tech p. 154; Campaigns p. 414)

Melee.Title: Ultra-tech melee
Melee.ReachHint: A monowire whip's, switchblade's or variable force sword's reach, within the weapon's own; blank for its longest. Changing it takes a Ready.
Melee.VibroHint: Vibrates when switched on: +1d cutting and an armour divisor (Ultra-Tech p. 164).
Melee.RocketHint: +$500 and 1 lb.; a boosted blow has +6 Striking ST and needs +3 ST (Ultra-Tech p. 163).
Melee.NeurolashHint: A neurolash added to this weapon: +$500, 0.5 lbs., a B cell for 20 strikes (Ultra-Tech p. 165).
Melee.HighPowerHint: Delivers a death beam's contact on the death setting (Ultra-Tech p. 165).
Melee.SprayerHint: +$50: two doses delivered as a follow-up once it penetrates (Ultra-Tech p. 166).
Melee.VariableHint: +$500: reach from C to 2, a Ready to change (Ultra-Tech p. 166).

Problem.notEdged: that edge needs a cutting or impaling weapon
Problem.notCutting: that edge needs a cutting weapon

Melee.VibroLine: Vibroblade ({state}): {seconds} seconds on a C cell; a Ready or Fast-Draw switches it on. A Hearing roll at a yard picks out its hum.
Melee.RocketLine: Rocket striker: {left} of {uses} boosts left; +{st} Striking ST and +{minSt} to the ST needed for a boosted blow.
Melee.SwitchLine: Now a {mode}; changing length or mode takes a Ready.
Melee.SnareLine: A snare pulled taut cuts thrust+1d({divisor}) each turn; a drop-weapon critical miss hits the wielder or a friend.
Melee.LimpetLine: Plants a mine that goes off 0 to {delay} seconds later; {magazine} mines to a magazine.
Melee.ChargesLine: {left} of {strikes} strikes left on the cell.
Melee.StunnerLine: A failed HT roll knocks the victim down paralysed; HT{recovery} each second to recover, DR no help. Holding contact with a Concentrate stops recovery and spends a strike a second.
Melee.ZapGloveLine: DR {dr} to the hand. Built into armour: +${cost} and {weight} lb.
Melee.NeurogloveLine: DR {dr}; damage through it wrecks it on a 1 in 6.
Melee.ForceLine: A Ready (or a Fast-Draw roll as it's drawn) activates it; the blade takes {seconds} second to form. It cuts any material as a tool.
Melee.NeuralHint: A failed HT roll has the neural disruptor's effect for this setting (Ultra-Tech pp. 121-122, 165).
Melee.RocketNote: Rocket striker: +{st} Striking ST on this blow.
Melee.RocketEmpty: The rocket striker is out of fuel.
Melee.CutHint: The weapon the blade parried, or that parried or blocked it short of a critical success (Ultra-Tech p. 166).
Melee.PickTarget: Target the character whose weapon the blade met.
Melee.StunnedLine: {name} convulses, falls and is paralysed: HT{recovery} each second to recover.
Melee.LimpetDr: DR of what it's stuck to
Melee.LimpetFlesh: Stuck to flesh (1 HP to pull off)
Melee.BladeTooltip: An ultra-tech edge, which reprices the weapon and changes its damage (Ultra-Tech pp. 163-164).

BladeHint.superfine: +2 cutting and impaling, armour divisor (2) (Ultra-Tech p. 163).
BladeHint.monowire: +2 cutting, armour divisor (10); can't cut into a flat surface (Ultra-Tech p. 163).
BladeHint.hyperdense: +2 cutting and impaling, armour divisor (5); ST 1.5 times (Ultra-Tech p. 164).
BladeHint.nanothorn: Corrosion instead of cutting, armour divisor (10) (Ultra-Tech p. 164).
BladeHint.vibro: The vibro field is on: +1d cutting and a better armour divisor (Ultra-Tech p. 164).

Melee.VibroDrainedHint: The vibroblade has run 300 seconds divided by its weight on its cell; it cuts as a plain blade until the cell is replaced.
Melee.WreckedHint: Damage to the hand wrecked this neuroglove as a weapon.
Melee.WreckedRefusal: The {name} is wrecked as a weapon.
Melee.GloveWrecked: Damage through the neuroglove (rolled {roll}): it's wrecked as a weapon.
Melee.GloveSurvives: Damage through the neuroglove (rolled {roll}): it still works.
Melee.HoldLine: Held in contact (Concentrate): the victim can't roll to recover this second. {left} charge(s) left.

Completes.combatOrSpaceHelmet: a combat infantry helmet or a space helmet
Completes.maskOrHelmet: an air mask or a combat infantry helmet
Completes.maskOrGill: an air mask or an artificial gill

Threat.Don: Takes {on} s to put on, {off} s to take off.
Threat.DonSkill: Takes {on} s to put on or take off; a {skill} roll halves it.
Threat.DonArmor: Takes {seconds} s a piece to put on or take off.
Threat.TankHours: Holds {hours} hours of air at TL{tl}. {hookUp} s to hook up, {jettison} s to jettison.
Threat.TankMinutes: Holds {minutes} minutes of air at TL{tl}. {hookUp} s to hook up, {jettison} s to jettison.
Threat.Patches: Patching a breach takes {seconds} s and a Vacc Suit roll, -1 for each failure; every attempt costs {minutes} minutes of air.

Patch.Title: Patch the suit
Patch.Label: Patch a breach ({item})
Patch.Sealed: The breach is sealed. The attempt cost {minutes} minutes of air.
Patch.Failed: The patch doesn't hold: the next attempt is at a further -1. The attempt cost {minutes} minutes of air.

Laser.ablative: Ablative: DR {dr} against any laser, a point lost at the spot struck for every 10 points of basic laser damage.
Laser.reflec: Reflec: DR {dr} against lasers and microwaves, none against X-ray or gamma-ray lasers or anything else.
Laser.retroReflective: Retro-reflective: DR {dr} against lasers and microwaves, and half of what it stops from a visible or near-infrared laser bounces back.

Reason.ablative: ablative armour's full DR against a laser
Reason.reflec: reflec's full DR against a laser or microwave
Reason.retroReflective: retro-reflective armour's full DR against a laser or microwave
Reason.transparent: transparent bioplas is no use against lasers

Laser.Bounced: {item} bounces {damage} points of the beam's damage back at {attacker}, who gets no defence if they didn't expect it.
Laser.TransparentHint: Almost invisible when worn, and twice the price, but no protection against lasers (Ultra-Tech p. 174).
Laser.ReflectiveHint: A rigid helmet made reflective: +20 DR against lasers and microwaves, +$50 (Ultra-Tech p. 173).

Tailor.Title: Tailored
Tailor.Hint: Build this suit into an outfit of your own: coverage, style and cut (Ultra-Tech pp. 174-175).

Reason.uncovered: the outfit doesn't cover this spot
Reason.arc: the outfit doesn't cover this spot from that side
Reason.missed: rolled {roll} against {target}: the blow missed the covered part
Reason.struck: rolled {roll} against {target}: the blow struck the covered part

Systems.EmaHint: Doubles DR, or triples it for laminate armour, against shaped charges and plasma bolts (Ultra-Tech p. 187).
Systems.EmaUsesHint: How many uses the vehicle or suit's power gives it; 0 doesn't count them.
Systems.EmaSpent: {item}'s EMA stopped the blow: {used} of {uses} uses spent.
Systems.AdaptiveHint: How many beam types it adapts to at once, 0 for none. $1,000 a pound for one, $4,000 for two, $9,000 for three, $16,000 for four (Ultra-Tech p. 190).
Systems.PasteHint: Reactive paste: adds its DR against bullets, beams and explosions, and detonates (Ultra-Tech p. 189).
Systems.PasteLine: Reactive paste: DR {dr}, {shaped} against shaped charges, against high-velocity attacks.
Systems.PasteDetonated: The reactive paste on {item} detonates at the {location}: {name} takes 1d crushing explosive damage, which the armour protects against. A later hit there may find it spent.
Systems.LivingMetalHint: Made of living metal at twice the price: it seals holes in two seconds and repairs a point of DR or HP an hour (Ultra-Tech p. 190).
Systems.LivingMetalRepair: Living metal: seals a hole in two seconds and repairs a point of DR or HP an hour.
Systems.BioplasRepair: Bioplas heals its own damage, 1 HP every {hours} hours.
Systems.FoamOn: {name} is coated in ablative foam: DR {dr} against burning damage. It takes {seconds} seconds a person to apply.
Systems.FoamHint: DR against burning, Hardened against lasers, a point lost for every point struck
Systems.FoamLine: Ablative foam: DR {dr} against burning only, Hardened against lasers, a point lost at the spot for every point of damage. {radar} to radar. {seconds} s to apply.
Systems.PlugsLine: Nasal filter plugs: +5 HT against breathed gas, while the mouth is closed. The bonus drops by 1 every two hours after four hours of use, and is gone after ten.
Systems.NearMissLine: Near-miss indicator: +2 to Vision rolls to find where projectile fire came from, with a HUD, not in vacuum.
Systems.MindShieldLine: Mind shield: +{bonus} to IQ or Will against telepathic abilities, and to Will against attempts to find the wearer's mind.
Systems.BiomedicalLine: Biomedical sensors: +{inPerson} to Diagnosis on the wearer in person, or Diagnosis at {remote} from afar.

Reason.warsuit: Warsuit: Hardened 3 against shaped charges and plasma

Systems.SelfRepaired: {name} repairs itself over {hours} hour(s): {lost} DR still to regain.

Agents.Title: Biochemical and nano weapons
Agents.KindHint: What this is, where the name doesn't say (Ultra-Tech pp. 159-162).
Agents.DeliveryHint: How a metabolic nanoweapon reaches its victim, which sets its price (Ultra-Tech p. 161).
Agents.DisadvantageHint: The mental disadvantage it instills or erases (Ultra-Tech p. 162).
Agents.PointsHint: The disadvantage's value: $100 a point (Ultra-Tech p. 162).
Agents.ReversibleHint: Double cost: the change undoes itself after a set time (Ultra-Tech p. 162).
Agents.MindTrappingHint: $100,000: stores the host's mind as a ghost program (Ultra-Tech p. 162).
Agents.PoisonLine: Resisted with {resist}; {delivery}. Dosed from the row action on targeted characters, or the sheet's Poison button.

Effect.riotGas: Each second in the cloud: a failure nauseates while there, by 5 or more retching; nauseated minutes equal to the margin after leaving.
Effect.nerveGas: 1d toxic a minute for six cycles; coughing and Neurological Disorder as HP is lost.
Effect.nerveGasResidue: Touching a contaminated area after the attack: HT-3.
Effect.sleepGas: Unconscious for the margin's minutes, then ordinary sleep.
Effect.paralysisGas: Each turn in the cloud: failing by 1-2 falls for the turn, by 3 or more paralysed for the margin's minutes; a critical failure is 1d and a coma.
Effect.pheromoneSpray: Lecherousness (9) while in the cloud and the margin's minutes after; aliens are almost never affected.
Effect.radiantPrism: Breathed without a filter: 1 point a second.
Effect.nervePoison: 1d toxic a minute for six cycles, with the nerve gas's symptoms.
Effect.contactNervePoison: On a blade (not a vibroblade) or a surface: +2 to resist, ten times the cost.
Effect.sleepPoison: Drowsy; by 5 or more unconscious for the margin's minutes.
Effect.contactSleepPoison: On a blade (not a vibroblade) or a surface: +2 to resist, ten times the cost.
Effect.nanoburn: Paralysed three minutes a point of failure, then 1d-1 every three minutes for half an hour. Torpine stops the damage; Aegis nano works.
Effect.dominator: Instills or erases the disadvantage on a failed HT-6 after six hours; permanent until undone.
Effect.dominatorSuperscience: As dominator nano, after a minute.
Effect.parasiteSeed: HT-4 each hour: a success kills the seed, a failure takes 3 HT; at 0 the host becomes a nanomorph.
Effect.splatter: 1d a dose per minute circulating (30d a dose at most), set off by timer or radio. Detonate it from the GM tool, with Aegis contests.
Effect.shrike: Hunts Aegis nano a contest a minute; run it from the GM tool.
Effect.antiTangler: Dissolves tangler bonds in one second.
Effect.disassemblerGlop: Half a chemical round's burst radius; double a disassembler cloud's damage, for 15 seconds.

Agents.SmokeLine: {vision} to see or aim through; blocks {blocks}. {senses}
Agents.SmokeSenses: Also penalizes Infravision, Hyperspectral Vision and Night Vision.
Agents.SmokeFormLine: Forms at a second per 5 yards of radius; lingers one to four minutes.
Agents.RadiantPrismLine: {penalty} to infrared- and radar-aimed attacks and sighting; lasts half as long; breathed without a filter, 1 point a second.
Agents.MuskLine: Bad Smell for {days} days, a day less per hour of washing; a sealed suit protects its wearer, not the suit.
Agents.MaskLine: {penalty} to Forensics for chemical traces and to tracking by scent through the masked area; the mask itself is easy to track.
Agents.FirefoamLine: Puts out fires of up to {dice}d; larger ones burn lower for 3d seconds.
Agents.EmbrittlementLine: 3d corrosion an hour to one metal for 12 hours, times SM for a large object inside the area; the GM tool rolls it.
Agents.NanotracerLine: +{bonus} to track the victim for a day or more; Aegis and diagnostic nano look for them at {penalty}.
Agents.CloudLine: The cloud lasts {seconds} seconds in a {wind} mph wind.
Agents.MuskSealed: {name}'s sealed suit keeps the musk off them, but the suit reeks.

Protected.metabolic: {name} has no metabolism for it to act on.

Failed.riotGasNauseated: {name} is nauseated while in the cloud.
Failed.riotGasRetching: {name} is retching while in the cloud, and nauseated {minutes} minute(s) after leaving it.
Failed.sleepGas: {name} is unconscious for {minutes} minute(s), then sleeps.
Failed.paralysisGasFalls: {name} falls and can't move this turn.
Failed.paralysisGasCritical: {name} takes 1d and falls into a coma.
Failed.pheromoneSpray: {name} gains Lecherousness (9) while in the cloud and for {minutes} minute(s) after.
Failed.nanoburn: {name} is paralysed for {minutes} x3 minutes; the nanomachines start their damage.
Failed.dominator: {name} gains or loses the programmed disadvantage.
Failed.parasiteSeedHt: {name} has lost {lost} HT to the seed; {left} left.
Failed.parasiteSeedDone: {name}'s HT is gone: they die, and the body becomes a nanomorph.

Tool.Title: Biochemical agents
Tool.PickVictims: Target or select the characters first.

Splatter.Title: Splatter nano
Splatter.Contests: Aegis won {wins} of the contests over {minutes} minute(s).
Splatter.Exterminated: Aegis exterminated the splatter before it went off.
Splatter.Label: Splatter detonates ({dice} dice)

Shrike.Title: Shrike nano
Shrike.AegisDead: the shrike kills the Aegis nano.
Shrike.DoseKilled: Aegis kills a dose of shrike.

Cloud.Title: Release the cloud
Cloud.NoPlace: No scene or place for the cloud: target a token or place a template.

Guns.Title: Guns, launchers and grenades
Guns.EtcHint: Electrothermal-chemical: 1.5 times piercing damage and range, twice the cost (Ultra-Tech p. 139).
Guns.LiquidHint: 1.5 times the shots a magazine holds and the cost, with boosted and low velocity (Ultra-Tech p. 139).
Guns.NonMetallicHint: 1.5 times the cost; unloaded, it passes ordinary metal detectors (Ultra-Tech p. 140).
Guns.ReactionlessHint: No backblast, five times the Max range; the missiles cost twice as much (Ultra-Tech p. 145).
Guns.SmartHint: A chip and communicator for programmed fusing: +$100 at TL9, free from TL10 (Ultra-Tech p. 147).
Guns.HomingTooltip: A homing seeker in the round this mode fires, where the round is big enough (Ultra-Tech p. 146).

Refusal.tl: That seeker isn't available at this weapon's TL.
Refusal.tooSmall: The round is too small for that seeker at this TL.

Guns.HomingLine: Homing skill {skill}, by {sense}; rounds cost x{cost}.
Guns.HomingHint: The projectile homes by {sense}; aim with Artillery (Guided Missile) for its Acc (Ultra-Tech p. 146).
Guns.EtcLine: ETC: an {cell} cell in the grip fires {magazines} magazines.
Guns.LiquidLine: Liquid propellant: a bottle fires {magazines} magazines and takes {seconds} seconds to change.
Guns.VelocityLine: Choose boosted or low velocity in the attack dialog.
Guns.GyrocLine: Damage divided by 3 at 1-2 yards and 2 at 3-10 with solid rockets; a Hearing roll to spot the firer by sound.
Guns.BackblastLine: Backblast: {damage} burning to everyone in a {yards}-yard cone behind, rolled when it fires.
Guns.ReactionlessLine: Reactionless: no backblast, x{range} Max range; missiles x{cost} cost.
Guns.GrenadeLine: Goes off {seconds} seconds after it's released; a second to pull the pin. {smart}
Guns.SmartLine: Smart: {readies} Readies to program, or pull the pin as an ordinary grenade.
Guns.SaucerLine: Thrown with Throwing; bounced round a corner at {penalty}; a scattering saucer bounces back off what stops it.
Guns.LimpetLine: Sticks and unsticks by radio; without its code, pulled off at ST{st}, a try a second.
Guns.VortexLine: Can be bounced off glancing surfaces round corners; light winds don't disturb it.
Guns.SprayCanLine: Up to {doses} doses at once fill a one-yard radius; the cloud lasts {seconds} seconds indoors.

VelocityNote.boosted: Boosted: +1 damage a die, x{range} range, {propellant} shots of propellant.
VelocityNote.low: Low: half damage, x{range} range, {hearing} to hear it, {propellant} shot of propellant.

Guns.Programmed: Set for {fuse} ({delay} s where it counts); {readies} Readies to program.
Guns.LimpetFlesh: Is it stuck to flesh (a point of injury to pull off)?

Suits.Title: Powered suit
Suits.OnHint: Off, or out of power, the suit adds nothing and its weight counts (Ultra-Tech p. 182).
Suits.AugmentationHint: Off, the cybersuit adds no ST, Move or Super Jump and doesn't limit DX, but still carries its own weight (Ultra-Tech p. 184).
Suits.FittedHint: An unfitted TL9-10 suit gives -1 to DX and DX-based skills (Ultra-Tech p. 182).
Suits.AccustomedHint: After a day carrying the same load, its mass no longer penalises DX (Ultra-Tech p. 75).
Suits.LoadHint: The weight in the pack. It comes off the carried gear that isn't worn, heaviest first.

Scope.all: Battlesuit skill limits DX and DX-based skills.
Scope.lowerBody: Battlesuit skill limits only tasks that need lower-body agility, such as melee attacks or jumping; the GM applies it.
Scope.arm: Battlesuit skill limits only tasks with the sleeved arm; the GM applies it.

Suits.WeightPowered: Its weight doesn't count toward encumbrance while powered.
Suits.WeightAlways: Its weight doesn't count toward encumbrance, even with augmentation off, while powered.
Suits.Payload: Carries up to {lbs} lbs. weightlessly while powered.
Suits.Fitting: Fitted to its wearer at TL9-10: refitting takes two hours and an Armoury (Body Armor)+2 roll.
Suits.Nanogel: Nanogel fits it to any wearer within 10% of its size.
Suits.Checkout: {stepIn} s to step in, {helmet} s for a helmet, {seconds} s to check out; a Battlesuit roll halves the checkout.

Note.sm1: The wearer is SM +1 in it.
Note.sm2: The wearer is SM +2 in it.
Note.hamFisted: The wearer is Ham-Fisted (-3 DX) for fine work.
Note.badGrip: The wearer has Bad Grip 2, and can't crawl, get up from prone, jump or swim.
Note.noSmell: No Sense of Smell/Taste outside the suit unless the hatch is open.

Unpowered.paralysed: Without power the wearer is effectively paralysed until they leave the suit.
Unpowered.nothing: Without power the field gives no DR and no enhancement.
Unpowered.carry: Without power the wearer can still move, but carries the suit's weight on their own ST.

Suits.Gravpack: Cancels the weight of up to {max} lbs. in the pack; -1 DX per {per} lbs. until used to the load.
Suits.CheckoutFast: Suited up and checked out in {seconds} seconds.
Suits.CheckoutSlow: Suited up and checked out in {seconds} seconds.
Suits.RefitDone: After {hours} hours the suit fits its new wearer.
Suits.RefitAgain: After {hours} hours the suit still doesn't fit: another attempt is needed.
Suits.RefitBroken: After {hours} hours the suit is damaged, or has a fault that won't show until it's used in action (GM's choice).

Medical.Title: Medical gear and drugs
Medical.FormHint: Pill or injection at the listed price, aerosol or contact agent x2, aerosol contact agent x10 (Ultra-Tech p. 204).
Medical.LifeSupportLine: Life support: attach a patient with Electronics Operation (Medical), 10 seconds a try; mortal wound checks daily, +{bonus}.
Medical.MedicalBedLine: +{bonus} to a physician's rounds; {rounds} rounds a day.
Medical.SuppliesLine: +1 to a physician's rounds, {days} patient-days; a doctor makes {rounds} rounds a day for up to {patients} patients. Without supplies, care is at TL6.
Medical.SuitDocLine: Physician-10 care for the wearer; a drug pack lasts {days} days.
Medical.SprayLine: Stops bleeding and restores 1 HP in {seconds} seconds.
Medical.Attached: {name} is on life support (+{bonus} to mortal wound checks, made daily).
Medical.BedTitle: In or out of the bed
Medical.InBed: {name} is in the medical bed: +3 to a physician's rounds, {rounds} a day.
Medical.OutOfBed: {name} is out of the medical bed.
Medical.IntoHibernation: {name} goes into hibernation over {hours} hour: a tenth the life support and ageing.
Medical.IntoNanostasis: {name} goes into nanostasis over {hours} hours: no air, food or ageing.

Revived.clear: {name} is revived after {out} hours, confused (9) for {hours} hours.
Revived.daily: {name} is revived after {out} hours: confused (9) for {hours} hours and partial amnesia for at least a week, a HT roll daily to recover.
Revived.weekly: {name} is revived after {out} hours: confused (9) for {hours} hours and partial amnesia for at least a week, a HT roll weekly to recover.

Inhibited.limb: {name}'s limb is paralysed and numb below the disk; +1 to First Aid for shock.
Inhibited.spine: {name} is paralysed from the neck down.

Rejuvenation.rejuvenated: {name} is young and healthy again after {days} days.
Rejuvenation.confused: {name} is rejuvenated after {days} days, but confused (9) for 1d days.
Rejuvenation.amnesia: {name} is rejuvenated after {days} days, with partial amnesia.
Rejuvenation.disaster: The rejuvenation goes terribly wrong for {name}: a messy death, or a body with no mind.

Chrysalis.mindless: {name}'s body lives again, with no mind or personality.

Medical.RayBarred: {name} can't take regeneration treatment again yet.

Ray.healed: {name} is healed of all damage; age and mortal-wound losses are restored and missing parts regrow.
Ray.toxic: Something goes wrong: {name} takes 3d toxic and can't be treated again for 1d weeks.
Ray.sideEffect: {name} seems healed, but a side effect will show in 1d weeks.

Resisted.morphazine: {name} falls into a deep, dreamless sleep for {minutes} minutes.
Resisted.soothe: {name} drifts into euphoria, with High Pain Threshold, for {minutes} minutes, and won't remember it.
Resisted.crediline: {name} becomes trusting and talkative: Gullibility (9) for {minutes} minutes.

Drug.analgine: {name} feels no pain, and is Numb, for {hours} hours.
Drug.antirad: The next exposure's rads are halved for {name}.
Drug.hyperstim: {name} is awake and can't fail a roll to stay conscious; when it wears off, roll HT.
Drug.ascepaline: {name} regenerates 1 HP every 4 hours for a day.
Drug.purge: {name}'s system clears of active drugs in {minutes} minutes.
Drug.purgeNausea: The purge does nothing, and {name} is nauseated for an hour.
Drug.purgeFailed: The purge has no effect on {name}.
Drug.memoryBeta: {name} can recall almost anything with an IQ roll; a failure loses them in their memories.
Drug.immuneWrong: The treatment was wrong: no effect.
Drug.criticalRepair: {name} can lose the Wounded disadvantage or regain the HT a mortal wound took.
Drug.respirocytes: {name} has +2 FP and doesn't need to breathe until the oxygen is used up.
Drug.torpine: {name} falls into a healing trance for 24 hours.
Drug.fastRegeneration: {name} regenerates fast for an hour, at 1 FP for each HP healed.

Medical.QuickhealHour: No more than one dose of quickheal an hour.
Medical.TorpineWakes: {name} wakes fully healed, famished, at 1 FP.
Medical.Stumped: The {name} is stumped: it sustains the patient and calls for help.

MemoryBeta.lost: {name} gets lost in their memories, reliving pieces of their life.
MemoryBeta.captured: {name} is captured by an especially strong memory; it may trigger buried phobias or trauma.

CriticalRepair.wounded: The nano repairs {name}'s scarring: Wounded is gone.

Force.Title: Force field
Force.RegenLine: Spent DR regenerates {rate} a second, on or off.
Force.SealedLine: While on: sealed, with pressure and vacuum support and radiation PF {pf}. A Ready maneuver turns it on or off.
Force.OpenLine: While on: not sealed, radiation PF {pf}. A Ready maneuver turns it on or off.
Force.BarrierLine: Barrier screen, {diameter} yards across: SM +{sm}. A shot that misses its target by no more than the SM difference hits the screen, and what penetrates may hit another occupant.
Force.ConformalLine: Conformal screen: covers what the wearer carries, up to extra-heavy encumbrance; a Ready maneuver covers anything picked up.
Force.CloakingLine: Cloaking: invisible to sight and active sensors; the power lasts half as long.
Force.OpaqueLine: Opaque: nothing inside can be seen or detected by active sensors from outside.
Force.StabilizedLine: Reality-stabilized: blocks matter transmission and reality disruption coming in.
Force.SafetyLine: Safety switch: turns on at an incoming attack slower than light, and after a beam is fired at the wearer.

Reason.energy: an energy screen doesn't stop this attack
Reason.kinetic: a kinetic screen doesn't stop energy attacks
Reason.velocity: a velocity screen stops only fast attacks

Force.AdjustHint: +100% to cost. A Ready maneuver reinforces one half at ×1.5 DR and weakens the other to ×1/2 (Ultra-Tech p. 191).
Force.DiameterHint: Cost and weight scale with the diameter; the SM follows it (Ultra-Tech p. 191).

Option.cloakingHint: +100% to cost; halves the operating time.
Option.energyHint: -50% to cost; stops only energy attacks and isn't sealed.
Option.kineticHint: -50% to cost; stops no energy attacks or radiation. Not with energy.
Option.opaqueHint: No extra cost; hides everything inside.
Option.permeableHint: +50% to cost; can let air through.
Option.velocityHint: -10% to cost; stops only fast attacks and isn't sealed.

Force.BreathingHint: Lets gas through so the user can breathe, and isn't sealed; a Ready maneuver (a second for a life support field) changes it.
Force.ReflectLine: A successful block against a ranged beam lets the wielder roll DX to return the blocked damage to the attacker.
Force.WardLine: A stationary barrier two yards high and a yard wide with hardened DR 100; its generator is on one side.
Force.Reflected: The shield returns {damage} points of the beam's damage to the attacker.
Force.NotReflected: The beam is blocked but not returned.
Force.StasisLine: Setting the duration takes {set} s and switching it on {on} s; only a reality stabilizer ends it early.
Force.StasisOn: {name} is in stasis for {seconds} seconds: nothing can affect them, and they can do nothing.
Force.TauInfinity: {name}'s tau-shield freezes them for {seconds} seconds, using {minutes} minutes of power.
Force.LifeSupportLine: While on: DR {dr} against energy attacks, radiation divided by {divisor}, +{heat}°F on the hot side of the comfort zone, and sealed unless set to breathe; without air or breathing, the air goes bad in 15 minutes.
Force.TauLine: Tactical: {ratio} subjective seconds a second, {extra} extra maneuvers a turn; the cell lasts {minutes} minutes. Infinity: stasis, {infinity} minutes of power a use.

Tau.LevelsHint: Levels 1-9: each is one more maneuver a turn, and divides the cell's 180 minutes.

Force.StabilizerLine: Blocks temporal, parachronic, FTL and teleportation superscience inside its radius and from outside into it.
Force.HypertimeLine: Everything outside seems frozen to those inside; nothing inside can affect the outside until it collapses.
Force.CollapsePick: Target whoever is in the stasis web.
Force.ShieldVanishes: The force shield's power is spent: it vanishes.
Force.SquareFeetHint: A stasis grid is $2,000 and 0.2 lbs. for each square foot it covers; a coffin-sized box is 72 square feet (Ultra-Tech p. 193).
Force.StasisGridLine: {squareFeet} square feet: ${cost}, {weight} lbs., on vehicle or building power.
Force.NoUsesLeft: Its cell has no uses left: change the cells.

Cyber.Title: Cybernetics
Cyber.ProcedureLine: {count} × {procedure} {kind}procedure at TL{tl}: {modifier} to Surgery, {minutes} min., {injury} HP injury on a failure, recovery {recovery} {unit}, ${fee} at a clinic.
Cyber.BrainRisk: A critical failure on major or radical brain surgery may cost a point of IQ or leave a disadvantage such as Epilepsy.
Cyber.ChipCaps: At TL{tl}: at most {slots} slots and {points} points a chip; skill chips ${perPoint} a point.
Cyber.CognitiveCap: At TL{tl}: at most {points} points an operation, ${price} a point.
Cyber.PsychLine: The disadvantage waits for the recovery to end. Worn three months or more, it may stay after removal.
Cyber.ConditionHint: Second-hand parts are 20-70% of the price, salvaged ones 10-35% (Ultra-Tech p. 208).
Cyber.SurgeLine: The surge knocks out {name}'s electrical implants ({list}) for {minutes} minutes.
Cyber.PsychTooSoon: Worn less than three months: the disadvantage ends with the implant.
Cyber.PsychFreed: The implant's effect ends with it.
Cyber.PsychStays: The disadvantage stays: the implant's effect has become permanent.

Tool.Title: Cybernetic surgery
Tool.Summary: {operation}: {done} of {count} {procedure} procedures succeeded; {minutes} minutes, ${fee} at a clinic.
Tool.CriticalSuccess: A critical success: the recovery is halved.
Tool.Injury: {name} takes {injury} HP of injury where the surgery was.
Tool.Defective: A critical failure: double injury, or defective cybernetics that break down at the worst moment or bring a disadvantage (GM's choice).
Tool.BrainInjury: Brain surgery gone wrong: the patient may lose a point of IQ, or gain a disadvantage such as Epilepsy or Phantom Voices.
Tool.SalvageDamaged: The parts come out needing major repairs.
Tool.PickBoth: Select the examiner's token and target the patient.
Tool.TrapGoesOff: The cyber-trap goes off: its effect is the GM's (a bomb implant, a poison, a wiped chip).

Cyber.SeedHint: A pill-sized seed that grows the implant inside the body: twice the price, only for implants that take a minor or simple operation at TL11 (Ultra-Tech p. 202).
Cyber.SeedLine: An implant seed: it grows in {hours} hour(s), and shows on a diagnostic bed or medscanner halfway through.
Cyber.SeedCantGrow: An implant seed can't grow this: it takes more than a minor operation at TL11.
Cyber.BombHint: Priced as a smart grenade: 40mm or 25mm in the torso, 15mm in a limb, 10mm elsewhere (Ultra-Tech pp. 146-147, 210).
Cyber.BombLine: A {calibre}mm smart grenade: 6d cr ex for an ounce; vitals x3, skull x4; an exploding skull throws 1d-3 cut fragments.
Cyber.BombUnpriced: The book prices no {calibre}mm hand grenade: the GM sets the cost.

equipmentOptions.Name: Equipment options and statistics
equipmentOptions.Hint: Gear takes options that reprice it: disguised (x2 mass-produced, x5 custom), styling in three tiers (+1 reaction from collectors and buyers for x2, +2 for x5, +3 for x10, while the piece is marked as shown), rugged (+2 HT, twice the DR, x2 cost, x1.2 weight), cheap (x1/2 cost, and either x1.5 weight or fragile at -2 HT and half the DR) and expensive (x2 cost, x2/3 weight); cheap and expensive leave the batteries out of the weight. Rugged, cheap and expensive aren't offered on clothing, weapons or armour. The item sheet shows HP, HT and DR as assumed (HT 10, rugged +2, good quality +1 and fine +2 on top), and whether gear under a thousandth of the campaign TL's average starting wealth may skip maintenance (High-Tech pp. 9-11).

combinationGadgets.Name: Combination gadgets
combinationGadgets.Hint: A row action builds one gadget from several of the character's: the heaviest part's empty weight plus 80% of the others' (50% where only one works at a time), the costliest part's price plus 80% (or 50%) of the others', one set of batteries, and the lowest LC of the parts. The parts stay on the sheet (High-Tech p. 10).

gearForSm.Name: Gear for other sizes
gearForSm.Hint: Gear marked to adjust for SM costs, weighs and draws power by the carrier's Size Modifier, from x1/20 at SM -4 to x2,000 at SM +10; the battery count scales with it once the batteries rule is on (High-Tech p. 10).

antiqueLegality.Name: Legality of antiques
antiqueLegality.Hint: Obsolete gear's LC rises by one for every two full TLs it is behind the campaign, two at most and no higher than LC4. Gear marked as chemical, biological or nuclear weapons stays as it is. The item sheet shows the class it is carried under (High-Tech p. 8).

blackMarket.Name: The black market
blackMarket.Hint: A GM tool for the selected buyer rolls the search in secret: a Contact's effective Streetwise or the buyer's own, minus the Control Rating, with Cultural Familiarity, +1 for a port, a low-CR border or weak law enforcement, -3 in an unfamiliar area, and +3 on the gray market. It whispers the GM what came of it by market (general, electronics, medical, combat gear), and the price: 5% of the legal price for copied media and textiles, about 60% for the rest, 50-80% used and 1-10% old stock. Outlawed (LC0) goods are left to an adventure (High-Tech pp. 7-10).

equipmentBonuses.Name: Equipment Bond and intrinsic bonuses
equipmentBonuses.Hint: A tool can carry an intrinsic bonus beside its quality, and the Equipment Bond perk gives +1 with the piece it names; both add to quality's bonus on the skill the tool serves (High-Tech pp. 7, 11).

tlFamiliarity.Name: TL penalties as unfamiliarity
tlFamiliarity.Hint: Optional: a DX-based skill's TL penalty, on an attack or from a tool, counts as unfamiliarity instead. It stays as large while the character is unfamiliar with the gear (the familiarity rule's -2 is folded into it) and goes once the gear is on their familiarity list. IQ-based rolls keep it (High-Tech p. 11).

firearmQuality.Name: Firearm quality
firearmQuality.Hint: Accurate and reliable work as separate grades on a gun: fine accurate +1 Acc (base Acc 2+) for 75% of its price, very fine +2 Acc (base Acc 4+) for 375%; fine reliable a step of Malf. for 25%, very fine two steps for 125%, none for a full-automatic weapon. A gun taken past Malf. 17 stays at 17 and rolls a malfunction again. These replace the Basic Set's fine and very fine grade on a gun (High-Tech p. 79).

gunCare.Name: Gun care
gunCare.Hint: -1 Malf. for a shooter at default or short of the gun's ST, and for a cloth belt; Malf. and Acc a gun has lost to abuse, age or harsh surroundings; a sniper rifle or target pistol rolling HT rather than HT+4 against abuse; rugged guns at HT 11 or 12; and at TL6-8, misfires and stoppages swapped on the malfunction table for anything but a revolver (High-Tech pp. 80-81, 129).

immediateAction.Name: Immediate Action
immediateAction.Hint: Clearing a stoppage takes -4 on the Armoury or IQ-based weapon skill roll, bought off by the Immediate Action technique for the weapon skill, plus the gun's TL and familiarity penalties. It takes two Ready maneuvers for a magazine-fed self-loader, four for a belt-fed gun (three with an assistant gunner) and three otherwise; Armorer's Gift and Weapon Bond help (High-Tech pp. 81, 249-251).

gunDrawing.Name: Drawing guns
gunDrawing.Hint: Fast-Draw one gun per hand each turn, the off hand at -4; a failure ends the turn's drawing and a critical failure drops the gun, or both. The odd positions apply, with where the gun is carried: a pistol +0 in the belt or at the hip, -1 at the small of the back or in a shoulder holster, -2 in an ankle holster or boot, -3 in a pocket or concealed; a long arm +0 on a patrol sling, -2 slung over the shoulder, -4 on the back. Holsters and slings by name: a military holster -2 (none with its flap tucked away), an undercover holster -1, a Fast-Draw rig +2, a patrol sling +1; a pistol takes a Ready in or out of its holster, a slung long arm two (three from the back), and a successful Fast-Draw saves one. A sleeve holster fails or breaks on its own terms, a retention holster gives +2 to Retain Weapon, a lanyard lets you recover a dropped gun with a DX roll, and Quick-Sheathe stows a gun as fast as Fast-Draw draws it (High-Tech pp. 81-82, 153-154, 249).

gunfightStandoff.Name: Who draws first (guns)
gunfightStandoff.Hint: A GM tool for a standoff between two gunfighters outside combat: a ready gun fires first against a foe without Fast-Draw, or wins a Quick Contest of weapon skill against Fast-Draw at -10 (+1 for Combat Reflexes, and ties); otherwise Fast-Draw or weapon skill decides, with +4 for a hand on the gun, -1 for the worse Bulk, and the odd positions (High-Tech p. 82).

triggerMechanisms.Name: Trigger mechanisms
triggerMechanisms.Hint: A gun's trigger as a field on it: single-action, double-action, double-action-only or safe-action. Left blank, a revolver at RoF 1 is single-action, one at RoF 2 or more double-action, and anything else single-action. An aimed shot from a double-action gun takes -1 unless the hammer was cocked first (a cocked revolver fires that one shot); a double-action-only gun is a point of Acc lower; DAO and safe-action guns are almost impossible to fire by accident (High-Tech p. 82).

burstFire.Name: Fire selectors and bursts
burstFire.Hint: A gun with a fire selector changes setting from its row: the listed RoF, a second RoF after a slash, or single shots at RoF 3 for any setting of RoF 4+ without a "!". Changing takes a Ready maneuver in combat, unless the gun has a double or progressive trigger. A limited-burst gun fires one to three whole bursts per attack (shots between bursts come down to the burst below) and can't use Spraying Fire; a high-cyclic gun ("#") is limited to bursts too, counts its hits at Rcl 1 and can't use Suppression Fire (High-Tech pp. 82-83).

fastFiring.Name: Fast-firing
fastFiring.Hint: A semiautomatic or double-action gun of RoF 2 or 3 pulled faster, up to RoF 6, at -4 to skill (bought off by the Fast-Firing technique) and +2 Rcl at RoF 5, +4 at RoF 6; it still can't use Spraying Fire, but at RoF 5 or 6 it may use Suppression Fire. A single-action revolver held in two hands is cocked with the off thumb: RoF 2 at no penalty, or up to RoF 4 at -2, bought off by Two-Handed Thumbing. Not for a limited-burst gun (High-Tech pp. 84, 251-252).

fanningAndThumbing.Name: Fanning and thumbing
fanningAndThumbing.Hint: A single-action revolver of RoF 1 fanned at RoF 2 for -4 (bought off by the Fanning technique), with another -2 for each RoF above 2 up to 5 and +2 Rcl at RoF 5, none of which a technique buys off, and never aimed; a critical failure fires nothing (the rounds stay in the gun) and drops the gun (1-3 on 1d) or bruises the hand, moderate pain for minutes equal to the margin of failure. Thumbing fires RoF 2 at -2 (bought off by the Thumbing technique); a failure fires nothing that turn and keeps its rounds, a critical failure drops the gun or fires it wild. A revolver whose trigger is tied back or removed can only be fanned or thumbed (High-Tech pp. 83-84, 251-252).

pistolero.Name: Two-handed pistol stance
pistolero.Hint: A pistol's row toggles the two-handed stance: minimum ST times 0.8 (rounded up), Bulk a step better on Move and Attack and in close combat, and every aimed shot braced. A gun in the stance can't be fanned or thumbed (High-Tech p. 84).

precisionAiming.Name: Precision Aiming
precisionAiming.Hint: A braced, scoped gun aimed for 6, 12, 24, 45 and 90 seconds may claim a further +1 each time, from the gun's row: an IQ-based weapon skill roll at -6, which the Precision Aiming technique buys off, with the GM's modifier for the conditions. The extra bonus can't pass +5, the scope's bonus or the gun's Acc. A failure loses the aim and every aiming bonus; a critical failure also gives the sniper away (High-Tech pp. 84, 250-251).

rangedRapidStrike.Name: Ranged Rapid Strike
rangedRapidStrike.Hint: A gun of RoF 2 or more may make two attacks in one second on Attack or All-Out Attack, each at -6 (Quick-Shot buys it off) and at half the RoF. Tick the option on both attacks; the Combat tab counts the second (High-Tech pp. 85, 252).

gunTechniques.Name: Gun techniques
gunTechniques.Hint: Close-Quarters Battle on a Move and Attack at no more than Per yards (its level in place of the skill, the Bulk penalty still taken, never above the skill). Targeted Attacks with guns, named "TA (Pistol/Skull)": the skill at the target's penalty, half of it bought off, the levels taken on a shot aimed there. Instant Arsenal Disarm from its technique's row: a grab at -4, then a Quick Contest against DX or Retain Weapon to take the targeted foe's gun apart Mounted Shooting improved keeps the rough ride from a moving mount or vehicle from taking a handheld weapon's skill below the technique's level (High-Tech pp. 250-252).

firearmLoading.Name: Reloading guns
firearmLoading.Hint: How a gun loads is a field on it, worked out from its Shots column where that is reliable: loose powder down the muzzle, a black-powder breechloader, a breechloader with or without an ejector, a gate, break-open or swing-out revolver, a tube or box magazine filled round by round or by charger clip, a detachable magazine, a drum or a belt. The Reload button takes the book's time for it and what Fast-Draw (Ammo) saves: a swing-out revolver 3 seconds and 2 a round (1 a round with Fast-Draw), timed for the rounds it is asked to load, a detachable magazine 3 (2), a belt 5 (3). It offers the aids that help: a powder flask or paper cartridges (which halve the time), a greased patch, a speedloader the character carries, clamped magazines, an assistant gunner. A character who knows Double-Loading rolls it at its own level in place of Fast-Draw (Ammo). Loading in the saddle needs a roll against the lower of the weapon skill and Riding (-3 for loose powder, -1 for cartridges), and loose powder on a moving vehicle the weapon skill at -2. A muzzle-loading long arm loaded other than standing takes 1.5 times as long (High-Tech pp. 86-88, 251).

carefulLoading.Name: Careful loading
carefulLoading.Hint: A muzzle-loading musket or rifle set to load carefully takes twice as long to load, and that load shoots at +1 Acc (High-Tech p. 86).

blackPowderFouling.Name: Black-powder fouling
blackPowderFouling.Hint: The shots a black-powder gun fires are counted until it is cleaned: every five add 10% to its loading time and take 1 off Malf., every ten take 1 off Acc. Cleaning it thoroughly takes two minutes, from the gun's sheet (High-Tech p. 86).

gunslingerExpanded.Name: Expanded Gunslinger (cinematic)
gunslingerExpanded.Hint: The optional additions to Gunslinger: Bulk ignored on Move and Attack and in close combat (no Acc bonus there), which makes Close-Quarters Battle redundant, and the default penalties of Fanning, Fast-Firing, Quick-Shot, Thumbing and Two-Handed Thumbing halved (High-Tech p. 249).

shootingEnvironments.Name: Special shooting situations
shootingEnvironments.Hint: A scene the GM marks underwater: a TL6-8 gun's ranges divided by 1,000 (by 25 for a gun built to fire underwater, such as the H&K P11 and the APS), Malf. 1 less, 2 less for an automatic. A scene in space: an automatic TL6-8 gun malfunctions on 14 (not revolvers or manual repeaters). Shots into water at -4, with the water's depth counted a thousand times over against the gun's ranges; shots at 50-90 degrees into the air at 80% of the range (High-Tech pp. 85, 92, 117).

sustainedFire.Name: Sustained fire
sustainedFire.Hint: Every round fired heats the gun: past its safe number (100 for most small arms, 50 if unreliable, 150-200 if reliable; a machine gun's 800, 400 or 200 by how it is fired; changed by TL, barrel and maintenance) Acc and Malf. drop by 1, at three times it by 2 for a machine gun, and the Acc lost becomes permanent. A minute's pause lets a gun short of it start again; 15 minutes cools one past it. Water jackets take the heat until the water is gone (500 rounds a pint, 5,000 with a condenser); a barrel change takes 10 seconds and a Guns or Gunner roll, a burned hand on a critical failure (High-Tech pp. 85-86, 129-137).

firefightAftermath.Name: After the firefight
firefightAftermath.Hint: A GM tool: everyone present (the selected tokens, or the fight's combatants) is at -4 to Hearing, -5 if the shooting was indoors, and at night -2 to Vision in the dark, for (20 - HT) minutes and then until an HT roll each second succeeds. Protected Hearing and Protected Vision prevent each (High-Tech p. 87).

vitalsOnTorsoHits.Name: Body hits: the vitals
vitalsOnTorsoHits.Hint: An impaling or piercing hit on the torso rolls 1d: on a 1 it struck the vitals. Otherwise, and on the groin, injury is capped at the victim's HP where Bleeding is in play (at twice HP where it isn't), and what the cap took off still counts toward the bleeding roll's -1 per 5 HP (High-Tech p. 162).

realisticLimbWounds.Name: Realistic limb wounds
realisticLimbWounds.Hint: A limb or extremity that takes at least twice the injury that cripples it, counted before the cap, is crippled for good, with no HT roll for how long; an impaling or piercing blow must do twice that again to sever it. The GM is told (High-Tech p. 162).

vitalBleeding.Name: Stopping severe bleeding
vitalBleeding.Hint: A bleeding wound to the skull, an eye, the neck or the vitals bleeds every 30 seconds, at a further -2 for the neck or -4 for the vitals, and only Surgery (a GM tool) stops it. First Aid and that Surgery take the bleeding roll's whole penalty, the wound's size included (High-Tech p. 162).

woundFrightChecks.Name: "You shot me, Mister!"
woundFrightChecks.Hint: 4 HP or more of injury to the torso or head, or a crippled limb or eye, offers the victim a Fright Check on their next turn: at -4 for a crippling wound, and the GM may make it worse; Combat Reflexes helps as usual (High-Tech p. 162).

airGunsAndStunners.Name: Air guns and ranged stunners
airGunsAndStunners.Hint: An air gun's charge is good for the shots its description gives and must be replaced when spent; the Girandoni loses damage and range after its 10th and 20th shots. A ranged stunner's victim who fails the HT roll is stunned while the trigger is held and (20 - HT) seconds after (at least 1), then rolls to recover at the shock's penalty; an EMD stunner knocks the victim down (High-Tech pp. 88-90).

revolverHandling.Name: Revolver handling and pistol whipping
revolverHandling.Hint: A TL5 revolver without a safety is carried with the hammer on an empty chamber, a round short, unless its owner carries it fully loaded and risks an accidental discharge. Any handgun can pistol whip with Brawling or DX at thrust-1 crushing plus the absolute value of its Bulk; pistols made for braining swing with Axe/Mace at swing+1. Suppressors don't work on ordinary revolvers (High-Tech pp. 90, 93, 159).

mechanicalMachineGuns.Name: Mechanical machine guns
mechanicalMachineGuns.Hint: A hand-cranked or lever-worked machine gun is at -5 for unfamiliarity rather than -2, at a further -1 to fix a malfunction for one who hasn't used the model, and at -8 fired off its mount (High-Tech p. 127).

backblast.Name: Backblast
backblast.Hint: Firing a light antitank weapon, recoilless rifle or missile throws its backblast into a 60-degree cone behind it: burning damage in full to 2 yards a die and half to 6 yards a die, or a countermass weapon's crushing damage to 2 yards a die. Fired indoors, a burning backblast reflects at the firer, and a firer without hearing protection rolls HT-4 or is stunned (High-Tech pp. 141, 147-153).

indirectFire.Name: Indirect fire and forward observers
indirectFire.Hint: A gun's row runs a fire mission: observed fire, where the forward observer's Navigation roll (+1 compass, +3 GPS, -10 without a map) and Forward Observer roll (-3 per 500 yards after magnification and a rangefinder, Vision modifiers, a fire-control computer) set the first shot's -10, each correction after a shot is another roll and 2d+5 seconds, and the gun attacks without Acc; or predicted fire on an area off a map. The card gives the time of flight and the scatter of a miss, squared for a target the gunner can't see (High-Tech pp. 139-141).

gunMagazines.Name: Gun magazines
gunMagazines.Hint: Extended, high-density and drum magazines worked out on the gun: capacity, weight and cost from the calibre's weight per shot, -1 Bulk past 1.5 (extended) or 3 (drum) times the normal capacity, and -1 Malf. for a drum or where the GM marks one unreliable; no high-density magazine in a pistol's grip (High-Tech p. 155).

gunSights.Name: Sights and aiming aids
gunSights.Hint: Scopes, night, thermal and computer sights, reflex sights, targeting lasers and tactical lights fitted to a gun: the best magnifying sight is the gun's scope on its rows (a fixed-power one gives its bonus only after as many seconds of Aim), and the combined bonus of all a gun's sights can't exceed its base Acc; a scope over 4x is -1 Bulk unaimed. Darkness penalties lose a point to a TL7+ scope on an aimed shot (two with an illuminated reticle), a point to improved-visibility sights, three to a reflex sight; a tactical light switched on for the shot leaves no worse than -3 within its beam. A targeting laser reaches as far as its colour does in daylight or low light, an infrared dot only for a shooter with Night Vision, Infravision or Hyperspectral Vision, and a reflex sight gives nothing while the laser is on. Looking through a night, thermal or computer sight gives its vision but leaves the shooter colorblind with tunnel vision. A targeting laser's colour prices it (High-Tech pp. 155-157).

suppressors.Name: Sound suppressors
suppressors.Hint: Suppressors fitted to a gun that takes one (never an ordinary revolver), bought by the -1 Hearing: their Bulk, a wiper suppressor's lost damage and range for its 40 shots, home-built grades, and a Hearing roll against the shot from the Hearing Distance Table (High-Tech pp. 158-159).

cinematicSilencers.Name: Silencers (cinematic)
cinematicSilencers.Hint: Suppressors near-silence the shot: their Hearing penalty is doubled, or tripled, on the roll to hear it (High-Tech p. 159).

stocksAndMounts.Name: Stocks, bipods and mounts
stocksAndMounts.Hint: A pistol stock (Guns (Rifle), +1 Acc, -1 Bulk, ST x0.8); a folding stock folded from the gun's row (Bulk a step better, -1 Acc, +1 Recoil, ST x1.2); a bipod opened from the row, bracing a prone shooter at two-thirds the ST; shooting sticks bracing a sitting one. A gun whose record keeps "Folded Stock" or "w/ Bipod" modes fires the one its state picks (High-Tech p. 160).

zenMarksmanship.Name: Zen Marksmanship (cinematic)
zenMarksmanship.Hint: Zen Archery for guns: a character who knows Zen Marksmanship (Pistol), (Rifle), (Shotgun), (Submachine Gun), (Musket) or (Gyroc), or (Beam Pistol) or (Beam Rifle), rolls it from the maneuver panel after concentrating, and a success takes two-thirds of the size and range penalties off the next shot with that Guns or Beam Weapons specialty (High-Tech p. 250).

ammunitionUpgrades.Name: Ammunition upgrades
ammunitionUpgrades.Hint: Each mode of a gun, and each box of rounds, holds a load: field-expedient shot, paper cartridges, light cases, extra-powerful, match-grade, subsonic or silent rounds, which change the row's Acc, Dmg, Range, ST and Malf. and how the shot is heard. A box's cost and weight per round come from the Ammunition Tables for its calibre, times the upgrades, less 5% for 500 rounds (15% for 5,000) and what an Area Knowledge roll finds. A caplock can be converted to fire cartridges (High-Tech pp. 161-165, 175-177).

handloading.Name: Handloading and reloading
handloading.Hint: Rounds handloaded cost their materials, the round's CPS; reloads half of it. A batch takes the tools' time, with an Armoury (Small Arms) roll every hour or half-hour (+2 for reloads); a critical success takes a quarter off a batch of reloads, a critical failure costs it a point of Malf. A load developed for a gun on Armoury and IQ-based Guns rolls makes its match-grade handloads a perfect match: Acc x1.5, up to +2 (High-Tech p. 174).

misloading.Name: Misloading
misloading.Hint: A round that isn't the gun's own, nor a shorter one down its chain of interchangeable calibres (for a revolver or manual repeater), rolls the Misloading Table when fired: it may fire at Acc 0, jam, misfire, damage the gun or burst it (High-Tech p. 178).

projectileOptions.Name: Projectile Options
projectileOptions.Hint: Each ranged mode (and each box of rounds) can load a projectile in place of the solid bullet: rifled slugs, hollow-points, poison, AP, APHC, frangible, APDS, APFSDS, baton, beanbag, SAPFSDS, underwater darts, the depleted-uranium rounds and Minié balls. The row's damage, type, divisor, range, Acc and Malf. follow, a shotgun working from its slug's figures, and the price takes the projectile's multiple. It replaces the Basic Set round chosen on the mode (High-Tech pp. 86, 109, 166-169).

exoticBullets.Name: Exotic Bullets
exoticBullets.Hint: A load's bullets can be silver (x50 cost; -1 Acc and Malf. in a rifled gun unless jacketed hollow-points; -3 to handload), another dense metal, a light material (half damage and range) or a very light one (a tenth) (High-Tech p. 168).

multipleProjectileLoads.Name: Multiple-Projectile Loads
multipleProjectileLoads.Hint: Canister, shotshells by shot size, buck-and-ball (its first hit is the ball), shrapnel, duplex and triplex, beehive, multi-flechette, rubber shot and ABF: the count of projectiles sets the damage by the NS table and the RoF multiple, their size the range and shot's damage type, and every gun fires them at Rcl 1 (High-Tech pp. 172-174).

projectileUpgrades.Name: Projectile Upgrades
projectileUpgrades.Hint: Airburst (a miss scatters by the margin squared; +3 or +4 to hit an area), incendiary, self-destruct and tracer (incendiary out to 1/2D), each x1.5 cost (High-Tech pp. 174-175).

explosiveProjectiles.Name: Explosive Rounds
explosiveProjectiles.Hint: LE, SAPLE, APEX, HE, SAPHE, SAPHEC, APHEX, EFP, HEAT, HEDP, HESH, MS-HEAT and thermobaric rounds on a mode whose record prints the blast: the shot's divisor, the blast linked or following, bursting inside, fragments or none, incendiary; early SAPLE duds, HESH spall, MS-HEAT against reactive armour, thermobaric blasts divided by twice the distance, and airburst HE doing only its fragments (High-Tech pp. 169-170, 175).

cargoProjectiles.Name: Cargo Rounds
cargoProjectiles.Hint: Illumination and signal flares that lift the darkness penalty under them, five kinds of smoke, tear gas (with or without a vomiting agent) and its resistance rolls, liquid rounds and scent markers, poison gas dosing a Basic Set poison, and white phosphorus's burning fragments and smoke; the cloud or light is left where the round lands (High-Tech pp. 143, 171-172).

batteries.Name: Batteries, generators and fuel
batteries.Hint: Gear that runs on batteries (T to VL) tracks what is left of its endurance on the Inventory tab. Batteries may be rechargeable, at five times the price, and are recharged rather than bought again; throwaway ones are taken from the spare batteries carried. A gadget may take batteries of another size or number, its endurance in proportion to their weight and its weight changed by the difference. A power adapter (the cost and weight of the usual batteries) lets it run on external power; an inverter (the cost and weight of its batteries, M or larger) lets gear built for external power run on batteries. Generators and collectors carried are listed with their fuel: a tank's hours, refilled from the fuel carried; cranking a muscle-powered generator costs 1 FP an hour and recharges about 10 lbs. of batteries an hour; a solar collector gives nothing at a -1 Vision penalty or worse; the TL8 portable gasoline generator weighs 2/3 as much (High-Tech pp. 10, 13-16).

booksAndLibraries.Name: Books and libraries
booksAndLibraries.Hint: A manual or reference work, marked on its item sheet with the skill it covers, gets a row button that rolls the skill at its attribute default (Easy -4 to Very Hard -7), even for a character with no default, with extra time's bonus capped at that penalty. A library is Research equipment by its grade (a small collection is improvised, -2), costs 100 times as much on an occult subject, and at the GM's option a good or fine library's bonus also counts for the skill it covers (High-Tech pp. 17-18).

computerSystems.Name: Computers and software
computerSystems.Hint: The TL8 computer models with their Complexity and storage, the options (compact, hardened, high-capacity, fast, slow) and, for a TL6-7 computer, one early technology (mechanical -5, vacuum tube -4 and hardened, transistor -3), repricing the computer. A program is priced from the Program Cost Table by Complexity and TL where its record has no price; a software tool shows the grade its Complexity reaches, and whether it is too simple for the skill at all. A worn head-up display gives +1 to Driving and Piloting (High-Tech pp. 19-22).

toolKits.Name: Tool kits and workshops
toolKits.Hint: A portable kit carried for another specialty of the same skill is -2; a workshop is -2 for another specialty or a close craft and -5 for a distant one, where no kit of the skill's own is carried. Kits for light crafts cost a quarter and weigh a tenth; a vehicle kit or shop for more than 10 tons costs and weighs (tons)/10 times as much. Labs show their set-up time, machine shops their output (High-Tech pp. 24, 29, 50).

forcedEntryTools.Name: Forced-entry tools
forcedEntryTools.Hint: Saws, drills, cutters and torches get a Forced Entry row with the damage they do each second (or each use) and what they work on; the rock drill and lock buster pass on a maul's blow. The hand ram (below ST 20), door opener and spreader/cutter need their Ready maneuvers before each use; the glass cutter and duct tape are row actions (High-Tech pp. 25-30).

chainsaws.Name: Chainsaws and nail guns
chainsaws.Hint: A chainsaw gets Forced Entry rows for rescue work, one at (0.5) against concrete or metal; a blow from it that fails to penetrate rolls 1d to stall (3-5) or snap (6) the saw, refusing its attacks until restarted or repaired. A carbide chain costs double and ends both. A nail gun fires at Guns (Pistol)-4, or DX-4 (High-Tech pp. 27-28).

householdHazards.Name: Household hazards
householdHazards.Hint: A row action rolls what a ruptured propane cylinder (a burning explosion with 1d cutting fragments), a hot stove, a blender, hot coffee, a hotplate, toaster or waffle iron, or an institutional microwave does. Lead is a poison the sheet doses; past half the victim's HP the worse symptoms are named (High-Tech pp. 31-33).

flamethrowers.Name: Flamethrowers
flamethrowers.Hint: A flamethrower's jet is a large-area injury and can set the victim's clothes alight; worn DR protects at a fifth unless the victim is sealed. The fuel then burns on the victim for 2d x 5 seconds (1d x 5 past 1/2D), 1d burn each second on their turn against the same fifth of their DR, until it burns out or the GM takes the condition off. Played over an area up to three yards wide as an All-Out Attack, each target is rolled for separately and damage and burning time are divided by the width. Unthickened fuel halves a TL7+ flamethrower's Range. A malfunction rolls the flamethrower's own table: no ignition (3-5), no fuel (6-17) or an explosion (18) that deals a second's damage to everything within two yards; clearing takes 10 seconds and an Armoury or IQ-based Liquid Projector roll, a critical failure an explosion. A shot at the weapon is at no penalty (-4 at a backpack model whose carrier faces the shooter) and meets DR 2; damage through it blows the tank up on a 1 on 1d and disables it otherwise (High-Tech pp. 178-179).

sprayGuns.Name: Spray guns and aerosols
sprayGuns.Hint: A spray must hit the face, but the wide jet gives +2 to hit it. Tear gas and pepper spray force two HT rolls at the spray's penalty, one against coughing and one against blindness; tear gas's last minutes equal to the margin of failure, pepper spray's until washed off with plenty of water (High-Tech p. 180).

laserDazzlers.Name: Laser dazzlers and blinding lasers
laserDazzlers.Hint: Only those looking toward the laser are affected, and DR has no effect. Protected Vision gives +5 to resist, a Nictitating Membrane +1 a level, and anti-laser goggles both (Nictitating Membrane 4); past 1/2D the roll is at +3. A dazzler blinds for minutes equal to the margin of failure; a blinding laser cripples the eyes, for good on a failure by 10 or more (High-Tech pp. 71, 181).

explosionSideEffects.Name: Side effects of explosions
explosionSideEffects.Hint: A blast in a sealed room or vehicle does double damage to everyone inside, 1.5 times with doors and windows to blow out (an attack option on an explosive row, and a setting on a charge). Anyone a blast's crushing damage reaches rolls HT against concussion, at -1 per 5 points through DR (+1 earplugs, +5 Protected Hearing or earmuffs); anyone looking toward it whom its crushing or burning damage reaches rolls HT against the flash, at -1 per 10 points received (+1 sunglasses, +3 welding goggles, +5 Protected Vision). Failure costs Hearing or Vision equal to the margin, the whole sense by 10 or more, for (20 - HT) minutes (two seconds with the sense protected), and stuns (High-Tech pp. 181-182).

demolitionCharges.Name: Demolition charges
demolitionCharges.Hint: The book's Relative Explosive Force Table joins the Demolition tool's list. An explosive record gets a row action that sets it off (its pounds, packed against a door or wall or set nearby, a shaped charge dividing the structure's DR by 10), and one that works out the charge a job takes -- a crater, timbers, girders, a hole in a wall or a plate -- by the explosive's REF, halved when tamped or shaped, and rolls Explosives (Demolition) for it: at TL6 a shaped charge takes rolls at -4 and -5 (High-Tech pp. 182-183).

unstableExplosives.Name: Unstable and home-made explosives
unstableExplosives.Hint: Nitroglycerin that is jolted -- a row action, or any blow to whoever carries it -- goes off on 12+ on 3d; set a number on an item for impure nitro or sweating dynamite. Skimming nitro from dynamite takes Chemistry-2 or Explosives (Demolition)-2: failure by 1 ruins it, by 2 blows half of it up, by more all of it. A row action cooks black powder, plastique, ANFO or a fuel-air device from the book's rolls; a failed batch is inert, or for plastique unstable, weak, smelly or inert; home-made ANFO needs Explosives (Demolition)+2 to set off. A fuel-air blast is divided by 2 x the distance, not 3 x (High-Tech pp. 184-187).

incendiaryAgents.Name: Incendiaries
incendiaryAgents.Hint: Thermite (a row action) burns on a victim at 3d a second against the DR where it lies, every 10 points taking 1 off that DR, for 25 seconds a pound; on an object it is worked out second by second against DR and HP. Its sparks do 3 a second within a yard and 1 at two yards. A hit from napalm clings and burns for a minute at 1d-1 a second against large-area DR; only immersion or burial puts it out, so take the condition off when it is (High-Tech p. 188).

radios.Name: Radios and telegraphy
radios.Hint: A radio's range by size and TL on its sheet (large, medium, small, tiny), and a GM tool for whether two characters' radios reach each other: the shorter range times 3, 10 or 30 as the other radio is one to three sizes larger, a tenth in a city or underground and again for live video, 2, 10 or 100 times for slowed data, and Electronics Operation (Communications) at -1 per 10% to stretch it to double. Radio options priced (code-only x0.5, direction finder x5, intercept x5, radiotelephone x1.5, receive-only 10% cost and 20% weight, ECCM x2, GPS x2, satellite uplink x2 on medium and large, a long antenna doubling range for a quarter more); a transmitting radio is detected at twice its range, 1.5 times with ECCM. Row buttons for a direction finder's Quick Contest (a margin of 5 gives an exact fix), an intercept, and telegraphy: sending or reading, recognizing a fist, faking one at -6, tapping a line (a Quick Contest from TL6), all at -4 when enciphered. The pocket laser communicator's two beams and the military diver communicator (High-Tech pp. 36-40).

activeSensors.Name: Active sensors
activeSensors.Hint: Sonar, radar, ground-penetrating and thru-wall radar with their range at their TL (radar doubled at TL8, at half the weight) and the skill each uses; tactical, LPI and imaging modes priced at x5 (imaging sonar twice the weight, a tenth the range). A sensor sweep GM tool: -2 per doubling past range, nothing outside the 120-degree arc, sonar's ambient noise (-1 to -6), a GPR's range twenty times in ice and a tenth in rock, and a Quick Contest against a jammer's operator (Electronics Operation (EW)) or an infiltrator's Stealth. Emissions are detected at twice the range, 1.5 times the halved range with LPI. A tactical sonar or radar locks on with an Aim for +3 to aimed ranged attacks at the target, on top of any targeting software (High-Tech pp. 45-47).

visualSensors.Name: Optics, night vision and thermographs
visualSensors.Hint: Worn optics give Telescopic Vision, a level per doubling of magnification (the system's Vision rolls and Aim use it). Night-vision optics give their Night Vision, two levels more while an IR source lights the scene (the earliest binoculars work only then); thermographs give Infravision, +2 to Vision to spot a warm target and +3 to Tracking. While in use, both impose Colorblindness, No Depth Perception and No Peripheral Vision. Coated military binoculars give Protected Vision. A worn IR illuminator makes its wearer a light to night-vision gear and thermographs: +4 to spot them. A row button rolls Stealth against lens shine, +4 with a hood (High-Tech pp. 47-48).

passiveSensors.Name: Hydrophones and sound detectors
passiveSensors.Hint: A hydrophone's row button rolls Electronics Operation (Sonar) with its bonus (+4 large, +2 medium, +2 per TL after its introduction), the target's size and speed and the range and current's penalties from the Size and Speed/Range Table; success fixes the target, +3 to hit it with an aimed attack (not a search hydrophone, a tenth the price) and +4 to shadow it. Sound-detection gear gives +4 to identify a sound, or rolls to locate one by miles and decibels with the ambient noise. A worn directional microphone is Parabolic Hearing 2 (TL7) or 3 (TL8) (High-Tech pp. 48-50).

survivalGear.Name: Survival and camping gear
survivalGear.Hint: A "Camping out" box on the Inventory tab: while it's ticked, the cold roll takes the best shelter or sleeping gear carried (blanket -2, emergency blanket -1, sleeping bag 0, +1 at TL8, tarp and tents +1, dome tent +2, heavy sleeping bag +3), its quality added, or -5 with none. A fire starter's row button rolls DX-based Survival at +5 to +10. A spring trap's button strikes the targeted character for thrust+2 crushing at the trap's ST, and its card rolls the Quick Contest of ST to break free. A survival kit carried for another environment is -1 (a similar one), -2 (a very different one) or -3 (land for water, or Urban Survival) as the Survival roll's equipment line, where no kit for the roll's own specialty is carried. A water filter in use gives +(TL-2) to HT against a digestive disease. The hand-pumped desalinator's button costs 1 FP for a cup (the large model a quart, at three times the cost and weight); the solar still's rolls Survival for a quart a day. A rescue signal in use gives +2 to a Vision roll to spot its user. Fishing and trapping gear notes the five foraging rolls a day (High-Tech pp. 56-59).

maritimeGear.Name: Life jackets, swim fins and dye markers
maritimeGear.Hint: A life jacket worn gives +6 to Swimming rolls and -3 in a Quick Contest of Swimming; a cork one (TL5) notes -3 on entering the water. Swim fins worn take Move on land down to 2. A dye marker's row button releases it: +2 to Vision rolls to spot its user for half an hour (High-Tech pp. 59-60).

parachuting.Name: Parachutes and Death from Above
parachuting.Hint: A parachute's row button makes a jump: the Parachuting roll, the canopy open 80 yards after the ripcord (40 for the mini-parachute), a jumper who hits the ground first landing at half the fall's velocity, 5 yards a second once open plus 1 per 50 lbs. over the chute's rated weight (150, 200 at TL7 and 250 at TL8 for the round chute), a chute that fails at 120% of it, and HT-4 against nausea with the earliest chutes. The card rolls the landing's collision damage for the GM to apply. Death from Above: an attack option on a ranged attack made on Move and Attack by someone with a parachute, at the lower of Parachuting and the weapon's skill (High-Tech p. 61).

rations.Name: Snacks and sports drinks
rations.Hint: A snack or sports drink's row button eats one, taking it off the count: it counts as a decent meal on the next rest (+1 FP, the Rest dialog's meal box), and a sports drink as a quart of water for the day's rations (High-Tech p. 35).

grenadeHandling.Name: Hand grenades
grenadeHandling.Hint: A TL6-8 grenade is primed before use (10 seconds each; a TL5 grenade's fuse takes five Readies to fit), then armed with a Ready (two for a stick grenade) before it is thrown. A pin grenade's fuse starts when the handle flies off: cook it off on the sheet, and the throw says how long is left and whether anyone has time to throw it back; one held too long goes off in the hand, and a critical failure drops it. Also booby traps (Soldier or Traps+4), improvised grenades, a Molotov through an engine grating, smoke and WP clouds, WP's burning fragments, the AN-M14 as thermite, and flashbangs resisted at +5 for each of Protected Hearing and Vision, their stun recovered at HT-5 (High-Tech pp. 190-193).

landMines.Name: Land mines
landMines.Hint: Placing a mine (Explosives (Demolition)+4, Soldier or Traps+2; improvised, Explosives (Demolition)-2), probing for one (Explosives (EOD) or Soldier-5) and disarming it (Explosives (EOD); the TMi35's anti-lifting fuse at -2, any failure setting it off). A bounding mine's fragments are rolled on their own card, and whoever is flat on the ground takes none. A Claymore attacks everyone targeted at skill 9 plus its rapid-fire bonus, less range, nearest first, until its 700 pellets are spent (High-Tech pp. 189-190).

rifleGrenades.Name: Rifle grenades
rifleGrenades.Hint: A rifle grenade is fired only once it is on a rifle: 5 seconds to fit a spigot or cup launcher, 3 to load the blank, 2 to put the grenade on. The rifle can't fire normally with the launcher on, and the grenade's Bulk is added to the rifle's. Inside its minimum range it doesn't arm: fire the dud row, 1d+1 crushing and no blast, as for one that fails to go off (High-Tech pp. 193-194).

nuclearEffects.Name: Nuclear weapons
nuclearEffects.Hint: A nuclear blast's burning is divided by twice the distance, and its flash always calls for the HT roll. EMP (a row action) is an HT-8(2) affliction on the Electrical and the electronics the targets carry: what fails is out until repaired, at -10 for solid-state gear and -4 for older devices. Fallout (a row action) gives the footprint for the yield and doses the targets with the rads for their hours in it: 100 an hour at first, 10 after two days, 1 after two weeks (High-Tech pp. 195-196).

lightSources.Name: Light sources
lightSources.Hint: A row action lights a light or puts it out (a lantern takes 30-60 seconds; a flashlight a Ready maneuver), and another sets a lit lantern or candle down as an area on the map; dropped on hard ground, a fuel lantern rolls against HT 6 or breaks (a glass lantern starting a 1-yard fire, a kerosene one dousing itself). An attack at a target a light reaches (one set down round it, one carried within its radius, or the attacker's own beam out to its length) is no darker than a lit spot, -3 before Night Vision. A tactical light shone in the eyes asks each target for HT-4 against 10 seconds' blindness per point of failure (High-Tech pp. 51-52).

navigationGear.Name: Navigation instruments and maps
navigationGear.Hint: The best of a compass (+1 Navigation), marine chronometer (+1 Navigation (Sea); +3 with navigating instruments), navigating instruments (+2 Navigation (Sea), +3 at TL6+), surveying instruments (+2 Mathematics (Surveying) or Navigation (Land)) or a GPS receiver in sight of its satellites (+3 Navigation), as a line on the skill; they don't add. A map is basic equipment for Navigation and Forward Observer: an inaccurate one is -1 to -5, none at all -10 (High-Tech pp. 52-53).

loadBearingEquipment.Name: Load-bearing gear and packs
loadBearingEquipment.Hint: A Soldier or IQ-based Hiking roll sets up LBE or fits a pack. Set-up LBE adds its quality (-2 if set up badly) to Fast-Draw from pouches and to a row action's DX roll to reach gear; a fitted pack of quality adds it to Hiking, and a badly fitted one gives moderate pain after a day's hiking. TL8 packs weigh half and backpacks cost double. The item shows an hour's march at Move/2 mph (High-Tech pp. 53-55).

climbingGear.Name: Climbing gear
climbingGear.Hint: A roped climber falls at most twice the distance past the last fastener; shooting while rappelling is -4 (-2 with a Sure-Footed perk); a grapnel is thrown at DX-3 or Throwing to ST x 2 yards; snowshoes are -1 Move while worn, except TL8 ones (High-Tech pp. 55-56).

clothingAndWeather.Name: Clothing against the weather
clothingAndWeather.Hint: The Weather dialog starts on the clothing class of what the character wears: summer, ordinary, formal and high-fashion clothes (and outfits made on them) as light clothing, winter clothes as winter clothing, arctic clothes as arctic clothing, or as winter or ordinary clothes with layers taken off. A worn winter or arctic outfit is -1 on the cold roll for each piece left off (boots, gloves, hat, scarf), ticked on the outfit's sheet. A worn wicking undergarment gives +1 on the heat roll. Fur winter or arctic clothes, ticked on the sheet, give DR 1 wherever they cover. An outfit's weight follows its TL: x2 at TL5-6, x0.5 at TL8 (arctic clothes x1.5, x1.25 and x0.5) (High-Tech pp. 63-65).

frostbite.Name: Frostbite
frostbite.Hint: At the GM's option: whenever the cold costs FP, a damage card for each exposed hit location, a point of injury per FP lost, through no DR, so it can cripple a hand or foot. Light clothing leaves the head, face, neck, hands and feet exposed; winter or arctic clothing only where a piece is left off (a hat the skull, a scarf the neck and face, gloves the hands, boots the feet); a heated suit nothing (High-Tech p. 63).

climateControl.Name: Climate-controlled clothing
climateControl.Hint: Worn heated clothing adds 60 degrees to the cold end of the comfort zone, a climate-control system 60 to both ends, a cooling vest 30 to the hot end, as Temperature Tolerance the cold and heat rolls read; the powered ones only while their cells last.
