Heated clothing counts as winter clothes with or without power. While gear that widens the hot end is worn, a hike in the heat costs no extra FP an hour (High-Tech p. 74).

bayonets.Name: Bayonets, rifle butts and combination weapons
bayonets.Hint: A gun that carries a bayonet adds its weight and price. Fixing it takes four Ready maneuvers, counted by the gun's row button (three after a successful Fast-Draw (Knife) on the first). Fixed, the gun gets a melee row -- Spear, thrust+3 impaling, Reach 1, 2* at TL4-6 and 1 at TL7-8 on a shoulder arm; a large knife's rows with Knife on a sidearm -- -1 on its Guns rows and a muzzleloader's reload a tenth longer; an unfamiliar gun and bayonet is -2 as an attack option. Every shoulder arm without melee rows gets its butt (Staff, thrust+2 crushing) and a swing by the barrel (Two-Handed Axe/Mace, swing+3 crushing), the swing noted where the gun isn't a TL4-5 single-shot built for it. The spiked tomahawk's spike is noted as a pick; the NRS-2 scout knife is turned round by a row button to shoot, and can't stab while it is (High-Tech pp. 196-199).

sheaths.Name: Sheaths apart from their blades
sheaths.Hint: A knife or sword's item sheet picks its sheath: rigid (the table's weight, a third of it the sheath), flexible or none (the blade alone, two thirds of the weight; -1 or -2 on HT rolls against corrosion and incidental damage). A rigid sheath of a pound or more is a baton, as two derived Shortsword rows at cheap quality for breakage. The sheet shows what a replacement sheath costs (High-Tech p. 198).

bladeComposition.Name: Blade composition and sword canes
bladeComposition.Hint: A knife, sword or axe (thrown ones too) can be stainless, ceramic or titanium, a field on its item sheet that reprices it: ceramic triple cost and half weight, breaking as cheap; titanium double cost and three quarters of the weight, breaking as very fine; stainless at no extra cost, but a stainless sword is priced from list by its grade -- list buys cheap at TL6 and good at TL7-8, and each of the two grades above costs 8 and 40 times list. A sword cane's thin blade is a grade lower than paid for, in its damage and its breakage (High-Tech pp. 196-198, 201).

stunWeapons.Name: Electric stun weapons
stunWeapons.Hint: The stun gun, stun baton and cattle prod: the seconds the weapon is held in contact are an attack option, and a victim who fails the HT-3 roll is stunned with no recovery roll for those seconds and (20 - HT) more (at least one), then rolls HT-3 each second to recover. The victim's armour is on the roll to resist, +2 a point of DR, metallic armour counting as DR 1 (High-Tech p. 199; Campaigns p. 432).

highTechBows.Name: High-tech bows, slingshots and spearguns
highTechBows.Hint: A bow or crossbow (not a composite bow) can be built compound on its item sheet: double cost, damage and range as if two ST stronger. A bow can take sights and stabilizers (+$100, +1 Acc for a user who knows the skill; -1 as an attack option for one unfamiliar with them) and string silencers ($1, -2 to hear it). A slingshot fires stones or lead and steel shot (+1 damage, double range). A speargun's range is a tenth in a scene set underwater, and its spear is on 10 yards of line (High-Tech p. 201).

camouflageGear.Name: Camouflage and scent masking
camouflageGear.Hint: The Gear tab says the terrain a character is hiding in and who is looking. The worn pattern worth most there is the Camouflage skill's equipment line: simple +1 anywhere; basic +2 in matching terrain, -1 elsewhere and -2 in contrasting terrain; advanced +3, and -2 elsewhere; a ghillie suit +3, -1 and -2, more once customised (to +8). From TL7, +1 against technological night vision or infravision; infrared suppression (the poncho, the IR net, a ghillie suit with it) +2 against infravision. In a Quick Contest, the other side's worn night-vision gear or thermograph counts in place of the Gear tab's choice. A reversible piece turns inside out from its row; a net's row button hides gear on the deployer's Camouflage. Scent masking worn is -4 to Tracking to follow the wearer. Patterns and scent masking on other clothing reprice it (High-Tech pp. 76-77).

breathingGear.Name: Breathing gear
breathingGear.Hint: Gas masks give Filter Lungs; every mask and diving rig gives No Sense of Smell/Taste and No Peripheral Vision (Tunnel Vision for the TL5 gas mask and hard-hat dress) and keeps tear gas out; SCBA and scuba masks give Doesn't Breathe while a tank feeds them, rebreathers while their gas lasts; a tank's air by TL, divided by the depth's pressure, a minute less for every FP spent and every failed Fright Check (High-Tech pp. 72-74, 76).

environmentSuits.Name: Environment suits
environmentSuits.Hint: Biohazard and NBC suits are Sealed with an air mask under them, and a biohazard suit triples the FP of effort and weather; a clean suit gives +4 HT against contagion; the Apollo space suits are Sealed with Vacuum Support under their helmets and breathe from a tank or the EVA suit's 7-hour pack; biomedical sensors give +1 to Diagnosis (High-Tech pp. 74-76).

locksAndSafes.Name: Locks and safes
locksAndSafes.Hint: A lock's quality reprices it (basic x1, good x5, fine x20) and sets the roll to pick it (+5, 0, -5); a lock's toughness and a safe's DR and HP; picking takes a minute, a safe an hour, with Time Spent; a lockpick gun is +4 against basic locks and -5 against the rest; a stethoscope or endoscope is +2; an older lock gives the burglar the Tech-Level Modifiers' penalty as a bonus; electronic locks and identity verifiers take Electronics Operation (Security) (High-Tech pp. 202-205, 213).

trapsAndBarriers.Name: Traps and barriers
trapsAndBarriers.Hint: A GM tool for caltrops (a Vision roll at the Move's speed penalty, thrust-3 impaling to the foot per caltrop stepped on), tripwires, stake pits, barbed and razor wire (DX-5 a yard, a Will roll not to cry out, snagged as a Binding ST 8), a cattle fence's stun held while in contact, a lethal fence's 3d a second and the electromagnetic car stopper; spike strips and smart fences on the item (High-Tech pp. 203-205).

emergencyMedicine.Name: Emergency medicine
emergencyMedicine.Hint: A manual defibrillator's row button rolls Electronics Operation (Medical), then the resuscitation roll at +2 (TL7) or +3 (TL8); an AED's rolls IQ+4 to hook it up, then resuscitates at its own skill of 12. CPR given with either, or from the GM's "Give CPR" tool (the selected character on the targeted one), costs the rescuer 1 FP per five minutes. First aid gear gives +1 at best unless the healer has blood or IV fluids and an IV kit (a crash kit carries its own until depleted); a first aid kit marked depleted works a grade lower. Hemostatic bandages give +1 (quality) to First Aid on a bleeding patient, a bandage used. A bag of IV fluid's button starts an IV (an IV kit needed): a quart of water, and dextrose a meal too (High-Tech pp. 219-221).

medicalFacilities.Name: Medical facilities
medicalFacilities.Hint: An imaging instrument's row button rolls Electronics Operation (Medical), then Diagnosis with its bonus (the TL6 X-ray machine giving patient and operator 1d rads). Portable surgery gives +2 to First Aid. On an operation, a surgical kit's own TL modifier (-2 at TL5 to +2 at TL8) stands in for the Basic Set table's by the surgeon's TL, and a suturing kit is improvised (-5). A chloroform mask's button rolls Physician to put the targeted patient under (a portable anaesthesia machine at +2); if it failed, the operation is at -2. Antiseptic cleans the targeted patient's wound: +2 on the next infection roll (High-Tech pp. 222-225).

encryption.Name: Encryption and code-breaking
encryption.Hint: "Break a code" on the Cryptography skill's row, a code-breaking program's row, or the GM's token controls for the selected character. An ad-libbed code is a Quick Contest of IQ-5 (either side may use Cryptography) with its maker: the targeted character, or a level given. A TL5-6 system such as a cipher wheel's is the Basic Set's Quick Contest of Cryptography, which only Cryptography may attempt. By hand at TL5-6, each other selected character with Cryptography 17+ gives the leader +1 (at most +4). The encryption standards are a Cryptography roll with Time Spent against their base time (TL6 basic: 10 years, or a year with Complexity 2 apparatus; TL7 basic: a week on a Complexity 3 computer; TL8 basic: a day on Complexity 5) and the code-breaking program carried, whose grade gives its bonus; secure encryption can't be broken before TL9 (High-Tech pp. 210-211; Characters p. 186).

disguiseAndSmuggling.Name: Forgery, disguise and smuggling
disguiseAndSmuggling.Hint: Forgery and counterfeiting tools forge from their row: a TL7+ document needs a computer and printer too (-5 without, as improvised equipment), fake credit cards a card printer and magnetic strip decoder/encoder, and a TL8 counterfeiter must avoid a printer that marks its pages. The Disguise skill's row rolls an improvised disguise at -5 in place of any kit; a disguise kit's row rolls Disguise with it, the advanced kit (+2) needing a day to prepare and two to six hours of fitting. Smuggler's luggage (+2) rolls Smuggling for what its secret area holds, a tenth of its capacity. A mule's row rolls HT at -1 per 50 pellets carried: failure is an incident, a critical failure bursts a packet, a dose of the Basic Set's overdose. The GM's token controls screen the targeted character: a Quick Contest of Search or Observation against Acting, or an X-ray machine's Electronics Operation roll and then Search (High-Tech pp. 213-215).

partialCoverage.Name: Partial armour coverage
partialCoverage.Hint: A piece that covers n in 6 of a location (shin guards, limb armour, a DAP, shoulder pads) protects when 1d comes up n or less, the n of several pieces there added up. An attacker may strike around it at -(n-1), never better than -1, and the blow passes it. A steel toe box gives its DR on 2 in 6 hits to the foot, high boots with the tops turned up cover 3 in 6 of the legs, and the TL7 fragmentation vest's vitals and the bomb disposal suit's torso are better armoured from the front (High-Tech pp. 66-69, 75).

concealedArmor.Name: Concealing armour
concealedArmor.Hint: Hiding worn armour from someone looking for it is a Quick Contest of Holdout against their Search at the range penalty: Holdout is at -DR for rigid armour and -DR/3 (rounded up) for flexible, with up to +4 back for a design made to be concealed. A worn long coat or poncho gives +4 to Holdout and undercover clothing +1 or +2 (High-Tech pp. 64, 66).

armorMaterials.Name: Armour materials
armorMaterials.Hint: Low-tech armour and shields remade in TL5+ steel have twice the DR, or keep it at half the cost and weight; smart foam is cloth armour at ten times the cost, DR 4 against crushing and 1 against the rest; titanium keeps the DR at a third of the weight and five times the cost. Trauma plates are semi-ablative: every 10 points of basic damage rolled take a point of their DR until the plate is replaced (High-Tech pp. 65, 67).

securityScreening.Name: Security screening and security systems
securityScreening.Hint: A metal detector's, baggage screener's, CT scanner's or portable X-ray's row button: the operator's Electronics Operation (Security) roll claims the gear's bonus (handheld metal detector +1 to Search, Traps and Explosives (EOD) for metal, +2 to Search with a pat-down; walkthrough +1 to +3; X-ray screener +3, +1 more at TL8 for metal and explosives; CT scanner +4, +6 for explosives; the EOD X-ray +5 to Search and +4 to Explosives (EOD) with no operator roll). With a character targeted, Search is a Quick Contest against their Holdout, and against a metal detector undercover clothing adds nothing. A GM tool runs a security system for the selected character: spotting it (Vision-5, Observation or Per-based Traps; a Quick Contest against Camouflage if hidden), identifying it, defeating it in secret (Traps or Electronics Operation (Security), the housing first if wired against tampering; any failure sets off the alarm), a smart fence (-4), a seismic detector (Stealth-4) and a signature pad (Forgery-3). The countersniper system rolls 10 plus the shot's Hearing modifier (High-Tech pp. 205-207, 217).

surveillanceGear.Name: Surveillance gear and countersurveillance
surveillanceGear.Hint: A spike mike in use (equipped) is Parabolic Hearing at TL-4 levels. Row buttons: a contact mike listens through a barrier at -(DR+HP)/5, -5 more into a shielded room; a pinhead mike's cable is guided on a DX-based Electronics Operation (Surveillance) roll; a search endoscope gives +3 to Search or +2 to Lockpicking; the document scanner copies a sealed document at -2; a bug is built at home on Electronics Repair (Surveillance) at SM+9 below a matchbox's size; a bug detector sweeps a minute per 100 square feet, a Quick Contest of Electronics Operation (Surveillance) with whoever hid the bug, at its quality, +4 for a radio beacon, and never finds a phone tap, laser mike or laser pinhead mike (High-Tech pp. 208-212).

jamming.Name: Electronic signals jamming
jamming.Hint: A jammer's row button switches it on (everyone near knows, not where it is). Radio gear's row button then rolls against each switched-on jammer on the map: within its range, a Quick Contest of the user's Electronics Operation for the gear against the operator's Electronics Operation (EW) (the expendable jammer's 18); within 10 times its range, an unopposed roll. A cell-phone jammer blocks cell phones and cellular beacons within 15 yards outright (High-Tech pp. 212-213).

protectiveOddments.Name: Protective oddments
protectiveOddments.Hint: Worn footwear on Stealth: moccasins, sneakers and climbing shoes +1, arctic, blast and firefighter boots -1. New footwear has a Break in action: the best of HT, Hiking or HT-based Soldier (+1 or +2 for a good or fine custom-made pair); failure is moderate pain for 2d days, critical failure terrible pain (or a crippled foot, at the GM's word). While worn: a hockey glove gives Ham-Fisted 1; earmuffs and earplugs Protected Hearing and Hard of Hearing, the electronic ones Protected Hearing alone; a dive mask or goggles Nictitating Membrane 1, anti-laser goggles 4 and Protected Vision, tactical goggles 5; TL6+ sunglasses and ballistic sunglasses Protected Vision; a cup +2 to knockdown rolls for groin hits and a mouthguard +1 for face hits, the mouthguard's speech -2 on Diplomacy, Fast-Talk, Performance, Public Speaking, Sex Appeal and Singing as Disturbing Voice; eyeglasses and contact lenses correct Bad Sight, eyeglasses give the eyes DR 1, and a head hit breaks them on a 1 on 1d or knocks them off on 2-3. Homemade armour has a Make action: Armoury (Body Armor)+5 for paper and tape, +3 for a plastic bucket (High-Tech pp. 68-71, 225).

portableCover.Name: Portable cover
portableCover.Hint: An explosives or radiation blanket has a Smother action: a charge set off beneath it, the blanket's DR 25 coming off the damage roll. A radiation blanket in use (equipped) gives PF 3 against a radiation dose (High-Tech p. 72).

lieDetection.Name: Lie detection
lieDetection.Hint: A polygraph's row button tests the one token targeted: a Quick Contest of the operator's Electronics Operation (Medical) against the subject's Will. The margin, won or lost, goes on Interrogation rolls against that subject, by whoever makes them; the VSA and CVSA software give half of it. A subject with Compulsive Lying reads as truthful: -5 on machine-aided Interrogation instead (High-Tech pp. 215-216).

restraintDevices.Name: Restraints
restraintDevices.Hint: Shackles, handcuffs, flex cuffs, leg irons and the straitjacket are put on from the item's sheet, on the prisoner's own sheet. Cuffed behind the back: -1 DX, -4 on tasks done with the hands alone, and no weapon use; in front: -1 on hands-only tasks and no one-handed blows. A straitjacket is cuffed behind with no slipping the arms round. Leg irons are Crippled Legs. Row buttons roll Escape at the restraint's modifier (shackles 0, handcuffs -5, flex cuffs -1, leg irons 0 or -5 ratcheting, straitjacket -10) and Acrobatics or Escape to bring cuffed wrists to the front (High-Tech p. 217).

prosthetics.Name: Prosthetics and elective surgery
prosthetics.Hint: Worn eyeglasses and contact lenses mitigate Bad Sight, a hearing aid (while its battery lasts) Hard of Hearing, an arm prosthetic One Arm (the basic one leaving Ham-Fisted 2) and a leg prosthetic Lame (Missing Legs), with a point of reduced Basic Move back for the basic leg and all of it for the advanced; a GM tool for elective surgery rolls the operation and records a step of build or Appearance, or laser eye surgery curing Bad Sight (High-Tech pp. 225-226).

personalConveyances.Name: Personal conveyances
personalConveyances.Hint: A bicycle, skateboard or wheelchair in use (equipped) is ridden. A bicycle's rider moves at the better of his relative Bicycling level (DX-4 or Driving (Motorcycle)-4 unlearned) and his Move, times the bike's Enhanced Move (x1.5, the racing bike x2), rounded down; a skateboarder at his Move times the board's. The Inventory tab's "Riding" box sets the slope, which doubles Move at 7.5°, triples it at 15° and quadruples it at 30°, and whether the rider is off the road, where Road-Bound Enhanced Move is lost. A penny-farthing ridden is -1 to Bicycling, and its row button rolls a spill: at least a two-yard fall. A bicycle's Long ride button rolls the better of HT and HT-based Bicycling every minute of paced (or 15 seconds of sprinting) riding, a failure costing 1 FP. The powered wheelchairs move at Move 3. The conveyance ridden isn't carried weight, and the safety bicycle weighs x0.8 at TL7 and x0.5 at TL8. The item sheet notes towing as a two-wheeled cart and a surfboard's Move on the best waves (High-Tech pp. 226, 230-231).

hygieneAndDrugs.Name: Hygiene and drugs
hygieneAndDrugs.Hint: Soap, hand sanitizer, foot powder, insect repellent, salt tablets, quinine and antimalarials worn in daily use give their bonuses to Contagion, Infection, illness and heat rolls; a row action gives a dose: smelling salts' HT roll to come round, morphine as a painkiller (High Pain Threshold, Unfazeable and euphoria for the margin's hours), aspirin taking 1 or 2 off pain, antibiotics' +TL/2 against an illness or a wound's infection, castor oil, charcoal, chelating agents and antitoxins against a poison, truth serum's FP and -2 to Will and self-control, DMSO making a blood or digestive poison a contact agent, and a psychiatric drug holding its disadvantages at bay (High-Tech pp. 221, 226-227).

highTechPoisons.Name: High-Tech poisons
highTechPoisons.Hint: Curare, ricin, strychnine, botulin and irradiated thallium dosed and cycled by the system: their damage whatever the roll, and a HT roll each cycle for curare's paralysis and choking, ricin's coughing and choking, strychnine's seizures and choking over 2d hours, and botulin's paralysis, a point harder each cycle and lasting as a crippling injury; a row action administers a dose to the targets (High-Tech p. 227).

vehicleComponents.Name: Vehicle components
vehicleComponents.Hint: Firing from a vehicle's gun port is an attack option: -1, a 30-degree arc, refused for a weapon bulkier than Bulk -5; shooting at someone at a gun port from outside is -4 to -7. Linked weapons fire as one, at the sum of their RoF. The GM's Vehicle components tool gives a turret's turn in Ready maneuvers, a searchlight's lit circle and its blinding attack (DX, Acc 12 aimed; at night an HT roll or blinded 1d seconds more), a smoke discharger's screen, and a Hearing roll at -(TL-4) against a sound-baffled vehicle (High-Tech pp. 228-229).

vehicleProtection.Name: Vehicle protection
vehicleProtection.Hint: Where a shot lands on a vehicle, spaced armour multiplies its DR by 1.5 and laminated armour by 2 against HEAT and HEDP, before the armour divisor, and either stops HESH's spall; armour skirts add their DR on their faces and work as spaced armour; a blow of 20 or more that riveted armour stops sends rivets flying on 1-3 on 1d. On flat run-flat tyres the control roll and Dodge are at -1 and Move is 20% less (CTIS ignores two flats, three on an eight-wheeler). The tool rolls an extinguisher (TL+2) or fire-suppression system (TL+4, again after two seconds), fires the airbags (DR 10) in a crash above Move 5, and rolls DX-2 to get out from behind one (High-Tech pp. 229, 234-235).

crewConditions.Name: Crew conditions
crewConditions.Hint: In a tank, the crew hear each other at -4 while the motor runs unless it has headsets, and hear outside at -10 (-3 with the motor off); buttoned up, Vision is at -2 and nothing within five yards is seen. A fight in a tank costs 1 FP more every 10 minutes, and the tool charges the ride's 1 FP an hour (none with your head outside). Driving (Tracked) already defaults to other Driving at -4, and another tank is only unfamiliar (High-Tech pp. 234-235).

Codes.PickBreaker: Select the character breaking the code.
Codes.MakerLevel: Maker's level (IQ-5 or Cryptography; a cipher wheel's is typically 16-18)
Codes.MakerTargeted: The maker: {name}, at their own level.
Codes.NeedsCryptography: Only Cryptography can beat an encryption system.
Codes.NeedsProgram: Breaking it needs a Complexity {complexity} computer running a code-breaking program.
Codes.SecureImpossible: Secure encryption can't be cracked before TL9: suborn a key-holder or find a weakness in its mathematics.
Codes.StandardLine: Takes {time} (base {base}) on a Complexity {complexity} computer or its equal.
Codes.NeedsCardGear: Fake credit cards need a card printer and a magnetic strip decoder/encoder.
Codes.TracedPrinter: Roll Counterfeiting to avoid a printer that marks each page with its serial number.
Codes.AdvancedPrep: A new disguise takes {hours} hours to prepare, and {min} to {max} hours of fitting each time it's worn.
Codes.HiddenHolds: Its secret area holds {lbs} lbs. or {cf} cu. ft.
Codes.TooMuch: {lbs} lbs. won't fit in the secret area.

Mule.safe: The ruse works, and the mule comes through.
Mule.incident: An incident: pills passed too quickly, or some thrown up.
Mule.dosed: The contents are dosed as an overdose: 1 point of toxic damage every 15 minutes for 24 cycles, HT-4 to resist.
Mule.tells: Cramps and sweating can tip off observers.

Codes.PickScreener: Select the screener and target the suspected mule.
Codes.Watch: Watch them (Search or Observation vs. Acting)

Gadget.Title: High-Tech
Gadget.RuggedHint: Shockproof, waterproof and shatterproof: +2 HT, twice the DR, a fifth more weight and twice the price (High-Tech p. 10).
Gadget.DisguiseHint: Built to look like something else of a similar shape, found with Search: twice the price mass-produced, five times custom-built (High-Tech p. 9).
Gadget.StylingHint: Jewels, tooled leather, plating and the like: a reaction bonus from collectors and buyers, and on Merchant used as an Influence roll on them (High-Tech p. 10).
Gadget.GradeHint: Cheap: half the price, and either half again the weight or fragile (-2 HT, half the DR). Expensive: twice the price, two thirds the weight. Batteries are left out of the weight (High-Tech p. 10).
Gadget.CellWeightHint: What the batteries in the gadget weigh, which cheap and expensive leave out of their weight (High-Tech p. 10). With the batteries rule on, the batteries the gear lists are weighed for you, and batteries swapped in change the weight by the difference.
Gadget.BuildHint: What the gadget is built from, for the DR the book assumes: plastic, wood or thin metal DR 2, a weapon DR 4, a solid-metal melee weapon DR 6, and armour or a vehicle its own (High-Tech p. 11).
Gadget.HealthHint: The HT the gadget's own entry gives; zero to assume HT 10 (High-Tech p. 11).
Gadget.AdjustForSmHint: Made for a user of another size: cost, weight and power go by the Size Modifier of whoever carries it (High-Tech p. 10).
Gadget.ShownHint: Being shown to collectors or potential buyers: its styling's bonus goes on reaction rolls toward the one carrying it (High-Tech p. 10).
Gadget.ControlledHint: A chemical, biological or nuclear weapon, whose Legality Class never rises with age (High-Tech p. 8).
Gadget.NoBuildOptions: Clothing, weapons and armour can't be built rugged, cheap or expensive (High-Tech p. 10).

Grade.fragile: Cheap, fragile (x1/2 cost, -2 HT, half DR)

Gadget.PricedAt: Built: ${cost} and {weight} lbs. (x{factor} the listed price).
Gadget.Sized: Adjusted for SM {sm}: cost, weight and power x{factor}.
Gadget.Antique: Obsolete at TL{campaign}: carried as LC{lc} rather than LC{was}.
Gadget.Maintained: Worth maintenance checks at TL{campaign}: it costs ${threshold} or more.
Gadget.Simple: Simple enough at TL{campaign} to skip maintenance: under ${threshold}.

Equipment.IntrinsicHint: A skill bonus the gear gives whatever its quality, from how easy it is to use or how seldom it fails; it adds to the quality bonus (High-Tech p. 11).
Equipment.BondedTo: {name} has an Equipment Bond with this piece: +1 when using it (High-Tech p. 7).
Equipment.CombineHint: Build {name} into one gadget with the pieces ticked below.
Equipment.NothingToCombine: There is no other gear on this character to combine it with.
Equipment.AllAtOnce: All usable at once (80% of the rest)
Equipment.OneAtATime: One works at a time (50% of the rest)
Equipment.CombinedAllAtOnce: The parts can all be used at once: the heaviest and costliest in full, 80% of the others (High-Tech p. 10).
Equipment.CombinedOneAtATime: One part works at a time: the heaviest and costliest in full, 50% of the others (High-Tech p. 10).
Equipment.PartsKept: The parts are still on the sheet; remove the ones now built in.
Equipment.MadeAllAtOnce: Combination gadget of {parts}, all usable at once (High-Tech p. 10).
Equipment.MadeOneAtATime: Combination gadget of {parts}, one working at a time (High-Tech p. 10).
Equipment.SharedEndurance: {name} runs {hours} hr. on the shared batteries (High-Tech p. 10).

BlackMarket.Title: Black market
BlackMarket.Hint: {name} goes looking. The GM rolls in secret; only the GM sees the result.
BlackMarket.ContactHint: The Contact's effective skill, where one does the looking; blank for the buyer's own Streetwise.
BlackMarket.FavourableArea: Port, low-CR border or weak law enforcement (+1)
BlackMarket.GrayLighter: On the gray market, make it far milder.

general.failure: Unwanted attention from the local police or a criminal syndicate.
general.criticalFailure: A police sting, an ambush by other criminals, or goods that are dangerously defective.

electronics.failure: What was bought doesn't do what was promised, or is a fake.
electronics.criticalFailure: Some very angry people now know exactly where the buyer is.

medical.failure: Nothing turns up, or the seller can't supply as much as asked.
medical.criticalFailure: Scars, placebos, or someone angry on the buyer's trail.

combatGear.failure: Only an inferior version of what was wanted.
combatGear.criticalFailure: Hardware that blows up on first use, or is being tracked.

BlackMarket.Outlawed: Outlawed (LC0) goods: no roll. Finding them is an adventure, and failing can cost loved ones, freedom or a life (High-Tech p. 9).
BlackMarket.Price: Price: about ${price} ({share}% of the legal ${list}). Haggling with Merchant seldom moves black-market dealers.
BlackMarket.PriceGm: Price: hard to get legally, so the dealer names it; the GM sets it.

Condition.used: Used: ${low} to ${high} (50-80% of new), and it may not be in perfect shape: an operation roll spots problems.
Condition.old: Old stock, not yet obsolete: ${low} to ${high} (1-10% of new).

Firearm.Title: Gun quality and care
Firearm.AccurateTooltip: Fine: +1 Acc, for a gun whose base Acc is 2 or more; very fine: +2 Acc, for base Acc 4 or more (High-Tech p. 79).
Firearm.ReliableTooltip: Fine: Malf. a step better; very fine: two steps. Not for a full-automatic weapon (High-Tech p. 79).
Firearm.GradeSetAside: Its Basic Set grade ({grade}) is set aside on a gun while this rule is on: choose accurate and reliable work here.
Firearm.RerollLine: Past Malf. {malf}: a malfunction is rolled again, and only happens if that roll malfunctions too.

Problem.accurate1: Fine accuracy work only helps a gun whose base Acc is 2 or more.
Problem.accurate2: Very fine accuracy work only helps a gun whose base Acc is 4 or more.
Problem.fullAuto: A full-automatic weapon can't be made more reliable.

Firearm.AccurateHint: Accuracy work on the gun (High-Tech p. 79).
Firearm.AccuracyLostHint: Accuracy lost to abuse, age or wear (High-Tech pp. 80-81).
Firearm.UntrainedHint: Shooting at default or without the gun's minimum ST (High-Tech p. 81).
Firearm.RerollSaved: Reliable: the malfunction was rolled again ({roll}: {dice}), under Malf. {malf}. No malfunction.
Firearm.RerollFailed: Reliable: the malfunction was rolled again ({roll}: {dice}), and malfunctions too.
Firearm.MalfunctionLostTooltip: Steps of Malf. the gun has lost to abuse, age, neglect or a hostile environment, as the GM rules (High-Tech p. 80).
Firearm.AccuracyLostTooltip: Acc the gun has lost to abuse or a worn barrel, as the GM rules (High-Tech pp. 80-81).
Firearm.RuggedLine: As an object: DR {dr}, HT {ht}, Unliving (High-Tech p. 80).
Firearm.PrecisionHint: A sniper rifle or target pistol rolls against HT, not HT+4, when abused; a failure costs it 1-3 Acc (High-Tech p. 80).
Firearm.ClothBeltHint: A cloth ammunition belt soaks up mud and water: -1 Malf. (High-Tech p. 129).
Firearm.SafetyLine: Safety: a free action at the start or end of a turn with a familiar gun, a Ready maneuver at default or with an unfamiliar one (High-Tech p. 80).
Firearm.MaintenanceLine: Maintenance checks: IQ-based Guns, Armoury (Small Arms) or Soldier; Gunner or Armoury (Heavy Weapons) for heavy weapons (High-Tech p. 80).
Firearm.FeedTooltip: What Immediate Action has to clear, which sets how long it takes (High-Tech p. 81).
Firearm.ReadiesBelt: Immediate Action: {ready} Ready maneuvers, {assisted} with an assistant gunner.

Drawing.Title: Drawing guns

Carries.smallOfBack: Holstered at the small of the back

Drawing.HolsterOwned: A holster or sling is chosen from the character's own gear, once the gun is on a character.
Drawing.ModifierHint: The place's and the holster's modifiers, and the situation's, for the master hand
Drawing.ReadiesHint: Ready maneuvers to draw or stow it without Fast-Draw; a success saves one
Drawing.Readies: Drawing or stowing takes {readies} Ready maneuver(s); a successful Fast-Draw saves one.
Drawing.DrawHint: One gun per hand each turn; the master hand's is rolled first
Drawing.StowHint: A Ready (two or three to sling a long arm), or a Fast-Draw roll with Quick-Sheathe
Drawing.PickGun: Pick a gun for at least one hand
Drawing.SameGun: One gun can't be drawn with both hands
Drawing.HandUsed: That hand has drawn its gun this turn
Drawing.TurnOver: The draw failed: no more Fast-Draw this turn
Drawing.LoopFirst: {gun}'s hammer loop takes a Ready to free before Fast-Draw
Drawing.DrawnFree: {gun} is drawn, as a free action.
Drawing.DrawnAfter: {gun} comes free a second sooner: {readies} Ready maneuver(s) still to go.
Drawing.DroppedBoth: Critical failure: both guns are dropped ({gun}).
Drawing.OnLanyard: {gun} hangs on its lanyard: a DX roll, one Ready per attempt, gets it back.
Drawing.SleeveFailed: The sleeve holster doesn't deliver the gun: the free hand and another Ready get it out.
Drawing.SleeveBroken: Critical failure: the sleeve holster breaks, and prying the gun out takes 2d seconds with the free hand.
Drawing.StowedFree: {gun} is stowed, as a free action.
Drawing.TooBulky: {holster} takes a gun of Bulk -1 or less
Drawing.FlapTuckedHint: No -2 to Fast-Draw, but no protection from the elements either
Drawing.HammerLoopHint: An early belt holster's loop over the hammer: a Ready frees it before Fast-Draw
Drawing.LanyardHint: Retrieve a dropped gun with a DX roll, one Ready per attempt
Drawing.LanyardRecord: Tie it to a gun on the gun's sheet: a dropped gun is retrieved with a DX roll, one Ready per attempt. It can be cut: -6 to hit, DR 2, HP 2.

Holsters.belt: A Ready in or out. An early one's hammer loop takes a Ready to free before Fast-Draw.
Holsters.military: The flap keeps out dirt; tucked away, it gives no -2 and no protection.
Holsters.shoulder: Worn under the off-hand arm: the shoulder holster's -1 is its place's.
Holsters.sleeve: Delivers a gun of Bulk -1 or less on a Fast-Draw roll; a failure needs the free hand and a Ready, a critical failure breaks it.
Holsters.fastDrawRig: A Ready in or out, and fast.
Holsters.undercover: Worn inside the waistband or at the ankle.
Holsters.retention: +2 to Retain Weapon while the gun is in it.
Holsters.rifleSling: Unslinging or slinging takes two Ready maneuvers, three from the back.
Holsters.patrolSling: Raising the gun takes one Ready.
Holsters.scabbard: Keeps the elements off a long arm.

Draw.Title: Who draws first (guns)
Draw.Pick: Select one gunfighter's token and target the other, or target both
Draw.OtherHint: Posture, a grapple, moving, where the gun is carried and its holster are applied for you; add anything else here.
Draw.Label: Who draws first: {a} and {b}
Draw.BothReady: Both guns are ready: the turn sequence decides.
Draw.Simultaneous: They fire at the same moment.
Draw.ThrowsAway: {name} drops the gun or shoots himself, and {foe} fires first!

RateOfFire.Title: Trigger and rate of fire
RateOfFire.TriggerTooltip: The weapon tables don't give a gun's trigger type: set it from the gun's description, or leave it to be worked out (High-Tech p. 82).

TriggerLine.sa: Single-action: cocked before the first shot; a revolver has to be cocked for every shot.
TriggerLine.da: Double-action: RoF 3 without cocking, but an aimed shot takes -1 unless the hammer was cocked first.
TriggerLine.dao: Double-action-only: RoF 3, and a point of Acc lower for the heavy pull.
TriggerLine.safe: Safe-action: RoF 3 with no penalty to an aimed shot.

RateOfFire.SafeLine: Almost impossible to fire by accident through unsafe handling.
RateOfFire.RevolverTooltip: Whether the gun is a revolver, which decides its trigger when that is left blank and whether it can be fanned or thumbed. Left blank, a pistol loaded a round at a time into five chambers or more counts as one.
RateOfFire.BurstLimitTooltip: Rounds per burst for a gun with a burst limiter, fired one to three bursts per attack at its listed RoF. 0 for none, or the high-cyclic mark's own: a RoF 9# gun fires three-round bursts (High-Tech p. 83).
RateOfFire.InstantSelectorHint: Changes between settings at once, with no Ready maneuver (High-Tech pp. 82-83).
RateOfFire.TieHint: A revolver with its trigger tied back or taken off can only be fanned or thumbed until it is untied (High-Tech p. 84).
RateOfFire.TiedRefusal: Trigger {tie}: this revolver can only be fanned or thumbed.
RateOfFire.SelectorHint: The row's fire selector button changes setting; in combat that takes a Ready maneuver unless the gun has a double or progressive trigger (High-Tech p. 82).
RateOfFire.SelectorNeedsReady: Changing the fire selector on {gun} takes a Ready maneuver.
RateOfFire.SelectorInstant: A double or progressive trigger: no Ready needed.
RateOfFire.BurstLine: Limited bursts of {limit}: {shots} shots an attack, and no Spraying Fire.
RateOfFire.HighCyclicLine: High-cyclic controlled bursts: hits counted at Rcl 1, and no Suppression Fire.
RateOfFire.BurstsNote: Up to {bursts} burst(s) of {limit} ({shots} shots): the shots come in whole bursts, those between bursts dropping to the burst below.
RateOfFire.FastFiringRefusal: This gun can't be fast-fired at RoF {rof} (it can at: {rates}).
RateOfFire.TwoHandedNote: Held in two hands, cocked with the off thumb.
RateOfFire.NotWithFanning: Fast-firing, fanning and thumbing don't combine.
RateOfFire.FanningNote: Fanned: the other hand works the hammer.
RateOfFire.FanningNoAim: A fanned revolver can't be aimed.
RateOfFire.FanningNoShots: Critical failure: no shots are fired, and the rounds stay in the gun.
RateOfFire.FanningBruised: 1d = {die}: a bruised hand, moderate pain for {minutes} minute(s).
RateOfFire.ThumbingNote: Thumbed: the thumb slips the hammer.
RateOfFire.ThumbingFailed: Thumbing failed: the gun doesn't fire this turn, and keeps its rounds.
RateOfFire.ThumbingFumble: Critical failure: the gun is dropped or goes off early and wild (the GM decides what it hits).
RateOfFire.NeedsSingleAction: Fanning and thumbing are for a single-action revolver of RoF 1.

Shooting.StanceOn: Held in the two-handed stance: minimum ST times 0.8, Bulk a step better, aimed shots braced; no fanning or thumbing.
Shooting.StanceHint: The two-handed pistol stance: minimum ST times 0.8 (rounded up), Bulk a step better, every aimed shot braced (High-Tech p. 84).
Shooting.StanceNoFanning: A gun in the two-handed stance can't be fanned or thumbed (High-Tech p. 84).
Shooting.PrecisionNotAiming: Precision Aiming needs the Aim maneuver.
Shooting.PrecisionNoScope: Precision Aiming needs a scope or sights that give an aiming bonus.
Shooting.PrecisionNotBraced: Precision Aiming needs the gun braced.
Shooting.PrecisionAtCap: No higher: the extra aim can't pass +{cap}, the lower of the scope's bonus and the gun's Acc.
Shooting.PrecisionWait: The next +1 needs {seconds} seconds of Aim ({aimed} so far).
Shooting.PrecisionGained: +{bonus} from Precision Aiming (at most +{cap}); the next roll at {next} seconds.
Shooting.PrecisionLost: The aim is lost with every aiming bonus: the shooter has to start over.
Shooting.PrecisionSpotted: Critical failure: the target sees a protruding barrel or a glint off the scope.
Shooting.RapidStrikeNote: Ranged Rapid Strike: two attacks this second, each at half the RoF.

RapidRefusal.rateOfFire: A Ranged Rapid Strike needs RoF 2 or more.
RapidRefusal.maneuver: A Rapid Strike is made on Attack or All-Out Attack.
RapidRefusal.spraying: A Ranged Rapid Strike isn't Spraying Fire.

Shooting.RapidSecond: The second attack of the Ranged Rapid Strike: tick the option again.
Shooting.TaName: Name it "TA (Specialty/Target)", such as "TA (Pistol/Skull)" or "TA (Rifle/Vitals Chinks)".
Shooting.TaWeaponNote: At a weapon: +1 against a large one, -1 against a small one, entered on the roll.
Shooting.IadTarget: Target the one foe whose gun you grab.
Shooting.IadDisabled: A vital part comes off: the gun can't fire until it is put back together.
Shooting.IadGmMarks: The GM marks the gun out of action.

IadResult.unready: The gun is intact but unready.
IadResult.intact: The gun stays in the foe's hands, intact and ready.
IadResult.shotAtHand: Critical failure: the foe keeps the gun and may shoot the disarmer in the hand at full skill.

Sustained.Title: Sustained fire
Sustained.BarrelTooltip: A light barrel halves a machine gun's safe number, an extra-heavy one adds half. An automatic rifle the book says to treat as a machine gun with a light barrel is marked light here (High-Tech p. 86).
Sustained.DisciplineTooltip: Sustained: bursts shorter than its RoF with 4-5 second pauses (800 safe rounds). Rapid: 2-3 second pauses (400). Assault: long bursts or no pauses (200). Worked out from the pauses and bursts unless set (High-Tech p. 86).
Sustained.WaterTooltip: A water-cooled gun fires without heating until the water is gone: a pint every 500 rounds (High-Tech p. 129).
Sustained.BarrelSecondsTooltip: Blank or 0 for the usual 10 seconds; some guns change faster (High-Tech pp. 129-136).
Sustained.AccuracyLostTooltip: Acc lost for good, as when a barrel was fired to three times its safe number (High-Tech p. 86).
Sustained.MaintainedHint: A well-maintained gun and feed device: its safe number x1.25 (High-Tech pp. 80, 85-86).
Sustained.CondenserHint: A condenser canister recovers the steam: ten times the rounds per pint (High-Tech p. 129).
Sustained.SafeSmallArms: Safe: {safe} rounds in under a minute.
Sustained.SafeMachineGun: Safe: {sustained} rounds of sustained fire, {rapid} rapid, {assault} assault.
Sustained.HeatOver: Heat: {shots} of {limit}: Acc -{accuracy}, Malf. -{malfunction} until it cools (15 minutes).
Sustained.CoolHint: The gun has rested 15 minutes, or had its barrel changed: its heat is gone.
Sustained.WaterLine: Water jacket: {pints} pints, {rounds} rounds of cooling left ({per} a pint).
Sustained.BarrelHint: A Guns or Gunner roll: on a success the fresh barrel is cool; a critical failure burns the hand, 1d minutes of moderate pain (High-Tech p. 129).
Sustained.BarrelChanged: Barrel changed in {seconds} seconds: the gun is cool.
Sustained.BarrelFailed: The barrel isn't changed: {seconds} seconds spent.
Sustained.BarrelBurned: Burned hand: {minutes} minutes of moderate pain (rolled {die}).
Sustained.NoActor: Only a gun someone carries can have its barrel changed.
Sustained.NoSkill: No level in {skill} to change the barrel with.
Sustained.Overheated: Overheated: Acc -{accuracy}, Malf. -{malfunction} until it cools.
Sustained.Warped: Fired to three times its safe number: Acc -{accuracy} for good.
Sustained.WaterGone: The water jacket has boiled dry: the barrel heats from now on.

Environment.Title: Shooting environment
Environment.Hint: Where the scene's guns are fired. Kept on the scene, with its air and water, for every book's weapons that read them.
Environment.NoScene: There is no scene to set.
Environment.UnderwaterHint: Only cased ammunition with sealed primers is reliable; caseless ammo fails in time; hollow-points do nothing (High-Tech p. 85).
Environment.SpaceHint: Vacuum and temperature extremes: an automatic TL6-8 gun malfunctions on 14 (High-Tech p. 85).
Environment.IntoWaterNote: {feet} feet of water count as {yards} yards more.
Environment.OutOfRange: Out of range: the shot counts {yards} yards against a Max of {max}.
Environment.UnderwaterBuiltHint: Built to fire underwater: distance counts x25, not x1,000 (High-Tech pp. 85, 92, 117).
Environment.IntoWaterHalf: Past its 1/2D of {half} yards: half damage.

Aftermath.Title: After the firefight
Aftermath.Hint: Hard of hearing, and at night half-blind in the dark, for (20 - HT) minutes: {names}.
Aftermath.Indoors: The shooting was inside a building or vehicle (-5 to Hearing, not -4)
Aftermath.Night: At night (-2 to Vision in the dark)
Aftermath.NoOne: Select the tokens who were there, or view the fight's combat.
Aftermath.VisionLine: After the firefight: Vision in the dark

Wounding.VitalsHit: {name}: 1d for the vitals rolled {roll}: the bullet struck the vitals.
Wounding.VitalsMissed: {name}: 1d for the vitals rolled {roll}: the torso, its injury capped.
Wounding.LimbPermanent: {name}'s {part}: {injury} injury, at least twice the {least} that cripples it: crippled for good, with no HT roll for how long.
Wounding.FrightText: {name} took a serious wound: a Fright Check ({modifier}) this turn. The GM may make it worse for a wound that spurts blood or breaks a bone, or better for someone used to injuries.
Wounding.NoSurgery: The surgeon has no Surgery skill

Reloading.Title: Reloading
Reloading.TypeTooltip: How the gun is loaded, which sets how long a reload takes and what Fast-Draw (Ammo) saves (High-Tech pp. 86-88). Worked out from its Shots column and skill where that is reliable; set it where the book's description says otherwise. "As its table" keeps the table's time.
Reloading.PowderTooltip: Black powder fouls the gun (High-Tech p. 86). Worked out from how the gun loads and its TL (TL5 and earlier) unless set.
Reloading.CarefulHint: Twice the loading time, for +1 Acc on the shot it loads (High-Tech p. 86).
Reloading.TimeWhole: A full reload: {seconds} seconds, {fastDraw} with Fast-Draw (Ammo).
Reloading.TimePerRound: Reloading: {seconds} seconds a barrel or chamber, {fastDraw} with Fast-Draw (Ammo).
Reloading.CarefullyLoaded: Carefully loaded: +{acc} Acc on the next shot.
Reloading.FoulingClean: Fouling: {shots} shots since it was cleaned.
Reloading.FoulingLine: Fouling: {shots} shots since it was cleaned: Malf. -{malfunction}, loading +{percent}%.
Reloading.FoulingLineAcc: Fouling: {shots} shots since it was cleaned: Malf. -{malfunction}, Acc -{accuracy}, loading +{percent}%.
Reloading.CleanHint: Two minutes' thorough cleaning clears the fouling (High-Tech p. 86).
Reloading.Cleaned: Cleaned: {minutes} minutes spent, the fouling gone.
Reloading.Fouled: Fouled after {shots} shots: Malf. -{malfunction}, loading +{percent}% until it is cleaned.
Reloading.FouledAcc: Fouled after {shots} shots: Malf. -{malfunction}, Acc -{accuracy}, loading +{percent}% until it is cleaned.
Reloading.FouledHint: {shots} shots of black powder since it was cleaned (High-Tech p. 86).

Aid.flask: Self-measuring powder flask (-{seconds} s; not with paper cartridges)
Aid.paperCartridges: Paper cartridges (half the time; not with the flask)
Aid.clamped: Clamped magazines ({seconds} s; not with Fast-Draw)
Aid.assistant: Assistant gunner ({seconds} s; not with Fast-Draw)

Reloading.DoubleLoadingLine: The reload rolls {name} at {level} in place of Fast-Draw (Ammo): a success saves Fast-Draw's seconds and a second or two a pair more (High-Tech p. 251).
Reloading.MountedRoll: Loading in the saddle: the lower of {skill} and Riding, {modifier}

Families.Title: Weapon family
Families.AirBandLine: The charge is running down: now {damage}, Range {half}/{max}.
Families.AirHint: The shots left in the air charge; a spent charge must be replaced before the gun fires again (High-Tech p. 88).
Families.AirBandHint: From shot {from} of the charge the pressure is down: less damage and range (High-Tech p. 88).
Families.AirEmpty: The air charge is spent: fit a fresh reservoir or gas cartridge from the gun's sheet (High-Tech p. 88).
Families.RechargeHint: Replace the air reservoir or gas cartridge; the gun's description says how long it takes.
Families.StunnerLine: Ranged stunner: on a failed HT roll the victim is stunned while the trigger is held ({seconds} s unless the shooter says otherwise) and (20 - HT) s after, then rolls to recover at the shock's penalty. Minimum range 1 yard (High-Tech p. 89).
Families.StunnerEmdLine: Ranged EMD stunner: on a failed HT roll the victim is knocked down and stunned while the trigger is held ({seconds} s unless the shooter says otherwise) and (20 - HT) s after, then rolls to recover at the shock's penalty. Minimum range 1 yard (High-Tech p. 89).
Families.HoldLabel: Stunner: seconds the trigger is held (0 for the gun's own)
Families.Stunned: {name} is stunned while the trigger is held ({held} s) and {after} s after, then rolls HT{penalty} each second to recover. The darts can't be pulled out meanwhile, and a victim soaked in something flammable may catch fire.
Families.StunnedEmd: {name} is knocked down and stunned while the trigger is held ({held} s) and {after} s after, then rolls HT{penalty} each second to recover. The darts can't be pulled out meanwhile, and a victim soaked in something flammable may catch fire.
Families.SafetyTooltip: Revolvers of TL5 and earlier have no safety unless their description says so (High-Tech p. 93).
Families.CarriedFullHint: Off: the hammer rests on an empty chamber, and the gun loads a round short (High-Tech p. 93).
Families.EmptyChamberLine: Carried with the hammer on an empty chamber: it loads a round short (High-Tech p. 93).
Families.CarriedFullLine: Carried with every chamber loaded: a knock on the hammer can fire it, and the GM may call for a DX roll whenever it is handled other than to shoot (High-Tech pp. 80, 93).
Families.NoSuppressorLine: Suppressors don't work on an ordinary revolver (High-Tech p. 159).
Families.WhipLine: Pistol whipping: Brawling or DX, thrust{modifier} crushing (High-Tech p. 93).
Families.BrainerLine: Made for braining: Axe/Mace, swing{modifier} crushing (High-Tech pp. 90, 93).
Families.BrainHint: Turning it round to grip the barrel takes a Ready maneuver (High-Tech p. 90).
Families.MechanicalLine: Mechanical machine gun: unfamiliarity {unfamiliar} rather than -2, {clearing} more to fix a malfunction for one unfamiliar with it, {offMount} fired off its mount (High-Tech p. 127).
Families.OffMountLine: Mechanical machine gun off its mount
Families.BackblastLine: Backblast: {damage} burning, full damage to {full} yards and half to {half} yards behind, in a 60-degree cone (High-Tech p. 147).
Families.BackblastCrLine: Backblast: {damage} crushing countermass to {full} yards behind, in a 60-degree cone; safe to fire indoors (High-Tech p. 147).

Backblast.Reach: {damage} {type}: full damage to {full} yards behind the firer, half to {half} yards, in a 60-degree cone.
Backblast.ReachFull: {damage} {type} to {full} yards behind the firer, in a 60-degree cone.
Backblast.NoAim: No target to aim by, so the cone isn't placed: apply it to whoever stands behind the firer.
Backblast.NobodyCaught: Nobody stands in the cone behind the firer.
Backblast.Reflected: Fired indoors: the walls throw it back at {name}.

IndirectFire.DialogHint: Target the token to be shelled first to measure the distances; the forward observer's own figures follow whoever is picked. Any figure can be changed.

Missions.predicted: Predicted fire (an area off a map)

IndirectFire.AidCounted: {item} is carried as a Navigation tool, already in the skill.
IndirectFire.AidAsk: No compass or GPS on the sheet: pick what the observer has.
IndirectFire.NoMode: This weapon has no mode that fires indirectly.
IndirectFire.NoGun: The gun or its attack row is gone.
IndirectFire.ObservedSummary: Observed fire, directed by {fo}. The target is {yards} yards from the gun: {trajectory}, {seconds} seconds of flight.
IndirectFire.PredictedSummary: Predicted fire on an area {yards} yards away: {trajectory}, {seconds} seconds of flight. No -10, but the fire can't follow a target that moves.
IndirectFire.Standing: The next shot is at {penalty}; the observer has spent {seconds} seconds spotting.
IndirectFire.NavigationRoll: {fo}: Navigation, to place himself and the gun
IndirectFire.Navigated: {fo} knows where he and the gun are.
IndirectFire.Lost: {fo} can't place himself and the gun yet; he may try again.
IndirectFire.Located: {fo} calls in the target in {seconds} seconds: the first shot is at {penalty}.
IndirectFire.Corrected: {fo} corrects in {seconds} seconds: the next shot is at {penalty}.
IndirectFire.CriticalSuccess: Critical success: no penalty from here on.
IndirectFire.FriendlyFire: Critical failure: the rounds come down somewhere the GM picks, perhaps on friends or on the observer himself.
IndirectFire.Missed: Shot {shot} misses by {margin}: it comes down {yards} yards off, direction {direction} ({bearing} degrees clockwise from the line of fire). {arrives}

Accessories.Title: Firearm accessories
Accessories.FittedToHint: The gun this accessory is fitted to, among the character's firearms. Its own price and weight stay on this item.
Accessories.GradeHint: A home-built suppressor's quality (High-Tech p. 159): it decides the build time, the roll, how long it lasts and what it costs.
Accessories.ScopeFixed: Fixed-power scope: +{bonus} Acc once the shooter has aimed {bonus} seconds or more, nothing before.
Accessories.ScopeVariable: Variable-power scope: up to +{bonus} Acc, a point for each second aimed.
Accessories.VisibilityLine: Improved-visibility sights: a point off darkness penalties on every shot.
Accessories.ReflexLine: +1 to Guns out to {yards} yards, on every shot, and up to 3 off darkness penalties; not with a magnifying scope, and nothing while a targeting laser is on.
Accessories.SightLine: Looking through it: {vision}, colorblind and tunnel vision (toggle from the gun's row).
Accessories.AddOnLine: An add-on: {vision} through the scope or sight it is mounted in front of; looking through it leaves the shooter colorblind with tunnel vision.
Accessories.SightAccuracy: +{bonus} Acc to an aimed shot, as a fixed-power scope.
Accessories.ComputerLine: Targeting program +{program} to the gun's skill; rangefinder +{rangefinder} to an aimed shot out to {yards} yards; magnification up to +{magnification}.
Accessories.LaserLine: Targeting laser: {yards} yards (in daylight {daylight}, in low light {low}). Tick the laser sight on the attack: its +1 and the target's Dodge bonus go as far as the dot does.
Accessories.LaserInfrared: Infrared: only a shooter with Night Vision, Infravision or Hyperspectral Vision sees the dot.
Accessories.LaserColourTl: Only red lasers exist at TL7.
Accessories.SuppressorLine: Hearing {penalty} to hear the shot. Fitting or removing it takes {seconds} seconds.
Accessories.WiperLine: Wiper design: damage and range x{damage}, good for {shots} shots.
Accessories.GradeNoRoll: no roll for anyone with Guns or Armoury (an IQ roll for a novice)
Accessories.SuppressorRevolver: A suppressor doesn't work on an ordinary revolver (High-Tech p. 159).
Accessories.SuppressorWornOut: The suppressor is worn out: it no longer muffles the shot.
Accessories.PistolStockLine: Attached: shoot with Guns (Rifle), +1 Acc, -1 Bulk, ST x0.8 (round up). {seconds} seconds on or off.
Accessories.FoldingStockLine: Fold or unfold it from the gun's row (a Ready): folded, Bulk a step better, -1 Acc, +1 Recoil unless it is 1, ST x1.2 (round up).
Accessories.BipodLine: Open or close it from the gun's row (a Ready): open, a prone shooter is braced and needs two-thirds the ST.
Accessories.SticksLine: A sitting shooter resting the gun on them counts as braced.
Accessories.MagazineTooltip: A magazine in place of the standard one (High-Tech p. 155), worked out from the calibre in the gun's name.
Accessories.UnreliableHint: An extended or high-density magazine is -1 Malf. at the GM's discretion; a drum always is.
Accessories.MagazineLine: {rounds} rounds (normally {normal}): {weight} lbs. loaded, ${cost} empty; Bulk {bulk}, Malf. {malf}.
Accessories.MagazineNoCalibre: The gun's name gives no calibre from the ammunition tables, so the magazine can't be weighed or priced.
Accessories.HighDensityGrip: A high-density magazine can't go in a pistol's grip (High-Tech p. 155).
Accessories.ReportTooltip: How loud the gun is, by the Hearing Distance Table (High-Tech p. 158).

Report.heavy: Heavy pistol, SMG, rifle, shotgun (512 yards)

Accessories.SealedBreechHint: A bolt-action or dropping-block gun, on which a suppressor works a point better (High-Tech p. 158).
Accessories.HeardAtLine: Heard on an unmodified Hearing roll out to {yards} yards.
Accessories.SightInUseLine: The shooter is looking through the sight.
Accessories.UseSight: Look through the sight, or stop
Accessories.SightOnSaid: Looks through the sight: colorblind, with tunnel vision.
Accessories.OtherSetupHint: This mode is for the stock or bipod the other way: change it from the gun's row first.
Accessories.RefuseFolded: The stock is unfolded: fold it first (a Ready), or fire the unfolded mode.
Accessories.RefuseUnfolded: The stock is folded: unfold it first (a Ready), or fire the folded mode.
Accessories.RefuseBipod: The bipod is folded: open it first (a Ready), or fire the mode without it.
Accessories.RefuseNoBipod: The bipod is open: fire the bipod mode, or fold it first (a Ready).
Accessories.RefuseNotProne: The bipod mode needs a prone shooter; standing, fire the mode without it.
Accessories.BipodHint: The bipod is open under a prone shooter: two-thirds the ST, and braced (High-Tech p. 160).
Accessories.FoldedHint: -1 Acc, +1 Recoil unless it is 1, ST x1.2, Bulk a step better (High-Tech p. 160).
Accessories.PistolStockHint: Shot with Guns (Rifle): +1 Acc, -1 Bulk, ST x0.8 (High-Tech p. 160).
Accessories.HearNoListener: Target the token of whoever might hear the shot.
Accessories.HearOutsideCone: Behind the gun or far off to its side (-1)
Accessories.ScopeDarkness: Collects light: -{offset} to darkness penalties on an aimed shot.
Accessories.IlluminatedHint: Lit by battery or tritium: up to 2 off darkness penalties on an aimed shot, in place of the scope's 1 (High-Tech p. 155).
Accessories.TacticalLightLine: Tactical light: switched on for a shot within its {yards}-yard beam, darkness is no worse than {floor}.
Accessories.TacticalLightNote: {name}: darkness no worse than -3 out to {yards} yards; the target may be dazzled (HT-4) at the GM's call.

Ammunition.Title: Ammunition (High-Tech)
Ammunition.NoCalibre: Its calibre isn't in the Ammunition Tables.
Ammunition.FromBox: Loaded from {box}: its rounds are the load.

UpgradeHint.fieldExpedient: Stones or coins for shot: -1 Acc, half damage and range, -2 Malf. (p. 163).
UpgradeHint.paperCartridge: Charge and ball wrapped in paper: half the loading time, and the reloading aid starts ticked (p. 163).
UpgradeHint.lightCased: Composite or plastic cases: WPS x0.7, CPS x2 (p. 164).
UpgradeHint.extraPowerful: A hotter charge: Dmg, Range and ST x1.1; -1 Malf. on most TL5-6 and cheap TL7-8 guns; CPS x1.5 (p. 165).
UpgradeHint.matchGrade: Acc x1.25, at most +1 (a handloaded perfect match x1.5, at most +2); not for automatic weapons or with extra-powerful; CPS x2 (pp. 165, 174).
UpgradeHint.subsonic: Pistol rounds -1 to Hearing and Range x0.8; PDW and rifle rounds -2 to Hearing and Dmg and Range x0.6; CPS x1.3 (p. 165).
UpgradeHint.silent: Heard on the 16-yard line of the Hearing Distance Table; most silent rounds need a gun built for them, though shotgun and grenade-launcher rounds were made for ordinary guns; CPS x10, LC1 (p. 165).

Refusal.tl: Not yet at the gun's TL.
Refusal.class: Not for this class of ammunition.
Refusal.excludes: Can't be combined with an upgrade already chosen.
Refusal.notPistolOrRifle: Only for pistol, PDW and rifle rounds.
Refusal.alreadyLight: This round is light cased already.
Refusal.projectile: Only with solid, hollow-point, AP or APHC projectiles.

Note.extraPowerfulAuto: Automatic: Malf. and RoF may change (GM)
Note.extraPowerfulPowder: Charge: Armoury or IQ-based Guns-2 to stay safe
Note.airburstFuse: Time fuse: +3 at an area (+1 at a flier)
Note.cargoHit: Hit: type the dice the description prints
Note.flareBurn: Flare: {dice} burn a second for {seconds} s
Note.wpBrush: DX to brush a fragment away

NoteHint.extraPowerfulAuto: Automatic weapons are often sensitive to a change of propellant: they may suffer Malf. penalties, and their RoF is likely to rise, as the GM rules (p. 165).
NoteHint.extraPowerfulPowder: Loading a powder-and-shot gun hot takes an Armoury (Small Arms) roll or an IQ-based Guns roll at -2 to stay within its safe limits (p. 165).
NoteHint.silent: The shot is heard on the Hearing Distance Table's 16-yard line (pp. 158, 165).
NoteHint.hearing: Subsonic ammunition is harder to hear (p. 165).
NoteHint.batch: A critical failure while reloading lowered this batch's Malf. (p. 174).
NoteHint.matched: Match-grade rounds handloaded for this gun: Acc x1.5, at most +2 (p. 174).
NoteHint.slug: A shotgun fires this projectile from a rifled slug's figures: four times the buckshot's damage, +1 Acc, 1/2D x2.5, Max x1.5 (High-Tech pp. 166, 168).
NoteHint.hpExpansion: At the GM's option a low-velocity hollow-point only expands, and gets its better damage type, on a roll of TL-3 or less on 1d (High-Tech p. 167).
NoteHint.noDr: An object with no DR gets DR 1 against it (High-Tech pp. 166-167, 173).
NoteHint.poison: A hit that penetrates delivers one dose of the poison as a follow-up attack; the GM applies it (High-Tech p. 167).
NoteHint.depletedUranium: Treat as an incendiary attack when it penetrates non-flexible armour with DR 10 or more (High-Tech p. 169).
NoteHint.underwaterDart: Underwater, distance to the target is multiplied by 25 rather than 1,000 (High-Tech p. 169).
NoteHint.minie: A muzzle-loading rifle firing Minié balls takes a musket's time to load (High-Tech pp. 86, 109).
NoteHint.ballRange: The full-calibre ball has 0.9 of the gun's range; the row's range is the buckshot's (High-Tech p. 173).
NoteHint.shell: Its figures are in the weapon's description; the load prices the shell and bursts in the air (High-Tech pp. 173-174).
NoteHint.beehive: Beehive explodes at its Maximum Range and has no 1/2D; its figures are the weapon's (High-Tech p. 173).
NoteHint.silver: Soft silver fouls a rifled barrel: -1 Acc and Malf. at the GM's discretion; jacketed hollow-points avoid it (High-Tech p. 168).
NoteHint.airburst: Attacking an Area (Campaigns p. 414): a proximity fuse gives the full +4. When fired indirectly the fragments rain down, ignoring posture and any cover that isn't overhead (High-Tech pp. 174-175).
NoteHint.airburstFuse: A TL5-6 time fuse gives +3 rather than +4 to hit an area, or only +1 against a flying target (High-Tech p. 174).
NoteHint.selfDestruct: The round destroys itself once it passes this distance, usually 1/2D (High-Tech p. 175).
NoteHint.tracer: Incendiary within this range. On the turn after a long burst the shooter may add +1 to skill; firing tracers gives away his position (High-Tech p. 175).
NoteHint.replacesBasic: A High-Tech projectile takes the place of the Basic Set round chosen on the mode; that round's effects are taken off the row (High-Tech p. 166).
NoteHint.cargoHit: The mode's line is another round's blast; the gun's description prints this round's own dice, which go in the Hit field (High-Tech pp. 143, 171).
NoteHint.sapleDud: Early SAPLE rounds are unreliable: at TL5-6 the round explodes only on a roll of TL-2 or less on 1d, rolled as it is fired (High-Tech p. 169).
NoteHint.heshSpall: Where neither the hit nor the blast gets through DR, the blast knocks spall off the inside: a tenth of its most damage, cutting, against a hundredth of the DR, both rounded up. Not through laminated armour (High-Tech p. 170).
NoteHint.msheat: The precursor charge blows a path through explosive reactive armour for the main charge; without such armour the charges work as one (High-Tech p. 170).
NoteHint.thermobaric: The blast reaches further: divide its damage by twice the distance in yards from the centre, not three times (High-Tech p. 170; Campaigns p. 104).
NoteHint.internal: The blast follows the round through the armour and bursts inside: an internal explosion (High-Tech pp. 169-170; Campaigns p. 415).
NoteHint.flareBurn: Every flare gets hot: it burns what it touches, though a flare fired at someone doesn't stay in contact (High-Tech p. 171).
NoteHint.liquid: Paint blinds someone with goggles or a visor, and half a dozen hits cover a windshield; a scent marker makes its victim reek for an hour (High-Tech pp. 171-172).
NoteHint.poisonGas: The round spreads its filler over the burst radius: those in it are dosed as the round lands (High-Tech p. 172; Campaigns p. 439).
NoteHint.wpLinger: The follow-up line keeps its fragments' type but not how long they linger; they burn 1d(0.2) every 10 seconds for a minute (High-Tech p. 172).
NoteHint.wpBrush: The victim or an ally makes a DX roll to brush a burning fragment away (High-Tech p. 172).
NoteHint.airburstFragments: An airburst HE round does only its fragments' damage, typically in a cone along the line of fire (High-Tech p. 175).

SourceLine.handloaded: Handloaded: materials at the round's CPS.
SourceLine.reloaded: Reloaded: materials at half the round's CPS.

Ammunition.SourceHint: Who made the rounds: bought, handloaded from components, or reloaded into fired cases (p. 174).
Ammunition.Matched: A perfect match for this gun.
Ammunition.BatchHint: Load rounds with a reloading press or machine: timed by the tools, with Armoury (Small Arms) rolls (p. 174).
Ammunition.BatchLine: {rounds} rounds with {tool}: {minutes} minutes, {rolls} Armoury roll(s) at {level}, {failures} failed.
Ammunition.BatchFaster: Critical success: the batch takes a quarter less time.
Ammunition.BatchWorse: Critical failure: the batch's Malf. drops by 1 (a round might even go off while loading, at the GM's word).
Ammunition.BatchFailures: Failed rolls: the GM rules on those rounds.
Ammunition.MatchHint: A day's work, an Armoury (Small Arms) roll and an IQ-based Guns roll: success on both makes match-grade handloads a perfect match for this gun (p. 174).
Ammunition.MatchFound: A perfect match: its match-grade handloads get Acc x1.5, at most +2.
Ammunition.MatchWasted: No match found: the day and the materials are wasted.
Ammunition.MatchExplosion: Critical failure: treat as an Explosion (p. B407)!
Ammunition.NoSkills: The character needs Armoury (Small Arms), and the gun's skill, or no character holds this.
Ammunition.RoundHint: A round other than the gun's own: a shorter one down its chain fires in a revolver or manual repeater; anything else is a misload (p. 178).
Ammunition.MisloadLine: Misloaded with {round}: each shot rolls the Misloading Table.

Misload.Rolled: Misloading Table ({round} in a gun made for {gun}): {roll}.
Misload.fires: The round fires, at Acc 0; clearing the case and loading another takes as long as reloading a break-open gun.
Misload.firesAndJams: The round fires, at Acc 0, and the gun jams after it (stoppage).
Misload.jams: The round doesn't fire, and the gun jams (stoppage).
Misload.damaged: The round discharges wrongly and damages the gun (mechanical problem).
Misload.bursts: The round bursts the gun: treat as an Explosion (p. B407), whatever its TL.
Misload.Repair: Repairs take at least {days} day and {percent}% of the gun's price in parts (${cost}).

Ammunition.ConvertHint: A gunsmith converts a caplock to fire cartridges on an Armoury (Small Arms) roll at {modifier}, {days} days' work; never to Magnum rounds (p. 164).
Ammunition.Converted: Converted to fire {round} after {days} days' work.
Ammunition.BoxCalibreHint: The round in the box, as the Ammunition Tables name it; blank for what the box fits.
Ammunition.ShopHint: An Area Knowledge roll for where you shop finds ammunition 5% cheaper, 15% on a critical success (p. 175).
Ammunition.NoAreaKnowledge: The character has no Area Knowledge to roll.
Ammunition.ShotMmHint: Diameter of each projectile in millimetres. Blank for the load's usual size (00 Buck, 8.38mm, for shot; 2mm flechettes; 12.7mm canister balls). Shot of 8mm and up is buckshot (pi), from 2mm birdshot (pi-, 0.5), below that smallshot (pi-, 0.2) (High-Tech p. 173).
Ammunition.ShotCountHint: Number of projectiles (NP). Blank for the most the bore holds, (calibre / diameter) cubed, a fortieth of it for flechettes; a shotgun's own buckshot keeps its listed count (High-Tech p. 172).
Ammunition.PoisonCostHint: The cost of one dose of the poison, added to the cost per shot (High-Tech p. 167).

ProjectileHint.solid: The solid bullet the gun's statistics assume (High-Tech p. 166). A shotgun's are for 00 buckshot.
ProjectileHint.minie: A hollow-based conoidal bullet: a muzzle-loading rifle loads as fast as a musket (High-Tech pp. 86, 109).
ProjectileHint.rifledSlug: Shotguns only: four times the buckshot's damage, pi++ from 20-gauge up (pi+ below), +1 Acc, 1/2D x2.5, Max x1.5, one projectile (High-Tech p. 166).
ProjectileHint.hollowPoint: (0.5), damage type a step up; -1 Malf. in a TL5-7 self-loader. LC3 (High-Tech pp. 166-167).
ProjectileHint.poison: A hollow-point with a dose of poison as a follow-up; must be handloaded. Cost per shot plus the dose. LC1 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.ap: (2), damage x0.7, a step down below 20mm. CPS x1.5, LC2 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.aphc: (2), a step down below 20mm. CPS x2, LC2 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.frangible: (0.5), a step up, never overpenetrates, Range x0.9. CPS x1.5, LC3 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.apds: Rifle and larger rounds: (2), damage x1.3, a step down below 30mm, Range x1.5. CPS x3, LC1 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.apfsds: From .50 calibre: (2), damage x1.5, below 40mm pi++ to pi and pi+ or pi to pi-, Range x2. CPS x4, LC1 (High-Tech p. 167).
ProjectileHint.baton: From 10mm: (0.5), damage /5 crushing (double knockback over 35mm), -1 Acc, Range /5. CPS x2, LC3 (High-Tech p. 168).
ProjectileHint.beanbag: From 9mm: (0.2), damage /5 crushing (double knockback from 15mm), Acc 0, Range /8. CPS x3, LC3 (High-Tech p. 168).
ProjectileHint.sapfsds: Up to 10mm: (2), pi-, Range x1.5. CPS x2, LC2 (High-Tech p. 168).
ProjectileHint.underwaterDart: Guns built to fire underwater: impaling, and distance underwater counts x25, not x1,000. CPS x2, LC2 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.apdu: (2), damage x1.2, a step down below 20mm; incendiary through rigid DR 10+. CPS x3, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.apdsdu: (2), damage x1.5, a step down below 30mm, Range x1.5; incendiary through rigid DR 10+. CPS x4, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.apfsdsdu: From 10mm: (2), damage x1.7, below 40mm pi++ to pi+ and pi+ to pi, Range x2; incendiary through rigid DR 10+. CPS x5, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.canister: From 20mm: damage x NS, pi+ (pi++ for balls of 15mm and up), 1/2D size x5, Max size x50, RoF times NP, Rcl 1. LC3 (High-Tech pp. 172-173).
ProjectileHint.shotshell: From 5mm: damage x NS, type and divisor by shot size, 1/2D size x5, Max size x100, xNP after RoF, Rcl 1. LC3 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.buckAndBall: From 10mm: the first hit is the full-calibre ball (Range x0.9), the rest 1d+1 pi buckshot, 1/2D size x5, Max size x100. LC3 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.shrapnel: A shell of balls with a small bursting charge; the weapon's own figures, airburst included. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.duplex: Two bullets: damage x0.85, Range /2, x2 after RoF, Rcl 1. CPS x1.5, LC3 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.triplex: Three bullets: damage x0.7, Range /3, x3 after RoF, Rcl 1. CPS x1.5, LC3 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.beehive: A shell of flechettes; the weapon's own figures, no 1/2D, airburst included. CPS x5, LC1 (High-Tech p. 173).
ProjectileHint.multiFlechette: Low-powered large bores, from 10mm: damage x NS, pi-, 1/2D size x50, Max size x600, xNP after RoF, Rcl 1. CPS x4, LC3 (High-Tech p. 174).
ProjectileHint.rubberShot: From 10mm: damage x NS crushing (0.2), 1/2D size x2, Max size x10, xNP after RoF, Rcl 1. CPS x2, LC3 (High-Tech p. 174).
ProjectileHint.abf: Annular blast fragmentation; the weapon's own figures, airburst included. CPS x5, LC1 (High-Tech p. 174).
ProjectileHint.le: A black-powder shell: (0.5) on the shot and a linked blast with fragments, the blast the record's. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.saple: A small charge fused to burst inside: a follow-up internal blast with fragments. At TL5-6 it bursts only on 1d <= TL-2. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.apex: AP with a small charge in the base: (2), damage x0.7, a step down below 20mm, and a follow-up internal blast with fragments. CPS x3, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.he: High explosive: (0.5) on the shot and a linked blast with fragments, the blast the record's. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.saphe: A follow-up blast with fragments. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.saphec: Thin walls, a larger charge: a follow-up internal blast without fragments. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 169).
ProjectileHint.aphex: APHC with a charge: (2), a step down below 20mm, a follow-up internal blast with fragments. CPS x4, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.efp: From 50mm: an explosively formed penetrator, pi++ (2), and a linked blast without fragments. CPS x8, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.heat: From 20mm: a shaped charge, (10), with a linked blast without fragments. CPS x3, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.hedp: From 20mm: HEAT with fragments. CPS x4, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.hesh: From 50mm: (0.5) and a linked blast; where neither gets through, the blast spalls the inside of the armour. CPS x3, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.msheat: From 50mm: tandem shaped charges, (10), a linked blast; the precursor defeats explosive reactive armour. CPS x8, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.thermobaric: From 20mm: (0.5) and a linked blast divided by twice the distance, not three times. CPS x8, LC1 (High-Tech p. 170).
ProjectileHint.illumination: From 10mm: a flare lighting its radius (darkness no worse than -3, a signal flare's -5); it burns 1d a second on contact. CPS x5, LC4 (High-Tech p. 171).
ProjectileHint.smoke: From 10mm: (0.5) on the hit, crushing with double knockback over 35mm from a low-velocity gun; a cloud of smoke where it lands. CPS x3, LC3 (High-Tech p. 171).
ProjectileHint.tearGas: From 10mm: as smoke, with a cloud of tear gas: HT-2 against coughing and against blindness (and retching with a vomiting agent), -3 a yard to Vision. CPS x3, LC3 (High-Tech p. 171).
ProjectileHint.liquid: Low-powered smoothbores only: (0.2), half damage, crushing, Range /4, and its filler's effect. LC by filler (High-Tech pp. 171-172).
ProjectileHint.poisonGas: From 20mm: (0.5) on the shot, a follow-up crushing blast, and its filler's gas over the burst radius. Cost by filler, LC0 (High-Tech p. 172).
ProjectileHint.whitePhosphorus: From 20mm: (0.5) on the shot, a follow-up burning blast whose burning fragments go on burning every 10 seconds for a minute, and smoke. CPS x2, LC1 (High-Tech p. 172).

ProjectileRefusal.record: only a mode whose record prints the blast

MaterialHint.silver: Normal damage; cost per shot x50. In a rifled gun -1 Acc and Malf. unless a jacketed hollow-point; -3 to Armoury to handload (High-Tech p. 168).
MaterialHint.dense: Gold and other dense metals do normal damage; the GM prices them (High-Tech p. 168).
MaterialHint.veryLight: A tenth of the damage and range (High-Tech p. 168).

ProjectileUpgradeHint.airburst: Bursts over the target area: a miss scatters by the margin squared. CPS x1.5; free with shrapnel, beehive and ABF (High-Tech pp. 174-175).
ProjectileUpgradeHint.incendiary: A solid bullet (or AP, APHC from late TL6) with the incendiary modifier; not for handguns. CPS x1.5 (High-Tech p. 175).
ProjectileUpgradeHint.selfDestruct: An explosive round that destroys itself past 1/2D. CPS x1.5 (High-Tech p. 175).
ProjectileUpgradeHint.tracer: Incendiary out to 1/2D, where it burns out; +1 to skill on the turn after a long burst; gives the shooter away. CPS x1.5 (High-Tech p. 175).

ProjectileUpgradeRefusal.solidOnly: Only for solid, AP or APHC bullets.

Ammunition.VomitingHint: Mixed with a vomiting agent: HT-2 against retching too, for the time in the cloud plus five minutes a point of margin (High-Tech p. 171).
Ammunition.SmokeHint: Screening -10 to sight and visually aimed attacks, coloured -7; hot smoke (TL8) also hides from infrared and hyperspectral vision, prism smoke also blocks lasers, electromagnetic smoke also radar (High-Tech p. 171).
Ammunition.IlluminationHint: Under a parachute flare the darkness penalty is no worse than -3; under a signal flare, -5; an infrared flare (TL8) lights only for those who see infrared (High-Tech p. 171).
Ammunition.LiquidHint: Paint is LC4, a scent marker LC2 (High-Tech pp. 171-172).
Ammunition.FillerHint: The Basic Set poison the round spreads over its burst radius (High-Tech p. 172; Campaigns p. 439).
Ammunition.AreaRadiusHint: The cloud's or light's radius, as the gun's description prints it; left blank, it is asked as the round is fired.
Ammunition.AreaSecondsHint: How long the cloud or light lasts, as the description prints it; a cloud typically lingers 1-4 minutes (High-Tech p. 171).
Ammunition.HitHint: The round's own dice where the gun's description prints them (a 40mm smoke round's 1d+1, p. 143); blank for the mode's own.
Ammunition.AreaAsk: Where the round lands: the latest template you placed, or the one token targeted.
Ammunition.AreaNoPlace: No place for the cloud: place a template or target one token (the GM places areas).
Ammunition.CloudPlaced: A cloud of {radius} yards' radius, for {seconds} seconds.
Ammunition.LightPlaced: A flare lights {radius} yards round it for {seconds} seconds.
Ammunition.PrismLasers: Prism smoke blocks lasers through it.
Ammunition.GasNoDose: {name}: no dose written (the GM doses those they don't own).
Ammunition.NoFillerChosen: The round has no filler chosen.
Ammunition.PoisonDelayed: {name} is dosed; it takes effect in {seconds} s.
Ammunition.SapleBursts: The round bursts (1d: {roll}, needs {need} or less).
Ammunition.SapleDud: A dud: no blast (1d: {roll}, needed {need} or less).
Ammunition.ScentMarked: {name} reeks of the scent marker for an hour.

Power.Title: Batteries
Power.SupplyPack: one {size} battery, worn as a pack
Power.RechargeableHint: Rechargeable batteries cost at least five times as much (the prices assume throwaway ones) and can be recharged dozens of times (High-Tech p. 13).
Power.AdapterHint: Lets the gadget run on external power instead of batteries, for the cost and weight of its usual batteries (High-Tech p. 14).
Power.InverterHint: Lets gear built for external power run on batteries: at least an M battery, lasting minutes to days by the device, an L or VL longer in proportion. The inverter costs and weighs what its batteries do (High-Tech p. 14).
Power.InverterEnduranceHint: How long the device runs on the inverter's batteries, which the book leaves to the device: from a few minutes to a few days on an M battery (High-Tech p. 14).
Power.SwapHint: Batteries of another size or number: endurance in proportion to their weight, and the gadget's weight changed by the difference (High-Tech pp. 10, 13).
Power.UsedHint: Hours the gadget has run on these batteries.
Power.UsesHint: Uses spent since the batteries were changed.
Power.WeaponHint: A weapon's batteries are changed with its Reload button.
Power.ExternalHint: Plugged into building, vehicle or generator power through its adapter or inverter: it runs as long as the power lasts (High-Tech p. 14).
Power.RunHint: Hours the generator has run since its tank was filled.
Power.Tank: {amount} gal. of {fuel} a fill, for {hours} hr.
Power.Burns: {wood} lbs. of wood and {water} gal. of water an hour; {output}
Power.BurnsOrCoal: {wood} lbs. of wood (or {coal} lbs. of coal) and {water} gal. of water an hour; {output}
Power.Cranked: muscle: {fpPerHour} FP an hour, recharging about {batteryLbsPerHour} lbs. of batteries an hour
Power.PalmCrank: muscle: {crankMinutes} minutes' cranking for {runMinutes} minutes of a small gadget, no fatigue
Power.Recharger: sunlight: recharges a hand-held device's batteries in a few hours; nothing at a -1 Vision penalty or worse

Source.wind: wind: external power, none on calm days
Source.solar: sunlight: external power; nothing at a -1 Vision penalty or worse

Power.Refuelled: Filled with {amount} gal. of {fuel}, for {hours} hr.
Power.RefuelledFrom: Filled with {amount} gal. of {fuel} from the {name} carried, for {hours} hr.
Power.CrankRecharged: {hours} hr. of cranking ({fp} FP) gave the {name} back {back} hr.
Power.CrankPowered: {hours} hr. of cranking ({fp} FP) powering a device.
Power.PalmRecharged: {cranked} minutes of cranking gave the {name} back {minutes} minutes.
Power.PalmPowered: {cranked} minutes of cranking: {minutes} minutes of use.
Power.SolarDark: No power: at a {darkness} Vision penalty the panel gives nothing.
Power.SolarRecharged: Recharged the {name}'s batteries over a few hours of good sunlight.
Power.SolarPowered: Powering a hand-held device in good sunlight.
Power.DarknessRead: The light where the character stands: {darkness} to Vision (the scene's lighting).
Power.LightRead: The light where the character stands is good (the scene's lighting).
Power.TankCylinder: a {fuel} cylinder a fill, for {hours} hr.
Power.RefuelledCylinder: Fitted a fresh {fuel} cylinder, for {hours} hr.
Power.RefuelledFromCylinder: Fitted a {fuel} cylinder from the {name} carried, for {hours} hr.

Computer.Title: Computer
Computer.KindHint: A computer is one of the book's standard models; a program is rated by its Complexity (High-Tech pp. 20, 22).
Computer.ModelHint: The standard model, with its Complexity and storage at TL8. A TL6-7 computer is a model available then, built with one of the early technologies (High-Tech p. 20).
Computer.Excluded: not with the other, or not yet at its TL

Option.compactHint: TL7: twice the cost, half the weight.
