Option.hardenedHint: TL7: +3 HT against EMP, microwaves and the like; twice the cost and weight. A vacuum-tube computer already is.
Option.highCapacityHint: TL7: runs half again as many programs at once, at 1.5 times the cost.
Option.fastHint: TL8: +1 Complexity at 20 times the cost. Not with Slow.
Option.slowHint: TL8: -1 Complexity at a twentieth the cost. Not with Fast.
Option.mechanicalHint: Early technology, TL6: -5 Complexity; storage in bytes.
Option.vacuumTubeHint: Early technology, early TL7: -4 Complexity, hardened at no extra cost; storage in kilobytes.
Option.transistorHint: Early technology, TL7: -3 Complexity; storage in kilobytes.

Computer.Figures: Complexity {complexity}, {storage} {unit}. Runs {own} programs of Complexity {complexity} at once, or {below} one level below.

Problem.belowZero: Its Complexity comes to less than 0: design a larger computer.
Problem.needsEarly: A TL{tl} computer must be built with one of the early technologies.
Problem.modelTooLate: This model isn't built yet at TL{built}.

Computer.CompactCells: Compact: half the batteries and half the operating time.
Computer.Hardened: Hardened: +{bonus} HT against EMP, microwaves and the like.
Computer.ComplexityHint: The least Complexity a computer must have to run the program (High-Tech p. 22).
Computer.DifficultyHint: The difficulty of the skill a software tool is for: an Easy skill needs one level less Complexity for each grade (High-Tech p. 22).
Computer.RunsOnHint: Which of the character's computers the program is running on.
Computer.MassMarketHint: Software sold to a huge user base costs as little as a tenth of the table's price (High-Tech p. 22).
Computer.TablePrice: ${cost}: Complexity {complexity} at TL{tl} on the Program Cost Table.
Computer.Unavailable: The Program Cost Table has no Complexity {complexity} program at TL{tl}.

Tool.none: Too simple for {skills}: at TL7+ a skill that needs software takes at least a basic program, Complexity {basic}.
Tool.basic: A basic tool for {skills}, no bonus: good needs Complexity {good}, fine {fine}.
Tool.good: A good tool for {skills} (+1); fine needs Complexity {fine}.

Computer.TooComplex: Too complex for this computer to run.
Computer.OverloadedHint: More programs than the computer runs at once: two of its own Complexity, ten times as many per level below.

ComputerUse.Title: Using the computer
ComputerUse.OperatingSystemHint: The operating system it runs. A user unfamiliar with it takes -2 to skill with the computer (High-Tech p. 20).
ComputerUse.TerminalHint: The terminal it is used through. A portable terminal costs -1 and a datapad -2 on demanding work, at the GM's option (High-Tech p. 21); the penalty goes on every roll made with the computer while it is set here.
ComputerUse.Familiarity: Under the familiarity rule, a roll made with this computer or a program on it takes -2 for each of its operating system, its type (the computer's name) and the program the character's familiarities don't list (High-Tech p. 20).

Books.Title: Reference work
Books.ManualHint: Followed while doing a task, a suitable manual lets its reader use the skill at the attribute default, even with no default; the GM decides what counts (High-Tech p. 17).
Books.SkillHint: The skill the manual or library covers, as the character sheet names it.
Books.Default: Followed: {skill} at {attribute}{penalty}; extra time can win back at most that penalty.
Books.OccultHint: A library for magical research, Hidden Lore and the like may cost 100 times as much (High-Tech p. 18).
Books.ExtendsHint: At the GM's option, a good or fine library's bonus also counts for the skill it covers, not only for Research on it (High-Tech p. 18).
Books.Library: {grade}: {modifier} to Research on its subject. Outside it, the Research roll takes the scope modifiers; as a curriculum, it can teach the skill (High-Tech p. 18).
Books.FollowHint: {skill} at {attribute}{penalty}. Time spent adds its bonus, up to that penalty.
Books.OwnBetter: {name}'s own {skill} ({level}) is already as good as following the manual.

Tools.Title: Tools (High-Tech)
Tools.KitTooltip: What size of kit this is: a mini-tool kit, a portable kit or a workshop (High-Tech p. 24). Set its skill and specialty in the item's skills.

KitLine.mini: A mini-tool kit: -2, for its own specialty only.
KitLine.portable: A portable kit: basic equipment for its own specialty, -2 for the skill's other specialties.
KitLine.workshop: A workshop: +2 for its own specialty; another specialty or a close craft -2, a distant craft -5.

Tools.VehicleTonsHint: A vehicle mechanic's or armourer's kit or shop does major repairs on vehicles up to 10 tons; one for larger vehicles costs and weighs (tons)/10 times as much (High-Tech p. 24).
Tools.VehicleLine: Built for vehicles up to {tons} tons: cost and weight x{multiplier}.
Tools.CloseCraftsHint: Skills this shop counts as reasonably close crafts for, at -2, separated by commas (High-Tech p. 24).
Tools.DistantCraftsHint: Skills this shop is only barely better than nothing for, at -5, separated by commas (High-Tech p. 24).
Tools.LightCraftHint: A kit for an art or light craft (drawing, painting, sewing): a quarter of the cost, a tenth of the weight (High-Tech p. 24).
Tools.WrongKitReason: a kit or workshop made for another specialty or craft (High-Tech p. 24)
Tools.SetupLine: Takes at least {time} to set up or pack (High-Tech p. 50).
Tools.PartsLine: Makes {pounds} lb. of parts an hour from a CAD project file (High-Tech p. 29).
Tools.WorkHint: Roll the damage for each second (or each use) the tool is worked against the thing, and apply it to the thing's DR and HP (High-Tech pp. 25-30).

Against.rope: rope, barbed wire and thin cable

Tools.StRollLine: Needs an ST{modifier} roll to use.
Tools.StRollHint: The user must make this ST roll for the tool to do its damage (High-Tech p. 25).
Tools.ReadiesLine: Needs {readies} Ready maneuver(s) before each use.
Tools.ReadiesWaivedLine: Needs {readies} Ready maneuver(s) between uses, unless the user has ST {st}.
Tools.NoReadiesNeeded: {name} needs no Ready maneuvers in these hands.
Tools.ReadiesRefusal: {name} isn't ready: {done} of {needed} Ready maneuvers done (High-Tech pp. 29-30).
Tools.GlassLine: Cuts a disk of glass on a DX or Forced Entry roll, at {penalty} in a realistic game.
Tools.GlassHint: A DX or Forced Entry roll, the better. Failure is a noisy break; a critical failure also cuts the hand for 1d-2. In a realistic game the roll is at -6 (High-Tech p. 26).
Tools.GlassCinematic: Cinematic: the cutter works as in the movies
Tools.GlassDone: A clean disk of glass lifts out.
Tools.GlassCutHand: The glass breaks, noisily, and cuts the hand.
Tools.TapeItemLine: Tapes up a prisoner, who breaks free with ST-3 or Escape.
Tools.TapeTarget: Target the one token to tape up.
Tools.TapeLine: {taper} tapes up {captive}, who breaks free with ST-3 or Escape (High-Tech p. 26).
Tools.RescueHint: As a rescue tool, a chainsaw is used with Forced Entry (High-Tech p. 27).
Tools.HardHint: Against concrete, metal and the like a chainsaw has an (0.5) armor divisor; a blow that fails to penetrate may stall the saw or snap its chain (High-Tech p. 27).
Tools.CarbideHint: Double the cost: no (0.5) divisor and no stalls or snaps against hard material (High-Tech p. 28).
Tools.CarbideLine: A carbide chain: full damage against hard material.
Tools.CarbideEdgeHint: A TL7+ blade with carbide or diamond teeth lasts longer and gets +{bonus} to damage (High-Tech p. 25).
Tools.HardLine: (0.5) against concrete and metal; a blow that fails to penetrate rolls 1d: 3-5 stalls, 6 snaps the chain.
Tools.StalledLine: Stalled: restart it before it cuts again.
Tools.SnappedLine: The chain has snapped: it needs repair.
Tools.StalledRefusal: {name} has stalled and must be restarted.
Tools.SnappedRefusal: {name}'s chain has snapped; it must be repaired first.
Tools.MishapNone: Failed to penetrate: 1d came up {roll}, and nothing happens.
Tools.MishapStall: Failed to penetrate: 1d came up {roll}, and the saw stalls. It must be restarted.
Tools.MishapSnapLashes: Failed to penetrate: 1d came up {roll}, and the chain snaps and whips round at the wielder (1d cutting).
Tools.MishapSnapBreaks: Failed to penetrate: 1d came up {roll}, and the chain snaps: the saw is out until repaired.
Tools.NailGunLine: Fired as a weapon, with its safety held back: Guns (Pistol){penalty}, or DX-4.
Tools.NailGunHint: A nail gun is fired at Guns (Pistol)-4 or DX-4 (High-Tech p. 28).
Tools.PropaneLine: DR {dr}: non-crushing damage that gets through near a flame ruptures it into a fireball, {damage} burn ex, fragments {fragments} cut.

HazardLine.injury: Does {damage} HP{pace} to what is inside it.

Tools.HeatHint: From {from} to {to}, by how hot it is (High-Tech p. 32).
Tools.LeadWorse: {name} has lost half their HP to lead: worse symptoms now, as the GM chooses: Bad Temper (15) or Laziness, or spells of agony, daze or retching, and a lost appetite. More failed rolls bring seizures and coma (High-Tech p. 33).

Flame.NoteHint: A large-area injury that can set clothes alight; unsealed DR at a fifth. The fuel burns on for 2d x 5 seconds (1d x 5 past 1/2D), 1d burn a second. Even plywood cover stops the jet. The GM may call for a Fright Check (High-Tech pp. 178-179).
Flame.SheetLine: Large-area injury; unsealed DR at a fifth; the fuel burns on for 2d x 5 seconds at 1d a second. DR 2 against a shot at the weapon.
Flame.UnthickenedHint: Plain fuel, such as gasoline, in a TL7+ flamethrower: half the Range (High-Tech p. 178).
Flame.FifthDr: Unsealed DR protects at a fifth against a flamethrower (High-Tech p. 178).
Flame.Title: Burning fuel
Flame.Burns: The fuel burns on {name} for {seconds} seconds ({dice}), 1d burn a second.
Flame.BurnedOut: The fuel on {name} has burned out.

Sweep.Label: Sweep an area (yards wide)
Sweep.NeedsAllOut: Sweeping an area is an All-Out Attack.
Sweep.Note: Swept over {width} yards: damage and burning time divided by {width}; roll to hit each target.

Malfunction.noIgnition: No ignition: sprayed with unlit fuel
Malfunction.Repair: Each attempt takes {seconds} seconds and an Armoury (Small Arms) or IQ-based Liquid Projector roll; a critical failure is an explosion.
Malfunction.explosionRepair: Everything within two yards of the firer takes a second's damage.

Tank.Note: DR 2 against a shot at the weapon (High-Tech p. 179).
Tank.Target: {name} (-4 at a backpack whose carrier faces you)
Tank.explodesLine: Damage got through {name}'s DR: 1d rolled {roll}, and the tank explodes!
Tank.disabledLine: Damage got through {name}'s DR: 1d rolled {roll}, and it is disabled.

Spray.NoteHint: Must hit the face to work; the wide jet gives +{bonus} to hit it (High-Tech p. 180).
Spray.UntilWashed: until washed off with plenty of water

NoteHint.dazzle: A cone: only those looking toward the laser are affected, and DR has no effect. Blind for minutes equal to the margin of failure (High-Tech p. 181).
NoteHint.blinding: Only a target looking toward the laser is affected. Failure cripples the eyes; a failure by 10 or more is for good (High-Tech p. 181).

Laser.BlindedLine: {name}'s eyes are crippled: roll for how long as for any crippling injury (Campaigns p. 422).
Laser.BlindedForGoodLine: {name} failed by 10 or more: the eyes are crippled for good.

Explosives.EnclosedNote: Enclosed: everyone inside takes x{times} damage. Anyone behind a door or window that bursts takes the fragments (High-Tech p. 181).
Explosives.DetonateHint: Packed against the target, the charge does it the most its dice could; set nearby, the share its distance leaves. A shaped charge with a metal liner divides the structure's DR by 10 (High-Tech pp. 182-183).
Explosives.Shaped: Shaped charge with a metal liner
Explosives.Inert: {name} doesn't go off: the batch is inert.
Explosives.AnfoFailed: {name} doesn't go off (home-made ANFO takes an Explosives (Demolition)+2 roll).
Explosives.PlanHint: The formulas take the size of the job in feet or inches, as the book gives them; fill in the ones the job reads (High-Tech p. 182).

Jobs.crater: A mine or crater (depth in feet)
Jobs.timberBored: A timber, charges in bored holes
Jobs.timberWrapped: A timber, charges looped around it
Jobs.brickWall: A hole in a brick wall
Jobs.ironPlate: A hole in an iron plate
Jobs.steelPlate: A hole in a steel plate

Explosives.Tamped: Tamped into a bored hole (half the explosive)
Explosives.ShapedJob: Shaped charge (half the explosive, not with tamping)
Explosives.PlanShaped: Shaped charge: half the usual weight.
Explosives.PlanShort: There are only {have} lb. here: not enough.
Explosives.ShapedRemember: Shaped charge at TL6: remembering the effect
Explosives.ShapedMake: Shaped charge at TL6: making one
Explosives.PlanSuccess: Set right: the charge does the job.
Explosives.PlanSuccessShort: Set right -- but there isn't enough explosive for the job.
Explosives.PlanFailed: The charge is set wrong: it still does the object some damage, but not the job.
Explosives.PlanShapedForgotten: The shaped-charge effect doesn't come to mind: set it as an ordinary charge.
Explosives.PlanCriticalFailure: Critical failure: most likely no explosion at all -- but anything can happen (the GM's call).
Explosives.Jolted: {name} is jolted: 3d rolled {roll}, and it goes off on {number}+.
Explosives.JoltedByBlow: The blow jolts {name}: 3d rolled {roll}, and it goes off on {number}+.
Explosives.ShockOnHint: The 3d roll a jolt sets it off on: 10 for impure nitro, the GM's number for old, sweating dynamite; 0 for the explosive's own -- 12 for nitroglycerin, never for anything else (High-Tech pp. 184-185).
Explosives.HomeMadeHint: What the roll to make the batch left it: unstable (-4 to Explosives rolls to use it), weak (half damage), smelly (found by an unmodified Smell roll) or inert (High-Tech p. 186).
Explosives.Stable: Stable: a jolt won't set it off.
Explosives.ShockLine: A jolt sets it off on {number}+ on 3d.

SkimOutcome.half: Failure by 2: half of {name} blows up!
SkimOutcome.all: Failure by 3 or more: all of {name} blows up -- the worse the failure, the closer the cook was.

Explosives.CookBlowsUp: Critical failure: the whole batch of {name} goes off!
Explosives.CookLabel: {name} goes off in the making ({pounds} lb.)

Cooked.sound: The batch of {name} comes out right.
Cooked.unstable: The batch of {name} is unstable: -4 to every Explosives roll to use it.
Cooked.weak: The batch of {name} is weak: half damage.
Cooked.smelly: The batch of {name} is smelly: an unmodified Smell roll finds it.
Cooked.inert: The batch of {name} won't work: it is inert.

Explosives.FlashLooking: Only if they were looking toward the blast (High-Tech p. 182).
Explosives.TinnitusLine: {name} is stunned, with tinnitus: Hearing -{penalty} {lasting}, then HT each turn to recover.
Explosives.DeafenedLine: {name} is stunned and deafened {lasting}, then HT each turn to recover; a critical failure on it leaves them deaf for good.
Explosives.DazzledLine: {name} is stunned and dazzled: Vision -{penalty} {lasting}, then HT each turn to recover.
Explosives.BlindedLine: {name} is stunned and blinded {lasting}, then HT each turn to recover; a critical failure on it leaves them blind for good.

Thermite.Title: Burning thermite
Thermite.Hint: 3d burn a second to whatever it touches, every 10 points taking 1 off the DR there; about 25 seconds a pound. Water won't put it out (High-Tech p. 188).
Thermite.Lit: Thermite burns on {name}'s {location} for {seconds} seconds: 3d burn a second.
Thermite.BurnedOut: The thermite on {name} has burned out.
Thermite.Sparks: Sparks and heat: {near} burn a second within a yard, {far} at two yards (no harm to DR).
Thermite.Through: The thermite burns through {label} in {seconds} of its {of} seconds: {injury} injury against HP {hp}; its DR there went from {dr} to {drLeft}.
Thermite.NotThrough: The thermite burns out on {label} after {of} seconds: {injury} injury against HP {hp}; its DR there went from {dr} to {drLeft}.
Thermite.NoObject: Choose an object with some HP.
Thermite.NotOwner: Only the GM, or whoever owns the target, can set it burning.

Napalm.Title: Burning napalm
Napalm.Clings: Napalm clings to {name} and burns for {seconds} seconds, 1d-1 a second; only immersion or burial puts it out, and it eats the air around them.
Napalm.BurnedOut: The napalm on {name} has burned out.

Sensor.Title: Comms and sensors
Sensor.CommModeHint: A receive-only radio is 10% of the cost and 20% of the weight (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.CodeOnlyHint: Sends Morse code (or similar) only: half the cost, and a lower bandwidth that stretches range (High-Tech p. 38).
Sensor.DirectionFinderHint: Fixes a broadcasting radio's position in a Quick Contest of Electronics Operation (Communications) with its operator; five times the cost (High-Tech pp. 38-39).
Sensor.InterceptHint: Eavesdropping gear, using Electronics Operation (EW); ECCM radios can spoof it. Five times the cost (High-Tech pp. 39, 209).
Sensor.RadiotelephoneHint: Routes a radio linked to a phone line over the telephone system; x1.5 cost (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.EccmHint: Frequency-hopping: no interference from selective jammers with a synchronized radio (none against noise jamming), and detected at 1.5 times its range at most. From TL7, twice the cost (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.GpsHint: A GPS unit and map display: two such radios show each other's position. From TL8, twice the cost (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.SatelliteUplinkHint: Reaches any other radio in the world by satellite. Medium and large radios only, from TL8; twice the cost (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.LongAntennaHint: Doubles the radio's range; 5 minutes to erect and an Electronics Operation (Communications) roll to set up. A quarter of the radio's cost and weight (High-Tech p. 39).
Sensor.WideBeamHint: Broadcasts rather than beaming: half a mile, no line of sight needed indoors, but it can be intercepted (High-Tech p. 40).
Sensor.MilitaryHint: Built-in encryption and double the range, at three times the cost and weight (High-Tech p. 40).
Sensor.TacticalHint: A military targeting mode: tracks up to 10 targets and, with an Aim, locks on for +3 to hit one with an aimed attack. Five times the cost (High-Tech pp. 45-46).
Sensor.LpiHint: Halves the range; the halved range is detected at 1.5 times rather than twice. Five times the cost (High-Tech p. 46).
Sensor.ImagingHint: High-frequency sonar that renders fine detail and profiles the sea floor, at a tenth of the range. Five times the cost, twice the weight (High-Tech p. 46).
Sensor.LensHoodHint: Partly shades the lens: +4 to the Stealth roll against lens shine (High-Tech p. 47).
Sensor.IrIlluminatedHint: An infrared source lights the scene within its range: two more levels of Night Vision. On gear with its own illuminator, it is switched on, and its wearer is a light to night-vision gear and thermographs (High-Tech pp. 47-48).
Sensor.SearchHint: A simple hydrophone for research, fishing or perimeter watch: a tenth of the cost, LC4, and no +3 to hit (High-Tech p. 49).
Sensor.TelegraphLine: Messages go in code: Electronics Operation (Communications) to send or read one; a failure isn't understood, a critical failure is badly misunderstood. Enciphered messages are at -4 (High-Tech p. 36).
Sensor.RadioRange: Range {range} at TL{tl} to a radio of the same size; from the shorter range, x3, x10 or x30 to a radio one to three sizes larger.
Sensor.LargeSetUp: Setting up takes about 15 minutes and an Electronics Operation (Communications) roll.
Sensor.UplinkLine: Satellite uplink: reaches any radio in the world.
Sensor.Detected: Its transmissions can be detected out to {range}.
Sensor.RadioInUse: Stretching range: Electronics Operation (Communications) at -1 per 10% added, to double. A tenth of the range in a city or underground, and a tenth again for live video.
Sensor.SlowedData: Repeating slowed data stretches range: x{quarter} at a quarter speed, x{hundredth} at 1/100, x{tenThousandth} at 1/10,000.
Sensor.DirectionFinderLine: Direction finder: a Quick Contest to fix a transmitter (row button).
Sensor.InterceptLine: Radio intercept: Electronics Operation (EW) to eavesdrop (row button).
Sensor.EccmLine: ECCM: selective jammers can't interfere with a synchronized radio; noise jamming still can.
Sensor.GpsLine: GPS: two radios with it show each other's position.
Sensor.RadiotelephoneLine: Radiotelephone: routes calls over a linked phone line.
Sensor.LaserRange: Range {range} with the narrow beam: line of sight, and only someone in the beam can intercept or jam it.
Sensor.WideBeamLine: Wide beam: half a mile, and it can be intercepted.
Sensor.DivecomLine: Fast currents and thermal layers can cut range to a tenth; hydrophones and sonar pick up its signals easily.
Sensor.ActiveRange: Range {range} at TL{tl}; -2 per doubling beyond. {skill} to detect or resolve detail.
Sensor.Emissions: Scans a {arc}-degree arc in front; its emissions can be detected out to {range}.
Sensor.SonarLine: Ambient noise gives -1 to -6; a very loud noise can jam or fool it. Ultrahearing detects it.
Sensor.RadarLine: Unaffected by darkness, smoke or weather; it can't see over the horizon, through solid objects or underwater, and can't tell a still target from ground clutter unless it saw it move.
Sensor.GprLine: Twenty times the range in ice, a tenth in concrete or rock; Electronics Operation (Scientific) reads soil, bedrock or buried items.
Sensor.ThruWallLine: Sees through a wall up to a foot thick to a person 20 yards beyond; under a foot through concrete.
Sensor.TacticalRadar: Tactical: tracks up to 10 targets, identifies their general class out to {range}, and locks on for +3 to hit.
Sensor.TacticalSonar: Tactical: tracks and identifies up to 10 targets, and locks on for +3 to hit.
Sensor.Magnification: x{magnification} magnification: Telescopic Vision {levels} while worn.
Sensor.NightVision: Night Vision {level} while worn (none against total darkness).
Sensor.NightVisionLit: Night Vision {level} while worn, only with an IR illuminator lighting the scene.
Sensor.Thermograph: Infravision while worn: sees warm targets even in total darkness, {spot} to Vision to spot them, {tracking} to Tracking a trail under an hour old, {distinguish} to tell objects of like size and shape apart.
Sensor.WarmUpFast: Ready in 3-5 seconds (an early TL8 model needs 1-2 minutes to cool).
Sensor.WarmUpSlow: Needs 1-2 minutes to cool down after switching on.
Sensor.Imposed: While in use: Colorblindness, No Depth Perception and No Peripheral Vision.
Sensor.Mounted: A camera or vehicle sensor: not worn as a sense.
Sensor.ProtectedVisionLine: Coated lenses: Protected Vision against laser light.
Sensor.StabilizedLine: Stabilized: cancels up to -{penalty} in movement penalties when observing (the GM applies it).
Sensor.LensShine: On a bright day its glint can be seen on a Vision roll; avoiding it takes a Stealth roll (row button).
Sensor.LensShineHooded: On a bright day its glint can be seen on a Vision roll; avoiding it takes a Stealth roll at {bonus} (row button).
Sensor.Hydrophone: {bonus} to detect with Electronics Operation (Sonar) at TL{tl} (row button); a fix gives +{identify} to identify, +{shadow} to shadow and +{hit} to hit with an aimed attack.
Sensor.SearchHydrophone: {bonus} to detect with Electronics Operation (Sonar) at TL{tl} (row button); a fix gives +{identify} to identify and +{shadow} to shadow, but no bonus to hit.
Sensor.HydrophoneHears: Detects sonar and underwater communicators at twice their range.
Sensor.SoundDetector: +{bonus} to Electronics Operation (Sensors) to analyze and identify a sound, or to locate one (row button). Works only in air.
Sensor.DirectionalMic: Amplifies a sound x{factor}: Parabolic Hearing {levels} while worn.
Sensor.CommPick: Select one character's token and target the other's.
Sensor.NoPair: They carry no radios or communicators of the same kind.
Sensor.UrbanLine: Urban or underground: a tenth of the range.
Sensor.AudioVisualLine: Real-time video: a tenth of the range.
Sensor.RoughWaterLine: Rough water: a tenth of the range.
Sensor.UplinkReach: A satellite uplink reaches any radio in the world.
Sensor.ReceiveOnly: {name} is receive-only: it can listen but not answer.
Sensor.OutOfRange: Beyond double the range: they can't reach each other.
Sensor.Stretch: Stretching the range: Electronics Operation (Communications) at {modifier}.
Sensor.SweepPick: Select the character with the sensor; target what they're scanning.
Sensor.ArcMiss: The target is outside the sensor's {arc}-degree arc: no roll.
Sensor.LockPick: Target what the sensor locks onto.
Sensor.Locked: The {sensor} locks onto {target}: +3 to aimed ranged attacks at it, on top of any targeting software.

Telegraphy.fake: Fake another operator's fist (vs. the recipient)
Telegraphy.sendResult: Success: the message is sent or read correctly. Failure: it isn't understood. Critical failure: it seems fine but is badly misunderstood.
Telegraphy.recognizeResult: Success: the operator is recognized by his fist.
Telegraphy.tapResult: Success: the tap listens in, or sends a false message, unnoticed.

Fix.general: A fix: the transmitter's general distance and direction.
Fix.exact: A fix: the transmitter's exact location.
Fix.again: The GM may allow another try about once a minute.

Sensor.Avoiding: The operator is avoiding interception (Quick Contest)
Sensor.EccmSpoofs: {name} has ECCM: it can spoof the intercept.
Sensor.FixSearch: A fix: the target's position, heading, rough size and class; +{identify} to identify it and +{shadow} to shadow it.
Sensor.Triangulate: Pinning the source down takes three sites each with its own gear: three successes, or a success at one and a critical success at another. Success finds a 100-decibel source at 10 miles to within two yards.
Sensor.HeatTrail: {name} (a heat trail under an hour old)
Sensor.HydrophoneFix: A fix: the target's position, heading, rough size and class; +{identify} to identify it, +{shadow} to shadow it and +{hit} to hit it with an aimed attack.

Survival.Title: Survival gear
Survival.CampingHint: Tick while the character is camping in freezing weather: the cold roll takes the best shelter or sleeping gear they carry, or -5 with none (High-Tech p. 56).
Survival.ShelterItem: {modifier} to the cold roll while camping out, its quality added ({none} with no shelter at all).
Survival.FireItem: +{least} to +{most} to the DX-based Survival roll to build a fire, only rolled in wet weather, high wind and the like.
Survival.FireHint: A DX-based Survival roll, with the starter's bonus (most give +5 to +10) and what the weather does to it.
Survival.ForagingItem: Up to {rolls} Fishing or Survival rolls a day for food (Foraging, p. B427).
Survival.TrapItem: ST {st}: strikes for thrust+{adds} crushing at that ST, and its victim breaks free against it.
Survival.TrapTarget: Target the one character caught in the trap.
Survival.KitItem: Made for its Survival specialty: -1 in a similar environment, -2 in a very different one, -3 on water for a land kit (or on land for a water one) or between Urban Survival and the wild.
Survival.SimilarHint: The Survival specialties this kit counts as similar to its own, for -1 instead of -2 (the book's example: an arctic kit in the mountains). Separate them with commas.
Survival.WrongKitReason: a survival kit for another environment (High-Tech p. 58)
Survival.FilterItem: In use: +{bonus} to HT against a disease caught by drinking; it doesn't remove salt.
Survival.DesalinatorItem: A cup of fresh water for {minutes} minutes' pumping and {fp} FP.
Survival.DesalinatorItemLarge: A quart of fresh water for {minutes} minutes' pumping and {fp} FP.
Survival.LargeHint: A quart for the pumping instead of a cup, at three times the cost and weight (High-Tech p. 59).
Survival.PumpedCup: {name} pumps for {minutes} minutes ({fp} FP): a cup of fresh water.
Survival.PumpedQuart: {name} pumps for {minutes} minutes ({fp} FP): a quart of fresh water.
Survival.StillItem: A Survival roll to set it up and gather the day's water: up to a quart.
Survival.StillWater: Up to a quart of drinkable water today.
Survival.StillNothing: No water from the still today.
Survival.SignalItem: In use: +{bonus} to a rescuer's Vision roll to spot the user, given line of sight.
Survival.JacketItem: Worn: +{drowning} to Swimming rolls to avoid drowning, {race} in a Quick Contest of Swimming.
Survival.CorkItem: Cork blocks: {penalty} to the Swimming roll against injury on first entering the water.
Survival.FinsItem: Worn: Move {move} on land. Each fin takes a Ready maneuver to put on or take off.
Survival.DyeItem: Released: +{bonus} to Vision rolls to spot it for about {minutes} minutes; it spreads in 3d seconds.
Survival.DyeReleased: {name} releases the dye: +{bonus} to Vision rolls to spot them for about {minutes} minutes, once it has spread (3d seconds).
Survival.ChuteItem: Rated for {rated} lbs.; opens {yards} yards after the ripcord is pulled. {don} seconds to put on, {doff} to take off.
Survival.ChuteItemUnrated: No rated weight printed; opens {yards} yards after the ripcord is pulled. {don} seconds to put on, {doff} to take off.
Survival.ChuteDescentItem: Comes down at {speed} yards a second, 1 more per 50 lbs. over its rating; at 120% of it the chute fails.
Survival.NauseaItem: The jumper rolls HT{modifier} against nausea.
Survival.CargoChuteItem: Holds up to {rated} lbs.; comes down at {speed} yards a second, drifting with the wind.
Survival.JumpHint: The height above the ground when the ripcord is pulled, and the weight the chute carries (the jumper and their gear). The canopy is open {yards} yards later.
Survival.ChuteFails: {load} lbs. is 120% or more of the chute's {rated}: it fails.
Survival.HitFirst: The ground comes before the canopy has opened ({yards} yards): half the fall's velocity, {velocity} yards a second.
Survival.Opens: The canopy is open {yards} yards after the ripcord.
Survival.Descent: It comes down at {speed} yards a second ({load} lbs. of its {rated}).
Survival.DescentOver: It comes down at {speed} yards a second: {load} lbs. is over its {rated}.
Survival.DescentUnrated: It comes down at {speed} yards a second.
Survival.Flies: It flies rather than drops (rated for {rated} lbs.); see its vehicle statistics.
Survival.FallLanding: {name} hits the ground at {velocity} yards a second
Survival.HardLanding: {name} lands hard at {velocity} yards a second
Survival.LandingHint: Rolled where the GM rules the landing hurts: the ground was reached too soon, the chute failed, or the Parachuting roll went wrong.
Survival.DeathFromAboveRefusal: Only on Move and Attack, coming down under a canopy.
Survival.DeathFromAboveLine: Parachuting is lower than the weapon's skill
Survival.DeathFromAboveNote: Death from Above: the lower of Parachuting and the weapon's skill, on Move and Attack (High-Tech p. 61).
Survival.SnackItem: Counts as a decent meal when resting: +{fp} FP (tick the meal on the Rest dialog).
Survival.SportsDrinkItem: Counts as a decent meal when resting (+{fp} FP), and as a quart of water for the day's rations.
Survival.SnackEaten: {name} has a {item}: it counts as a decent meal on the next rest, +{fp} FP.
Survival.DrinkWater: It also counts as a quart of water for the day's rations.

Ordnance.Primed: Primes {count}: {seconds} seconds putting grenade and detonator together.
Ordnance.FuseFitted: Fits the fuse to {count}: {seconds} seconds (five Readies each).

Armed.pin: Pulls the pin on the {name} (Ready maneuvers: {readies}). The fuse starts when the handle flies off.
Armed.string: Pulls the cord on the {name} (Ready maneuvers: {readies}). The fuse is burning.

Ordnance.NotPrimed: The {name} isn't primed: prime it first (10 seconds a grenade at TL6-8).
Ordnance.NotArmed: The {name} isn't armed: pull the pin, pull the cord or light the fuse first (a Ready maneuver).
Ordnance.NoLightingInRain: A fuse can't be lit in rain.
Ordnance.Cooking: The handle flies off: the fuse ({fuse}) is burning. Wait, then throw.
Ordnance.Impact: Impact fuse: it goes off where it lands.
Ordnance.ImpactDropped: Impact fuse: dropped, it goes off at the thrower's feet.
Ordnance.FuseUnknown: The fuse is the GM's to time.
Ordnance.FuseLeft: {burned} seconds of fuse gone before the throw: it goes off in {least}-{most} seconds.
Ordnance.ThrowBack: Long enough for a foe to pick it up (a Ready) and throw it back (p. B410).
Ordnance.NoThrowBack: Too little fuse left for anyone to throw it back.
Ordnance.Dropped: Critical failure: the {name} is dropped at the thrower's feet.
Ordnance.DroppedPickUp: There is time to pick it up again (a Ready) and throw it.
Ordnance.DroppedNoTime: There is no time to pick it up.
Ordnance.InHand: {name} held the {grenade} too long: it goes off in the hand.
Ordnance.BoobyTrapRoll: Rigging the {name} as a booby trap
Ordnance.BoobyTrapSet: The {name} is rigged on a tripwire ({minutes} minutes' work).
Ordnance.BoobyTrapFailed: The {name} isn't rigged right ({minutes} minutes spent).
Ordnance.ImproviseFuse: Make the fuse from scratch too
Ordnance.ImproviseHint: Explosives (Demolition) and 10 minutes a grenade; making a fuse is Explosives (Demolition)+2.
Ordnance.ImproviseFailed: The {name} is a dud ({minutes} minutes spent).

Engine.Title: Molotov through the engine grating
Engine.Hint: A hit through an unprotected engine grating is a vital-area hit, at {penalty} to hit. The vehicle rolls HT at once and every 3 seconds until the fire burns out.
Engine.Burns: The fire in {vehicle}'s engine burns for {seconds} seconds.
Engine.destroyed: {vehicle}'s engine catches fire: it is destroyed.

Ordnance.CloudPlaced: Smoke fills a {radius}-yard radius for {seconds} seconds.
Ordnance.CloudNoPlace: No scene or spot to put the cloud on: place a template or target a token.
Ordnance.FlashbangStunned: {name} is stunned: recovery rolls are at HT-5.

Mine.AntiLifting: Anti-lifting fuse ({penalty}; any failure sets it off)
Mine.TaskHint: Placing: Explosives (Demolition)+4, Soldier or Traps+2; improvised: Explosives (Demolition)-2. Probing: Explosives (EOD) or Soldier-5. Disarming: Explosives (EOD). A metal detector finds some buried mines, but not plastic or wooden ones.
Mine.Pdm: An M86 PDM puts out its tripwires after 25 seconds and is armed {arms} seconds after it is dropped; left alone it destroys itself after {hours} hours.
Mine.BoundingCard: The burst is five feet up: whoever drops flat at once takes none of its fragments (Dodge and Drop, p. B377). Drop them before the fragments are applied.
Mine.Flat: {name} is flat on the ground: the fragments pass overhead.
Mine.BoundingHint: Its fragments come from Set off, on their own card: whoever is flat on the ground takes none.
Mine.PelletsHint: At basic skill {skill}; Set off resolves everyone targeted, nearest first, until the pellets are spent.
Mine.NoTargets: Target those in the mine's cone first.
Mine.VolleyHint: Yards from the mine to each (the mine's token, where it has one). Past {max} yards nothing is hit.
Mine.DodgeHint: A successful Dodge stops one hit, plus one per point of margin.

Rifle.ReadyHint: Fitting a launcher takes {launcher} seconds, loading the blank {blank}, putting the grenade on {grenade}.
Rifle.NoRifle: No rifle to put it on.
Rifle.LauncherOn: The {launcher} is fitted: the rifle can't fire normally until it comes off.
Rifle.Blank: Loaded with a blank to launch it.
Rifle.BulletTrap: Fired with an ordinary round, trapped in its tail.
Rifle.LauncherFitted: A grenade launcher is fitted: the rifle can't fire normally until it comes off (5 seconds).
Rifle.NotReadied: The {name} isn't on a rifle: ready it on one first.
Rifle.InsideMinimum: {yards} yards is inside the {minimum}-yard minimum range: the grenade won't arm. Fire the dud row ({damage} cr) for that.
Rifle.DudHint: Inside its minimum range, or failing to go off, a rifle grenade does 1d+1 crushing and nothing more (High-Tech p. 194).

Nuclear.EmpHint: HT{modifier}({divisor}) against the targeted: the Electrical roll HT, and each ticked piece of gear its object HT, at +1 per 2 DR. What fails is out until repaired.
Nuclear.NoTargets: Target those the pulse or fallout reaches first.
Nuclear.EmpDown: {name}: rolled {roll} against {target}, knocked out until repaired.
Nuclear.EmpResisted: {name}: rolled {roll} against {target}, shrugs off the pulse.
Nuclear.GearOut: {name}'s {gear}: rolled {roll} against {target}, knocked out until repaired (at {penalty}).
Nuclear.UseRepair: Knocked out by EMP: use its Repair (EMP) action.
Nuclear.FalloutHint: Only a ground burst leaves fallout. Everyone targeted takes the dose, through their protection factor.
Nuclear.Footprint: At {kt} kilotons the footprint is {length} yards long and {width} wide, drifting downwind.
Nuclear.Rate: {rate} rads an hour, {hours} hours after the blast.

Expedition.Title: Expedition gear
Expedition.PlacedLine: Lit and set down on the map.

KindLine.lantern: Breaks if dropped on hard ground (HT 6); 30-60 seconds to relight.
KindLine.glassLantern: Breaks if dropped on hard ground (HT 6), starting a 1-yard fire; 30-60 seconds to relight.
KindLine.kerosene: Breaks if dropped on hard ground (HT 6) but douses itself; 30-60 seconds to relight.

Expedition.ReadyLine: A Ready maneuver switches it on or off.
Expedition.TacticalLine: Shone in the eyes: HT{ht} or blinded for 10 seconds per point of failure; stuns in a surprise situation (the GM's call).
Expedition.SnappedOn: {name} is snapped and shaken: it glows for about 12 hours.
Expedition.LitLantern: {name} is lit (lighting a lantern takes {min}-{max} seconds).
Expedition.DropHint: A lantern dropped on hard ground rolls against HT 6 or breaks.
Expedition.GlassFire: The oil starts a fire {yards} yard round it (Molotov Cocktail, High-Tech p. 191): the GM's to play out.
Expedition.NoPlace: Nowhere to set it down: no token or template on the viewed scene.
Expedition.SetDownLine: {name} is set down, lighting {yards} yards round it.
Expedition.EyesTarget: Target the tokens to shine the light at.
Expedition.EyesTitle: A tactical light in the eyes
Expedition.EyesSurprise: In a surprise situation the light also stuns (Campaigns p. 393): the GM says whether the victim was surprised.
Expedition.EyesSurprisedPartial: {name} is surprised by the light: mentally stunned, recovering with IQ.
Expedition.EyesSurprisedTotal: {name} is totally surprised by the light: mentally stunned and frozen for {seconds} seconds before the IQ rolls begin.

NavLine.compass: +1 to Navigation (Air, Land or Sea); the best instrument counts, they don't add.
NavLine.instruments: +2 to Navigation (Sea) at TL5, +3 at TL6+; its chart books count as a map at sea.
NavLine.gps: +3 to Navigation (Air, Land or Sea) while in sight of its satellites.
NavLine.map: Basic equipment for Navigation and Forward Observer; without a map, -10.

Expedition.MapPenaltyHint: 0 for an accurate map; -1 to -5 for an inaccurate one (High-Tech p. 52).
Expedition.NoSignal: Out of sight of the satellites
Expedition.NoSignalHint: A GPS receiver gives its +3 only in line of sight of the satellites (High-Tech p. 53).
Expedition.LbeNotSetUp: Not set up: a Soldier or IQ-based Hiking roll sets it up.
Expedition.LbeLine: Set up: {bonus} to reaching gear and to Fast-Draw from its pouches; a Ready maneuver (free on a Fast-Draw roll) to take something out.
Expedition.LbeBadLine: Set up badly: it counts as improvised, {bonus} to reaching gear and to Fast-Draw from its pouches.
Expedition.PackNotFitted: Not fitted: a Soldier or IQ-based Hiking roll fits it. Getting something out is a long action (1d or 2d seconds), with no Fast-Draw.
Expedition.PackFitted: Fitted. Getting something out is a long action (1d or 2d seconds), with no Fast-Draw.
Expedition.PackBadlyFitted: Badly fitted: moderate pain (-2) after a day's hiking.
Expedition.MarchLine: An hour's march: Move {move}/2 = {mph} mph, before terrain and weather.
Expedition.SetUpDone: {name} is set up: +{bonus} from its quality.
Expedition.SetUpFailed: {name} is set up badly: it counts as improvised, -2.
Expedition.FitFailed: {name} fits badly: moderate pain after a day's hiking.
Expedition.PackPain: {name} is in moderate pain from a badly fitted pack.

ClimbLine.harness: Stops a fall at twice the distance past the last fastener.
ClimbLine.rappelKit: Stops a fall at twice the distance past the last fastener; rappels down a rope.
ClimbLine.ascender: Cancels the -2 for climbing up a rope.
ClimbLine.descender: Cancels the -1 for climbing down a rope, and lets the climber hang with both hands free.
ClimbLine.grapnel: Thrown at DX-3 or Throwing, to ST x 2 yards.
ClimbLine.crampons: Terrain Adaptation (Ice) and +1 to Climbing on ice; +2 to kicking damage; -2 to Stealth on hard floors and bare rock.
ClimbLine.skis: Snow is good terrain cross-country, and Move is normal on the level; uphill is half Move without ski climbers.
ClimbLine.suctionCup: Holds 200 lbs.; cancels the -3 for climbing a modern building.

Expedition.SnowshoeFast: No Move lost, but no sprinting.
Expedition.FallHint: A roped climber falls at most twice the distance between the last fastener and where they were.
Expedition.FallLine: {name}, {above} yards past the last fastener, falls at most {yards} yards: roll it with the sheet's Fall.
Expedition.GrapnelLine: Reaches {yards} yards at most; holds {lbs} lbs.
Expedition.GrapnelRing: On stone or concrete it rings: an unmodified Hearing roll at 1 yard (-2 for a padded grapnel).

Oddments.Title: Protective gear and cover
Oddments.BreakInHint: New footwear worn into danger: roll HT, Hiking or HT-based Soldier, whichever is best. Failure is moderate pain for 2d days; critical failure terrible pain, or a crippled foot at the GM's word (High-Tech p. 69).
Oddments.BrokenIn: {name} break in quickly, with little discomfort.
Oddments.BreakInPain: {name} is in moderate pain for {days} days while the new footwear breaks in.
Oddments.BreakInTerrible: {name} is in terrible pain for {days} days while the new footwear breaks in; the GM may rule a crippled foot instead.
Oddments.BrokenInHint: Footwear already broken in needs no roll (High-Tech p. 69).
Oddments.NotBrokenInItem: Not yet broken in: use Break in on the row before trekking off in it.
Oddments.NotMade: {minutes} minutes' work, and {name} isn't fit to wear: try again.
Oddments.PaperSoaks: It won't stand water: it comes apart in damp weather.
Oddments.HomemadeItem: Made with Armoury (Body Armor)+{bonus} (IQ-5+{bonus} at default) and {minutes} minutes' work.
Oddments.VoiceItem: Speech is difficult: Disturbing Voice, {penalty} on Diplomacy, Fast-Talk, Performance, Public Speaking, Sex Appeal and Singing while worn.
Oddments.HamFistedItem: Ham-Fisted 1 for fine work with the gloved hand, while worn.
Oddments.EarsBlockedItem: Protected Hearing, and Hard of Hearing, while worn.
Oddments.MembraneReason: its DR is the Nictitating Membrane it gives
Oddments.ProtectedVisionItem: Protected Vision against bright ordinary light while worn.
Oddments.EyeglassesItem: Corrects Bad Sight and gives the eyes DR 1 while worn; a head hit breaks them on a 1 on 1d, knocks them off on 2-3.
Oddments.EyeglassesBrokenItem: Broken: they neither correct Bad Sight nor protect until replaced.
Oddments.BrokenHint: Broken eyeglasses neither correct nor protect; untick once replaced (High-Tech p. 225).
Oddments.ContactsItem: Corrects Bad Sight while worn, and can't be knocked off or broken; no eye protection.
Oddments.SmotherHint: A charge set off beneath the blanket: its DR {dr} comes off the damage roll (High-Tech p. 72).
Oddments.BlanketItem: Smothers a charge: DR {dr} off its damage roll.
Oddments.RadiationBlanketItem: Smothers a charge: DR {dr} off its damage roll. In use (equipped), PF {pf} against radiation.

Clothing.Title: Clothing against the weather
Clothing.MissingItem: Pieces left off: {penalty} on the cold roll.
Clothing.MissingHint: Winter and arctic clothes must cover feet, hands, head and neck: each piece left off is -1 on the cold roll, and bare to frostbite (High-Tech p. 63).
Clothing.WornAsHint: With a few layers off, arctic clothes count as winter or ordinary clothes (High-Tech p. 63).
Clothing.FurHint: Fur winter or arctic clothes may give DR 1, at the GM's option (High-Tech p. 64).
Clothing.WeightItem: Weight at TL{tl}: x{factor} the TL7 outfit's.
Clothing.WickingItem: +{bonus} on HT and HT-based rolls against FP loss in the heat while worn.
Clothing.ZoneCold: Adds {degrees} degrees to the cold end of the comfort zone while worn.
Clothing.ZoneBoth: Adds {degrees} degrees to both ends of the comfort zone while worn.
Clothing.ZoneHeat: Adds {degrees} degrees to the hot end of the comfort zone while worn: {hours} hours a charge, recharged by {minutes} minutes in ice-cold water (not tracked).
Clothing.HotMarchItem: A hike in the heat costs no extra FP while it runs.
Clothing.HeatedWinterItem: Counts as winter clothes, with or without power.
Clothing.HotMarchLine: {name}: no extra fatigue for the heat
Clothing.FrostbiteLabel: Frostbite: {name}'s {location} ({fp} FP lost to the cold)

Melee.Title: Melee and muscle-powered weapons (High-Tech)
Melee.BayonetTooltip: The gun has a bayonet to fix: its weight and price are added to the gun's, and its row button fixes it (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.BayonetWeightHint: The bayonet's weight, from the description of the gun that mounts it (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.BayonetCostHint: The bayonet's price, where the gun's description gives one.
Melee.BayonetLine: Fixing the bayonet takes {readies} Ready maneuvers ({fastDraw} with a successful Fast-Draw (Knife)).
Melee.BayonetFixedLine: Bayonet fixed: a melee row, -1 to Guns, and a muzzleloader reloads a tenth slower.
Melee.BayonetHint: A fixed bayonet: Spear on a shoulder arm, a large knife's figures with Knife on a sidearm (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.BayonetGunsHint: A fixed bayonet upsets the gun's balance: -1 to Guns (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.ClubHint: Only TL4-5 single-shot muskets and rifles are built to be swung by the barrel; the GM may call for a HT roll against breakage (High-Tech p. 198).
Melee.PickHint: The spike is impaling, and the rules for picks apply: it may get stuck (High-Tech p. 196; Characters p. 405).
Melee.Reversed: Turned round to shoot: the trigger bar is ready.
Melee.Unreversed: Turned back to use as a knife.
Melee.NotReversed: {name} must be turned round (a Ready) before it can shoot.
Melee.IsReversed: {name} is turned round to shoot; turn it back (a Ready) to use it as a knife.
Melee.SheathTooltip: Rigid: the table's weight, a third of it the sheath. Flexible or none: the blade alone, with -1 or -2 on HT rolls against corrosion and incidental damage (High-Tech p. 198).
Melee.SheathWeightHint: The sheath's own weight where the book gives one; blank for a third of the table weight (High-Tech p. 198).
Melee.FlexibleLine: Flexible sheath: {modifier} on HT rolls against corrosion and incidental damage.
Melee.NoSheathLine: No sheath: {modifier} on HT rolls against corrosion and incidental damage; the GM may call for DX rolls to avoid cutting yourself.
Melee.BatonLine: The {weight}-lb. rigid sheath can be used as a baton.
Melee.ReplacementLine: A replacement sheath: ${flexible} flexible, ${rigid} rigid (double or triple reinforced or with tools, GM's option).
Melee.SheathHint: A hollow rigid sheath used as a baton: cheap quality for breakage (High-Tech p. 198).

BladeLine.stainless: Stainless (TL{tl}): corrosion-resistant, no extra cost; a stainless sword's list price buys one grade lower, and the two grades above cost 8 and 40 times list.
BladeLine.ceramic: Ceramic (TL{tl}): missed by a metal detector but plain on an X-ray; breaks as cheap; triple cost, half weight.
BladeLine.titanium: Titanium (TL{tl}): nonmagnetic and corrosion-resistant; breaks as very fine; double cost, three quarters of the weight.

Melee.StainlessTooFine: A stainless sword can only be improved two grades above what list buys.
Melee.SwordCaneLine: A thin blade: it fights and breaks as {grade}, a grade lower than paid for (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.SwordCaneHint: A sword cane is a grade lower than paid for (High-Tech p. 197).
Melee.StunLine: Electric stun weapon: on a failed roll the victim is stunned while it is held in contact and (20 - HT) seconds after, then rolls HT{recovery} each second to recover.
Melee.StunNote: Held in contact: HT{recovery} to recover
Melee.StunHint: The seconds held in contact are an attack option. A current may set flammable liquids alight (High-Tech p. 199).
Melee.ProdHint: The burn is only against an unprotected location. The seconds held in contact are an attack option. A current may set flammable liquids alight (High-Tech p. 199).
Melee.Stunned: {name} is stunned: {held} s in contact, {seconds} s in all before the first roll to recover at HT{recovery}.
Melee.CompoundTooltip: Pulleys and cables: double cost, damage and range as if two ST stronger, drawn at the same ST (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.CompoundHint: Damage and range as if two ST stronger (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.SightsTooltip: +$100: +1 Acc for an archer who knows the skill, -1 for one unfamiliar with them (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.SightsHint: Bow sights, wind gauges and stabilizers help a skilled archer (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.SilencersTooltip: $1 the pair: -2 to Hearing rolls to hear the string (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.SilencerLine: String silencers: {hearing} to Hearing rolls to hear the shot.
Melee.ShotTooltip: Stones are free; lead or steel shot is +1 damage and double range (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.MetalShotHint: Lead or steel shot: +1 damage, double range (High-Tech p. 201).
Melee.SpeargunLine: Range a tenth ({divisor}) under water; the spear is on {line} yards of line.
Melee.LineHint: The spear is tethered by its line; see Harpoons (Campaigns p. 411). Range is a tenth under water (High-Tech p. 201).

Camouflage.Title: Camouflage
Camouflage.TerrainHint: How the terrain around the character compares with the pattern they wear (High-Tech pp. 76-77).
Camouflage.ObserverHint: What whoever is looking sees with. TL7+ camouflage gives +1 against technological night vision or infravision, infrared suppression +2 against infravision. In a Quick Contest, the other side's worn gear decides (High-Tech p. 77).
Camouflage.EquipmentReason: {name}, for the terrain and who is looking (High-Tech pp. 76-77)
Camouflage.NotWornReason: Camouflage clothing counts only while worn (High-Tech pp. 76-77)
Camouflage.PatternHint: The camouflage printed on it. On clothing that isn't a camouflage record, basic adds 100% of its cost and advanced 200% (High-Tech pp. 76-77).
Camouflage.SecondHint: A reversible piece's second pattern, turned outward from its row; its cost is added too (High-Tech p. 77).
Camouflage.InfraredHint: +2 to Camouflage against infravision. $500 more in a ghillie suit (High-Tech p. 77).
Camouflage.ScentHint: -4 to Tracking to follow the wearer by scent. 200% of the clothing's cost (High-Tech p. 77).
Camouflage.NetHint: Laid over gear rather than worn: its row button hides gear, on the deployer's Camouflage (High-Tech p. 76).
Camouflage.CustomHint: What customising added to the suit's bonus in matching terrain, to {most} in all (High-Tech p. 77).
Camouflage.PatternLine: {matching} to Camouflage in matching terrain, {nonMatching} elsewhere, {contrasting} in highly contrasting terrain.
Camouflage.NetLine: Hides gear: the deployer's Camouflage, with the net's pattern.
Camouflage.ScentLine: {value} to Tracking to follow the wearer by scent.
Camouflage.CustomiseFailed: The customising didn't take: the suit keeps its bonus.

Breathing.Title: Breathing gear and environment suits

Protection.comfort: comfort zone widened {cold}° at the cold end and {heat}° at the hot end

Breathing.Don: Takes {on} s to put on, {off} s to take off.
Breathing.Irritants: Immune to eye and nose irritants: tear gas doesn't reach the wearer.
Breathing.Muffled: Muffles the wearer's voice: a listener needs a Hearing roll to understand him, over a radio too.
Breathing.Amplifier: A voice amplifier and a radio adapter: the wearer is understood as usual.
Breathing.Hose: The filter hangs on a hose, {toHit} to hit; cutting it exposes the wearer.
Breathing.Filter: The weight includes a replaceable filter (${cost}, {weight} lb.).
Breathing.TankFed: Breathes from an air tank: Doesn't Breathe while a carried tank holds out.
Breathing.Bubbles: Open circuit: its bubbles can be seen on the surface.
Breathing.Oxygen: Closed circuit, no bubbles; pure oxygen, dangerous below {feet}' (the bends).
Breathing.MixedGas: Closed circuit, no bubbles; mixed gas, safe for deep dives.
Breathing.HardHat: Air comes down a hose from a crew on the surface; risky work in it is a Diving Suit roll.
Breathing.Holds: Holds {minutes} minutes of air at TL{tl}, twice that for a child under 12.
Breathing.LeftAtDepth: {left} minutes of air left at {feet}' ({pressure} atm).
Breathing.Exertion: Each FP spent takes {fp} minute off it, and each failed Fright Check {fright}.
Breathing.DepthHint: How deep the wearer is: the air lasts a third as long at 66', a quarter at 100'.
Breathing.Breathed: {minutes} minutes breathed at {feet}': {left} minutes of air left.
Breathing.HotSuit: Incredibly hot: the FP of effort and weather are tripled while it is worn.
Breathing.NbcSeal: Loses its seal quickly in the wet, and is unreliable after {hours} hours at most.
Breathing.CleanSuit: +{bonus} HT against catching a disease from a victim.
Breathing.AntiG: +{bonus} to HT rolls to resist high acceleration: the GM adds it, as the system rolls none.
Breathing.DrySuit: Resists thermal shock in cold water; proper clothing beneath it keeps out the cold.
Breathing.Wetsuit: Counts as winter clothing in cold water.
Breathing.Turnout: Wet, it gives +{dr} DR against burning, but burning damage that gets through is multiplied by {times}.
Breathing.WetHint: Soaked with water: +5 DR against burning, and burning damage that gets through doubled (High-Tech p. 75).
Breathing.Biomedical: Biomedical sensors: +{bonus} to Diagnosis on the wearer, or Diagnosis at {remote} from afar.

Security.Title: Locks, traps and barriers (High-Tech)
Security.QualityHint: A basic lock is +5 to pick, a good one no modifier, a fine one -5; good costs x5 and fine x20. Electronic locks, identity verifiers and a safe's lock take the same grades (High-Tech pp. 203-205).

Trap.Title: Traps and barriers
Trap.Target: Target whoever meets the trap or barrier.
Trap.Avoided: {name} picks a way through without stepping on one.
Trap.SteppedOn: {name} steps on {count} caltrop(s): {formula} impaling to the foot each; footwear's DR counts.
Trap.Lodged: {count} lodged: each does its damage again every turn the foot is walked on, and takes {readies} Ready maneuvers to pull out.
Trap.Dirty: The wounds are dirty: {modifier} or worse to resist infection (Campaigns p. 444).
Trap.FellIn: {name} falls on the stakes: {formula} impaling, from their own ST.

Barrier.Snagged: The wire snags clothing and gear: held as by a Binding of ST {st} (Characters p. 40).
Barrier.SnaggedBound: The wire snags {name}'s clothing and gear: held by a Binding of ST {st} until broken free (Characters p. 40).
Barrier.Stunned: {name} is stunned, and may roll HT each second to recover.
Barrier.StunnedHeld: {name} is stunned while touching the fence, {seconds} second(s) more; the rolls to recover begin once the contact ends.
Barrier.Unaffected: {name} has no electronics for it to disable.
Barrier.KnockedOut: {name} is out of action for {seconds} second(s).

Item.Safe: DR {dr}, HP {hp}; the lock's own toughness doesn't count.

Pick.lock: Lockpicking {modifier} to pick it; a minute an attempt, with Time Spent. An older lock gives a higher-TL burglar a bonus.
Pick.safe: Lockpicking {modifier} to open it; an hour an attempt, with Time Spent. A stethoscope is basic equipment for it.
Pick.electronic: Electronics Operation (Security) {modifier} to get past it, with an electronic lockpicking kit or Electronics Repair (Security) tools. Cutting the power opens a fail-safe lock, not a fail-secure one.
Pick.verifier: Electronics Operation (Security) {modifier} to bypass it with the case open and suitable tools.

Item.Forgery: Forgery {modifier} to fool it, with Electronics Operation (Security) and a computer analysis of an authorized signature.
Item.Gun: {basic} more against a basic lock, {other} against a good or fine one; five seconds an attempt.
Item.picks: Basic equipment for Lockpicking; improvised or better picks use the Equipment Modifiers.
Item.kit: Basic equipment for Electronics Operation (Security) against electronic locks.
Item.Stethoscope: +{bonus} against a mechanical lock or other device heard working, in a very quiet place.
Item.Endoscope: +{bonus} to crack a lock or safe by seeing inside it.
Item.Caltrops: Covers a hex. Moving through it: a Vision roll each second at the Move's speed penalty, -2 more when not watching the ground; one caltrop stepped on per point of failure (at least one), each thrust{modifier} impaling to the foot. One that does at least the footwear's DR lodges; {readies} Ready maneuvers remove each.
Item.BarbedWire: DX-5 a yard to get through; a failure tears the skin (a Will roll not to cry out: +3 High Pain Threshold, -4 Low) and snags as a Binding of ST {st}. Laying something over it lets anyone climb across.
Item.RazorWire: As barbed wire, but a failed DX-5 roll also does 1d-3 cutting and the Will roll is at minus the injury; snags as a Binding of ST {st}.
Item.WireLaying: A coil takes {minutes} man-minutes to lay, {bare} without gloves, wire cutters and fasteners.
Item.CattleFence: A HT roll each second of contact; a failure stuns while the victim touches it, and HT rolls each second to recover once they let go (Campaigns p. 432).
Item.LethalFence: {damage} burning a second, a lethal shock (Campaigns p. 432).
Item.SpikeStrip: A tire driven over it deflates in {seconds} seconds: {driving} to Driving and Top Speed x{topSpeed}.
Item.CarStopper: HT{modifier} for a TL8+ vehicle or anyone with Electrical, or out of action for seconds equal to the margin; pre-TL8 vehicles are immune.
Item.SmartFence: Electronics Operation (Security){modifier} to neutralize each 10-yard section.
Item.StakePit: Thrust impaling from the victim's own ST; a punji pit's dirty stakes give {modifier} or worse to resist infection.

Security.SafeNote: A safe's own DR and HP (High-Tech p. 203)

Medicine.Title: Medical gear
Medicine.CprWho: Select the rescuer's token and target the patient.
Medicine.CprFatigue: {name} has given {minutes} minutes of CPR: {fp} FP.
Medicine.NoFluidsReason: No blood or IV fluids: +1 at best
Medicine.NeedIvKit: Starting an IV needs an IV kit.
Medicine.IvStarted: An IV of {item} goes into {name}: a minute to start, {least}-{most} hours to run.
Medicine.IvWater: It counts as drinking a quart of water.
Medicine.IvMeal: Its sugar counts as a meal for recovering FP and HP.
Medicine.Under: {name} goes under: a minute if cooperative, {least}-{most} if not.
Medicine.NotUnder: {name} isn't properly under: Surgery at {penalty}, as with no anaesthetic.
Medicine.SurgicalKitLine: {name} in place of the TL{tl} table
Medicine.Cleaned: {name}'s wound is cleaned: up to -{bonus} of the dirt's penalty off the roll against infection.
Medicine.AirwayItem: A tracheotomy without this kit is at -5 for improvised equipment.
Medicine.DefibrillatorItem: On an Electronics Operation (Medical) roll, +{bonus} to the resuscitation roll.
Medicine.AedItem: IQ+{bonus} to hook it up; then it resuscitates at skill {skill}.
Medicine.IvFluidItem: Given through an IV kit over {least}-{most} hours, a bag counts as a quart of water; blood or IV fluids let first aid gear give +2.
Medicine.IvMealItem: Given through an IV kit over {least}-{most} hours, a bag counts as a quart of water and a meal; blood or IV fluids let first aid gear give +2.
Medicine.KitItem: Without blood or IV fluids, first aid gear gives +{best} at best.
Medicine.CrashKitItem: Carries its own IV and a unit of fluids, so gives its +2 until depleted; otherwise +{best} at best.
Medicine.HemostaticItem: +{bonus} (quality) to First Aid on a bleeding wound, in {seconds} seconds; a bandage a treatment.
Medicine.ImagingItem: On an Electronics Operation (Medical) roll, a new Diagnosis roll with its bonus.
Medicine.XrayItem: Each photograph gives the patient and the operator {dice}d rads.
Medicine.SurgicalKitItem: Its own TL modifier stands in for the Basic Set table's by the surgeon's TL.
Medicine.SuturingItem: Basic equipment for stitching simple wounds; improvised ({penalty}) for an operation.
Medicine.AnesthesiaItem: A Physician roll puts the patient under; if it fails, Surgery is at {penalty}. Good for {hours} hours here.
Medicine.AnesthesiaMachineItem: A Physician roll at +{bonus} puts the patient under; if it fails, Surgery is at {penalty}. A tank lasts {hours} hours.
Medicine.AntisepticItem: Cleaning a wound takes no roll and removes up to -{bonus} of the dirt's penalty on the roll against infection.
Medicine.DepletedHint: Used for several treatments: the reusable tools left work a grade lower (High-Tech p. 221).

Armor.Title: High-Tech armour
Armor.CoverageHint: How much of each location the piece covers. A piece covering n in 6 protects when 1d comes up n or less, and an attacker can strike around it (High-Tech p. 69).
Armor.CoverageItem: Covers {n} in 6 of each location: 1d at or under the sixths of every partial piece there protects. Striking around it: {penalty}.
Armor.FrontItem: DR {dr} against blows from the front on the {locations}.
Armor.ToeItem: Steel toe box: DR {dr} on {n} in 6 hits to the foot.
Armor.TopsUpHint: With the tops turned up, high boots cover 3 in 6 of the legs (High-Tech p. 68).
Armor.TopsUpItem: Tops up: covers {n} in 6 of the legs.
Armor.ToeMissed: toe box missed: 1d rolled {roll} against {n} in 6
Armor.DesignHint: Armour designed to be concealed takes +1 to +4 off the Holdout penalty to hide it, never beyond it (High-Tech p. 66).
Armor.ConcealItem: Holdout to hide it from a search: {modifier} ({rule}).
Armor.ConcealPick: Target the character searching you first.
Armor.MaterialHint: Low-tech metal armour and shields in TL5+ steel or TL8 titanium, or cloth armour in TL8 smart foam (High-Tech p. 65).

MaterialItem.steel: TL5+ steel: twice the DR at the same cost and weight.
MaterialItem.steelLight: TL5+ steel: the same DR at half the cost and weight.
MaterialItem.smartFoam: Smart foam: DR 4 against crushing and 1 against everything else, concealable under ordinary clothes; ten times the cost.
MaterialItem.titanium: Titanium: the same DR at a third of the weight and five times the cost.

Armor.SemiAblativeHint: A ceramic trauma plate cracks as it stops bullets: every 10 points of basic damage rolled take a point of its DR, whether or not the blow got through (High-Tech p. 67).
Armor.PlateReplaced: {item} is replaced: its DR is whole again.

Surveillance.Title: Security and surveillance

Screen.Title: Screen with {name}
Screen.Label: {skill} with {name}
Screen.OperatorFailed: The operator's Electronics Operation (Security) roll failed: the gear gives no bonus this time (p. 206).
Screen.MetalWeapons: Looking for metallic weapons or detonators
Screen.Against: Search against {name}'s Holdout, in a Quick Contest.
Screen.UndercoverLine: {name}: no help against a metal detector
Screen.Operator: Its operator rolls Electronics Operation (Security) to claim the bonus (p. 206).
Screen.Undercover: Undercover clothing adds nothing to Holdout against a search with a metal detector (p. 206).
Screen.handheldMetal: +1 to Search, Traps and Explosives (EOD) to find metal; +2 to Search with a one-minute pat-down (p. 206).
Screen.walkthroughMetal: +1 to +3 to Search in Quick Contests against Holdout, as its sensitivity is set; high settings mean pat-downs and long queues (p. 206).
Screen.baggage: +3 to Search to find weapons and contraband; at TL8, +1 more for metal weapons, detonators and explosives (p. 206).
Screen.ct: The best equipment for Search at TL8: +4, +6 to find explosives (p. 207).
Screen.portableXray: +5 to Search examining a package's or vehicle's contents, +4 to Explosives (EOD) defusing a bomb (p. 217).

Security.Title: Security system
Security.Sophisticated: Electronic (not mechanical or a simple circuit)
Security.SeismicCrossed: {name} crosses the zone at Move 1 without being detected.
Security.ShooterFound: Located: the shooter's position, range and calibre, direction to within 20 degrees (p. 207).
Security.ShooterLost: The system can't place the shot.
Security.MillimeterWave: Sees as Imaging Radar out to {range} yards, through clothing, packaging and thin walls (p. 207).
Security.OpticalRecognition: Recognizes faces as a guard with Per {conservative} (or {generous}+ if the GM is generous); Disguise and Acting fool it as they would a guard (p. 207).
Security.Countersniper: Locates a shooter on a roll against {base} plus the shot's total Hearing modifier (p. 207).
Security.Seismic: An intruder who knows it's there crosses at Move 1 on a Stealth roll at {modifier} (p. 206).
Security.Voiceprint: A good recording or a voice modulator fools it (p. 205).
Security.Proximity: Detects someone approaching or touching what it guards; its field shows on an EM field meter (pp. 205-206).
Security.MicrowaveFence: Detects movement in a 10-yard swath between its units, up to 500 yards apart (p. 205).

Mike.Spike: In use (equipped): Parabolic Hearing {levels}, hearing {factor} times as far through the wall (p. 208).
Mike.Pinhead: Its cable is guided on a DX-based Electronics Operation (Surveillance) roll: failure, stuck or noisy; critical failure, broken or detected (p. 208).
Mike.Contact: Hears through a barrier on Electronics Operation (Surveillance) at -(DR+HP)/5 (p. 208).
Mike.LaserTl7: Range {range} yards; ordinary noise or a white noise generator defeats it, and most bug detectors can't sense it (p. 208).
Mike.LaserTl8: Range {range} yards; filters ordinary noise, but a white noise generator defeats it, and most bug detectors can't sense it (p. 208).
Mike.PinheadStuck: The mike gets stuck or makes a noise.
Mike.PinheadBroken: The mike breaks, or the target notices it.

Bug.Undetectable: Bug detectors can't find it; only a physical search does (pp. 208-209).
Bug.Noisy: Anyone sweeping for bugs has {bonus} to find it (p. 210).
Bug.Homemade: SM {sm}: built at home at {modifier} to Electronics Repair (Surveillance) (p. 210).
Bug.CellularBeacon: Battery lasts {hourly} times as long reporting hourly, {daily} times daily; needs a cell network, and jammers stop it (p. 210).
Bug.Built: Built: about {hours} hours' work and ${low}-${high} of parts (p. 210).
Bug.NotBuilt: It doesn't work: {hours} hours and ${low}-${high} of parts gone.

Sweep.Title: Sweep for bugs
Sweep.Label: Sweeping with {name}
Sweep.Line: Finds a hidden bug in a Quick Contest of Electronics Operation (Surveillance) with whoever hid it, a minute per 100 square feet; good quality +1, fine +2; {bonus} for a radio beacon (pp. 210, 212).
Sweep.CantSense: A bug detector can't sense this: only a physical search finds it.

Kind.undetectable: A phone tap, laser mike or laser pinhead mike

Endoscope.Title: Search with the endoscope
Endoscope.Label: {skill} with {name}
Endoscope.Search: {search} to Search in hollow objects and body cavities; {lockpicking} to Lockpicking through a drilled hole (p. 209).
Endoscope.Surveillance: {vision} to Vision through its lens; spotting its tube takes Vision{spot} (p. 209).

Surveillance.DocumentScanner: Copies a document in a sealed envelope on Electronics Operation (Security or Surveillance) at {modifier} (p. 209).
Surveillance.ShieldedRoom: At least {modifier} to electronic intelligence-gathering on the room (p. 212).
Surveillance.VoiceModulatorTl7: Makes the voice an anonymous monotone; fools a voiceprint analyzer (pp. 205, 212).
Surveillance.VoiceModulatorTl8: Hides the voiceprint and can pass as another sex or age; fools a voiceprint analyzer (pp. 205, 212).

Jammer.Operated: Range {range} yards, run by its operator's Electronics Operation (EW); radio gear within range is used in a Quick Contest against it, and within {shadow} times its range on an unopposed roll (p. 212).
Jammer.Unmanned: Range {range} yards at an effective Electronics Operation (EW) {skill}, with no operator; radio gear within range is used in a Quick Contest against it, and within {shadow} times its range on an unopposed roll (pp. 212-213).
Jammer.Blocks: Blocks every cell-phone call within {range} yards (p. 213).
Jammer.Hindered: Radio gear: a jammer in range makes using it a Quick Contest, and one within {shadow} times its range an unopposed roll (p. 212).
Jammer.WhiteNoise: Defeats laser mikes, audio bugs and tape recorders (p. 213).

Jamming.SwitchTitle: Switch the jammer on or off
Jamming.SwitchedOn: A jammer is switched on: everyone near knows it, though not where it is (p. 212).

LieDetection.Title: Lie detector
LieDetection.PickSubject: Target the one subject to be tested.
LieDetection.Holds: Holds a reading of {subject}: {value} to Interrogation.
LieDetection.Contest: Row button: a Quick Contest of {skill} against the subject's Will; the margin, won or lost, is the interrogators' modifier to Interrogation. The operator and the questioner may be different people (High-Tech p. 216).
LieDetection.Half: A voice stress analyser: half a polygraph's effect on Interrogation (High-Tech p. 216).
LieDetection.Compulsive: A subject with Compulsive Lying reads as truthful: {value} on machine-aided Interrogation (High-Tech p. 216).

Restraints.Title: Restraint
Restraints.StateHint: Whether this restraint is on the character whose sheet it is on, and for cuffs, whether the wrists are cuffed behind the back or in front (High-Tech p. 217).
Restraints.Slipped: {name} brings the cuffed wrists round to the front.
Restraints.NotSlipped: {name} can't get the cuffed wrists round to the front.
Restraints.NoWeapons: Restrained by {name}: no weapon can be used (High-Tech p. 217).
Restraints.NoOneHanded: Cuffed in front by {name}: no one-handed blow; two-handed weapons and guns only (High-Tech p. 217).
Restraints.NoPunch: Restrained by {name}: the hands can't strike (High-Tech p. 217).
Restraints.Behind: Cuffed behind: {dx} DX, {hands} on tasks done with the hands alone (worked blind behind the back), and nothing that needs the arms free. Acrobatics or Escape brings the wrists to the front.
Restraints.Front: Cuffed in front: {hands} on hands-only tasks; one-handed blows are impossible, two-handed weapons and guns unhindered, other weapons -1 to -4 (the GM's call).
Restraints.Straitjacket: As cuffed behind the back ({dx} DX, no weapon use), with the hands useless in the sleeves and no slipping the arms round to the front.
Restraints.LegIrons: Crippled Legs: Move is half Basic Speed, -3 on skills that need the legs; kicking is impossible. TL5 leg irons don't ratchet (Escape unmodified); TL6-8 ones do (Escape-5).
Restraints.Ball: The prisoner carries the {weight}-lb. iron ball, which counts toward encumbrance.

Prosthetics.Cured: Cured by laser eye surgery (High-Tech p. 225)
Prosthetics.Title: Elective surgery
Prosthetics.Hint: The surgeon's Surgery roll is the system's operation. Once it is in, say on the card how it went: a success is recorded on the patient. The GM may charge points for a beneficial change (High-Tech p. 225).
Prosthetics.NoPatient: There is no character to operate on.

Plan.build: {name}: build from {from} to {to}. $5,000; a week to recover.
Plan.appearance: {name}: Appearance from {from} to {to}. ${cost}; a week to recover.
Plan.vision: {name}: laser surgery on {eyes} eye(s) against Bad Sight. ${cost}; a couple of days to recover.

Prosthetics.SetBuild: Recorded. Set {name}'s build to {to} on the sheet and adjust the weight to match.
Prosthetics.SetAppearance: Recorded. Set {name}'s Appearance to {to} on the sheet.
Prosthetics.BuildChanged: Recorded: {name}'s build is now {to}. Adjust the weight to match.
Prosthetics.SightCured: Recorded: {name}'s Bad Sight is cured and out of play. Remove the trait when the points are settled.
Prosthetics.OneEyeDone: Recorded: one eye done. Bad Sight stays until the other eye is operated on too.

FailedNote.build: Nothing changed. What a failure costs the patient is the GM's.
FailedNote.appearance: Nothing improved. Cosmetic surgery can go wrong: infection, nerve damage, or a lower Appearance, at the GM's word (High-Tech p. 225).
FailedNote.vision: Nothing changed. What a failure costs the patient is the GM's.
FailedNote.fingerprints: Nothing changed. What a failure costs the patient is the GM's.

Refusal.NotABuildStep: {name}'s build can't go a step further that way: surgery works between Very Fat and Skinny (High-Tech p. 225).
Refusal.NoAppearanceStep: Surgery can only improve Appearance to Attractive, Handsome/Beautiful or Very Handsome/Very Beautiful, a step at a time (High-Tech p. 225).
Refusal.NoBadSight: {name} has no Bad Sight to cure.

Conveyance.Title: Personal conveyance
Conveyance.BicycleItem: Ridden with {skill}: Move is the better of relative skill and Move, x{multiplier} (Enhanced Move), rounded down.
Conveyance.SkateboardItem: Ridden with {skill}: Move x{multiplier} (Enhanced Move), rounded down.
Conveyance.RoadBoundItem: Road-Bound: the Enhanced Move counts on a road only.
Conveyance.DownhillItem: Downhill, Move is multiplied by the slope: {steps}.
Conveyance.LongRideItem: Long rides: the better of HT and HT-based Bicycling every minute of paced riding (15 seconds of sprinting); a failure costs 1 FP.
Conveyance.TowingItem: Towing, it counts as a two-wheeled cart: the load and cart pull at 1/{divisor} of their weight, 1/{smooth} on a smooth, level surface (Campaigns p. 353).
Conveyance.SpillItem: Any spill is at least a {yards}-yard fall.
Conveyance.SurfboardItem: Ridden with {skill}. The best waves carry a surfer at Move {least}-{most}; paddling is seldom faster than Move {paddling}.
Conveyance.StairsItem: Climbs curbs and stairs, a step a second; balances on two wheels at a standing person's eye level.
Conveyance.SlopeHint: The slope the rider is going down: Move x2 at 7.5°, x3 at 15°, x4 at 30° (High-Tech p. 230).
Conveyance.OffRoadHint: Road-Bound Enhanced Move counts on a road only.
Conveyance.SurfHint: Paddling is seldom faster than Move 1; the best waves carry a surfer at Move 12-15 (High-Tech p. 231). This is the character's water Move.
Conveyance.Towed: Moved as cargo, in the towed load
Conveyance.CargoHint: The bicycle counts as a two-wheeled cart: the bike and its load pull at 1/{divisor} of their weight, 1/{smooth} on a smooth, level surface, and count toward encumbrance until stopped (High-Tech p. 230; Campaigns p. 353).
Conveyance.CargoLine: {name} moves {weight} lbs. on the bicycle, counting as {effective} lbs.
Conveyance.CargoTooHeavy: Past {limit} lbs. (15 x Basic Lift) the load can't be moved at all (Campaigns p. 353).
Conveyance.SpillLine: {name} takes a spill: a {yards}-yard fall, {velocity} yards/second.
Conveyance.LongRideHint: A roll against the better of HT and HT-based Bicycling for every minute of paced riding or 15 seconds of sprinting; a failure costs 1 FP (Campaigns p. 354).

Drugs.Title: Hygiene, drugs and poisons (High-Tech)
Drugs.BotulinCrippled: {name}'s lungs and spine are crippled: a lasting injury that heals in {months} month(s) of immobility on a ventilator, the paralysis lasting as long (High-Tech p. 227; Campaigns p. 422).
Drugs.BotulinHealed: {name}'s lungs and spine have healed: the botulin paralysis is over.
Drugs.PickVictims: Target the characters to poison first.
Drugs.NoPoison: {name} has no poison in them to treat.
Drugs.Doses: {used} of {per} doses used from this one.
Drugs.DmsoItem: Mixed with DMSO: a contact agent.
Drugs.PoisonRollItem: Each cycle: {roll} against what a failure brings.
Drugs.MitigatesHint: The character's disadvantages this drug keeps at bay, comma-separated; blank for the book's list: Chronic Depression, Epilepsy, Flashbacks, Lunacy, Manic-Depressive, Paranoia, Phantom Voices, Short Attention Span and Split Personality (High-Tech p. 227). Give the trait a Mitigator limitation (Characters p. 112) on the Traits tab.
Drugs.MorphineResisted: {name} shrugs the dose off: no relief.
Drugs.MorphineWorks: {name} feels no pain to speak of for {hours} hours: High Pain Threshold, Unfazeable and euphoria, and Laziness while it lasts.
Drugs.AnalgesicTaken: {name} takes the edge off the pain: 1 or 2 less from pain's penalty, and it helps a hangover. Remove the condition when it wears off.
Drugs.WoundTreated: {name}'s wound: +{bonus} against infection for a day.
Drugs.IllnessTreated: {name}: +{bonus} to the HT rolls against the illness. Resistant bacteria reduce or negate it.
Drugs.PoisonTreated: {name}: +{bonus} to the HT rolls against the poison.
Drugs.AntitoxinHint: An antitoxin gives +1 to +TL/2 against one specific poison, by how good a match it is.
Drugs.BotulinAntitoxin: The antitoxin reaches {name} before paralysis sets in: the botulin does nothing more.
Drugs.CurareAntitoxin: The curare antitoxin takes 30 minutes to work.
Drugs.ChelatingRadiation: Chelating agents also remove radioactive matter (see Radiation Treatment, Campaigns p. 436).
Drugs.TruthSerumWorks: {name}: {penalty} to Will and to self-control rolls for {minutes} minutes.
Drugs.PsychiatricTaken: {name} takes the day's dose: {list} out of play for a day.
Drugs.NoAgentForDmso: Carry a blood or digestive poison to mix the DMSO into.
Drugs.DmsoHint: One dose of DMSO lets one dose of a blood or digestive agent work through the skin.
Drugs.StrychnineHours: The seizures go on for {hours} hours.

Protected.metabolic: {name} has no metabolism for it to work on.

Note.curareParalysed: {name} is paralysed until the next cycle.
Note.ricinChoking: Failed the first roll and this one: {name} is choking, and it may kill.
Note.botulinParalysed: {name} is paralysed (HT{penalty} failed). It heals as a lasting crippling injury of the lungs and spine (Campaigns p. 422), immobile and on a ventilator the whole time.
Note.botulinHolds: {name} holds off the paralysis (HT{penalty}); the next roll is one worse.
Note.thalliumRadiation: {name} also has the radiation's gastrointestinal syndrome: the daily HT rolls for it (Campaigns p. 435).

Effect.soap: Used daily: +1 to HT rolls against Contagion and Infection.
Effect.footPowder: +2 to resist fungal infection of the feet: trench foot, jungle rot and the like.
Effect.saltTablets: +1 to HT rolls to avoid FP loss from heat. Each tablet treats a quart of water.
Effect.sunscreen: DR {dr} against sunburn for 2-4 hours (Campaigns p. 434).
Effect.vitamins: Makes up for a poor diet: the character can live on nutritionally inadequate food.
Effect.handSanitizer: Used regularly: +1 to HT rolls against Contagion.
Effect.ammonia: Waved under a stunned or unconscious person's nose: a HT roll to recover at once.
Effect.castorOil: Might give +{castor} to HT rolls against the ongoing effects of some stomach ailments and digestive poisons.
Effect.morphine: A painkiller (Campaigns p. 441): HT-4 to resist; on a failure, High Pain Threshold, Unfazeable, Laziness and euphoria for the margin's hours.
Effect.quinine: +3 to HT rolls to recover from malaria; taken daily before, during and after travel in a malarial area, +5 to avoid catching it.
Effect.charcoal: +{charcoal} to HT rolls against many digestive poisons, arsenic and strychnine among them.
Effect.analgesics: Takes 1 or 2 off pain's penalty (after Pain Threshold); good for a hangover too.
Effect.antibiotics: +{bonus} (TL/2) to HT rolls against bacterial disease, or against infection on a wound. Resistant bacteria reduce or negate it.
Effect.antibioticOintment: On a wound: +{bonus} (TL/2) to HT rolls against infection.
Effect.antimalarial: As quinine: +3 to recover from malaria, +5 to avoid catching it. It may leave the patient slightly nauseous.
Effect.antitoxin: +1 to +{most} (TL/2) to HT rolls against one specific poison.
